Found while adding the rename-aware merge's own warnings, which quote paths too. | `main.rs` `cmd_merge`: `for w in &res.warnings { warn(w) }`; `render::warn` does not escape. | `duplicate_cli::merge_warnings_quoting_hostile_paths_are_escaped` (failed before the fix), `duplicate_cli::hostile_names_in_rename_reports_are_escaped` |
| BUG-681 | medium (**fixed**, Git-parity fix wave 1) | embargo / declassification | **Fixed:** one rule for every route that copies content from one revision into another (`veil_core::confinement`): a snapshot is *confined* to an unreleased embargo when it is its withheld history, builds on it (what a push refuses), or sits under its wrapper (the embargoed line); content of a confined snapshot is copied only into a change confined to the same embargo. `vl restore --from` (with and without paths) checks it against `@`; `vl squash` (`--into`, partial or whole, and into the fix's own public parent) against the destination; `vl duplicate`/`cherry-pick` now also refuse work *built on* the fix, whose edits of the fix's files were copied out as conflicts (destinations must still be on the fix line); `Transaction::commit` refuses any rewrite that moves a confined change onto parents outside its embargo (`vl rebase -r/-s` of work on the fix, `vl abandon` of the fix under such work; moving the fix itself is fine, the embargoed merge follows it); `vl resolve` only picks versions already in the change and `vl cat` writes nothing; `vl split` keeps both halves where the change was. Refusals name the change and the embargo, never a file or description. Found, beyond the reported route, by this fix: `restore --from` the embargoed merge (published the fix's names), `rebase -r <work on the fix> -d <public>` (names and plaintext content as a conflict, then `vl resolve` made it an edit), `duplicate` of such work, `squash --into`. `vl restore --from <fix> PATH` on a line outside an unreleased embargo copies a file of the withheld fix as an ordinary edit of that line: public plaintext when the fix was not cloaked (sealed for its scope when it was, which still publishes its name and size). The next push to a public remote publishes the fix's file name and content before the release, although the fix itself is withheld and the threat model promises the embargoed tree is sealed whole. `vl duplicate`/`cherry-pick` refuse the same copy (design 1, threat review 11, whose adversarial note flagged this route). | `main.rs` `cmd_restore` / `checkout::restore_paths`: the source revision is not checked against `remote::embargo_withheld`; the restored entry is recorded by the builder under the destination line's policy. Suggested fix: refuse a `--from` revision an unreleased embargo withholds unless `@` is inside that embargo (the rule `Repo::duplicate` applies), or keep restored entries sealed under the embargo key. | `duplicate_cli::restoring_from_an_embargoed_fix_onto_another_line_publishes_nothing`; `embargo_copy_cli` (one test per route) |
| BUG-682 | high (**fixed**, Git-parity fix wave 2; feature **removed**, format 8) | squash / cloaked lines / push | **Fixed:** the leak was the sealed version's *fallback* (what readers without the key see), not its content. Squashing the draft into the cloaked change merged it into a version of `a.txt` that change already sealed; the merge (`merged_visibility`) gives a sealed result the other side's public version as fallback ("the newest public version"), here the draft's plaintext blob, and `embargo::seal_introduced` kept already-sealed entries as they were, fallback included, so the push of the cloaked change sent the draft. `seal_introduced` now lets a version sealed under the line's scope fall back only to what the line's base already shows readers without the key at that path (`publicly_seen`); any other fallback becomes the base's public version (`public_fallback`). The same rule covers every route that folds content into a cloaked change (squash, rebase onto it, `vl duplicate` and `vl cherry-pick`), so it also fixes **BUG-707** (the same fallback through `vl duplicate`, found by adversarial pass A in round 9). Pinned by `adversarial7::rewrites::a_draft_squashed_into_a_sealed_edit_publishes_nothing_sealed`, `adversarial7::fallbacks` (squash, rebase then squash, duplicate, cherry-pick, and a split of what the cloaked change took in; each fails without the fix) and `split_squash::a_draft_squashed_into_a_sealed_edit_never_becomes_its_fallback` (decoded packs searched with `backend_contains`). A public edit in `@` that was never pushed, squashed into a cloaked change (`vl squash -r @ --into sec@`), reaches the public mirror as plaintext with the next `vl push` of that cloaked change. Present before the Git-parity round (fails the same at `c935cc9`). | BUG-480 | high (**fixed**, round-7 sealing wave; feature **removed**, format 8) | squash / conflicts / cloaking | **Fixed:** `seal_introduced` now seals an introduced conflict entry's public versions (`embargo::seal_conflict_terms`): each version (add or remove) whose plaintext readers without the key could not already see at that path in the base (a public entry, a sealed entry's fallback, a public version of the base's conflict) is sealed for the line's scope; a forged public label gets its real one; the conflict keeps its shape. Applies to squash into a cloaked change and to rebases of cloaked lines (`Repo::rebase_tree`). `vl squash` into a cloaked change ("seals what it brings for that change's scope", `--help`) leaves a **conflict entry** it brings exactly as it was: its public side, the very work being moved, stays plaintext in the cloaked change. Pushing that change to a public remote sends the conflict object and the public side, and a mirror reader's checkout shows it. The same squash of a plain file seals it (control). ## Round 7 hypotheses (not demonstrated)

* **Idle `vl serve` clients hold every slot forever**: demonstrated and fixed as BUG-495 (round-7 serve wave).
* **Decompression bomb in a pack from a hostile remote** (both decoders, pre-existing). A pack entry declares `raw_len`, and nothing bounds it: a few KB of zstd RLE blocks declaring 8 GiB make `Pack::get` allocate it (`pack.rs:526-531` libzstd streaming, `pack.rs:607-622` ruzstd) before the hash check. Not run: it would exhaust this machine's memory.
* **Idle `vl serve` clients hold every slot forever** (same-user DoS, low). There is a 60 s write timeout but no read or idle timeout (`serve.rs:471`, `serve_client` at `:568`): 32 connections that never send (or send half a line) make every other client, the user's editor, get `-32001 too many clients` until the server restarts. Reproduced by hand (a `python3` client: still refused after any wait); not made a test, as a correct server would only free a slot after an idle timeout of minutes.
* **Decompression bomb in a pack from a hostile remote**: demonstrated safely and fixed as BUG-490.
* **WASM locks on a networked backend with no clock installed.** A no-`os` holder writes `renewed: 0` and has no heartbeat; a native contender takes the lock over at once, and the holder's self-fencing never fires (`clock::monotonic()` stuck at 0). The documented skew analysis predicts a failed write on the WASM side, with the same residual window. Not testable in the native suite (no-`os` is compile-time).
* **Scanner windows inside a > 2 KiB line.** `line_start` (`secrets.rs:2014`, `LINE_LOOKBACK` 2048) gives up after 2 KiB, so a 256 KiB chunk boundary inside a longer line still starts mid-line (the BUG-400 condition); only a v6 key with a 256+ character unquoted value could flip. A shift harness over minified bundles found nothing.
* **Positional hunk numbers in a plan go stale.** A `--plan` or `--hunks` names hunks by number, and `vl split` first snapshots the working copy: an edit made after the script read `vl diff --json` renumbers the hunks and the plan takes different ones, silently. Nothing is lost or re-audienced (both changes keep everything), so it is a correctness note; a plan could carry the snapshot id it was made from.
* **A conflict object with 64 removes** (the maximum) makes every merge or rebase that touches it fail with "more than 64 removes" (`Conflict::validate`), a recoverable denial by a hostile remote until the conflict is resolved.
* **`vl serve` with a closed standard error**: checked, `eprintln!` is redefined so it never panics; requests still succeed.

## Round 7 coverage notes

* **`--json` confidentiality** (`api.rs`): for a non-member on a team clone and a reader of a public mirror, with an embargoed merge (sealed description, new path, fixed line) and a cloaked workspace: `log`, `ls`, `show`, `diff`, `status`, `files`, `resolve --list`, `tag list` print no sealed description, no embargoed path or content. Op-log descriptions name changes and tags but never messages. Text and JSON are built from the same structures; strings go through `to_json`'s escaping.
* **Conflicts (format 4)**: materialisation for a member and an outsider, partly edited markers (sides are sealed as the resolution), a hidden base, two scopes, `resolve --ours/--theirs/--base` (sealing kept), the Git export and a public push of a conflict with a sealed side (redacted): no leak found outside BUG-480/481. Hostile terms of the wrong kind or with forged labels are handled (`verify_sealing`, `Corrupt` → unreadable).
* **`vl split` / `vl squash`**: partial squash into an unrelated change by hunk and `vl undo` restore exactly; audiences of in-between files follow the new version (`selection::classify`); `.veilpolicy`, conflicts and embargoes move whole; stale selections are refused by `check_current`.
* **`vl push --dry-run`** reads the remote through `ReadOnly` and takes no lock; the object list is the real push's (`PlanRecord`). Only the `files` part is computed apart, from labels (BUG-482).
* **`vl serve --local`** (fork): 40 server writes raced against 40 CLI writes, and a 50 ms working-copy `watch` against 60 rounds of CLI `commit`/`new`/`describe`: no edit or operation lost. 200,000 levels of nesting, huge limits and ids, 900 KB revisions and a 1 MiB+ line without a newline: the server stays up. A second server is refused, a stale socket replaced, symlinked `sock` and `serve.lock` refused. Nothing served beyond what the CLI shows the same identity.
* **Scanner v6** (fork): 38 crafted shapes at 1 and 4 MiB all scan in at most 132 ms (release), ratio ≤ 3.5×; 1.2 GB of real code in under 4 s. UTF-16/32 secrets at chunk boundaries found; no boundary-dependent finding on minified bundles. New v6 shapes (camelCase keys, `*_KEY`, XML elements and attributes, connection strings, URL passwords) found apart from BUG-487/488.
* **WASM / no-`os`** (fork): `cargo check -p veil-core --no-default-features --features wasm` passes for the host and for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`; 1.5 million mutated zstd frames through a copy of `pack::pure::decompress` with ruzstd 0.9.1: no panic, no loop, none slower than 500 ms; pack framing reviewed with no panic path found; a clock at 0 makes locks fail safe.

## Round 8 findings (Opus, sandboxes, mount and team vault)

Baseline: `integration` @ `aa78e6d`. Line numbers refer to it. Tests:
`crates/vl/tests/cli_adversarial/adversarial8/` (modules `sandbox`, `mount`, `vault`;
the mount tests skip without `/dev/fuse` and `fusermount3`, mount under
`$TMPDIR` and unmount on drop) and `crates/veil-core/tests/core_security/adversarial8_core/`
(module `vault`). Each `#[ignore = "BUG-NNN: …"]` test asserts the
correct behaviour and fails today:

```sh
cargo test -p vl --test cli_adversarial -- --ignored adversarial8::
cargo test -p veil-core --test core_security -- --ignored adversarial8_core::
```

Summary: 8 high, 11 medium, 1 low. No critical: every leak below needs a
member's own action (a command they run in a sandbox, a mountpoint they
chose, a teammate's vault entry), not only a hostile remote.

| BUG-520 | high (**fixed**, round-8 vault wave) | `vl run`, team vault | **Fixed:** (1) `vl run` never sets execution-affecting names from a team vault (`team_vault::is_execution_variable`: `PATH`, `LD_*`, `DYLD_*`, `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`, `PROMPT_COMMAND`, `PS1`–`PS4`, `SHELL`, `IFS`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `PYTHON*`, `PERL*`, `RUBY*`, `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`, `GIT_*`, `NPM_CONFIG_*`, `XDG_*`, `VEIL_*`, compiler/build flags, proxies, CA bundles, tool config paths, case-insensitive) and warns; `vl secret set --scope` stores them but warns. (2) Default changed: `vl run` loads no team vault unless `--scope` is given or the device chose its default with `vl run --scope S --remember` (`.veil/local/run-scopes.json`); it says which scopes hold secrets. (3) New writes need shell identifiers; older `.`/`-` names are still read but not set by `vl run`. By default `vl run` loads the team vault of every scope you belong to, and team entries override the environment. Nothing restricts which names a member may set, so any member of any shared scope can store `BASH_ENV`, `PATH`, `LD_PRELOAD`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `KUBECONFIG` and the like. | BUG-560 | high (**fixed**, round-8 closing wave) | `ws exec` sandboxes / policy | **Fixed:** recordings of files a command wrote (`ws exec` sandboxes, full, sparse and ephemeral, and mounts: `SnapshotOptions::policy_from_command`) are pinned by the recorded `.veilpolicy` of the tree they were synced from (`Repo::command_policy`, `policy::command_edit`). An edit that cannot weaken it (same rules, appended `isolate`/`ignore`, dropped `public!`, or proved never weaker by the fold's exhaustive check) is recorded; one that only inserts `cloak`/`isolate`/`ignore` rules is recorded unless it weakens a path of the snapshot; anything else (truncate, a rule deleted, `public!`, `** public`, a scope retargeted; in a mount also a deleted, symlinked or unreadable file) is held back: it applies where stronger, the recorded classification where weaker (`P` paths, `BuildReport::policy_held_back`), and the tree keeps the recorded `.veilpolicy` (`BuildReport::policy_edit_held`), so later runs stay pinned without device state. The edit stays in the sandbox or mount overlay until `vl policy accept --workspace NAME` (`Repo::accept_workspace_policy`) records it and lists what it weakens; an ephemeral run drops it, with a warning. The mount is treated as a command (tools and agents write there). `vl serve` needs nothing: no method writes files, and its `snapshot` records the project directory under the accepted policy. Tests: `adversarial8` `policy_edits::*` (every shape through full, sparse, ephemeral sandboxes and the mount; accept; strengthening), `veil-core` `policy::tests::command_edits_are_judged_against_the_recorded_policy`. A command in a `vl ws exec` sandbox (typically an AI agent) can weaken `.veilpolicy` (truncate it, or add `secret/ public`), and the recording takes it as the member's own edit, so it applies at once and declassifies cloaked files in that workspace's next snapshot. In the project directory the member is the editor; in a sandbox the editor is the command. A sandbox's policy weakening must be held back like an incoming one (`policy_incoming`: the pin guards it until `vl policy accept`). Found by the round-8 sandbox wave (reported as low for the truncate case; upgraded). | sandbox recording builds with the member-edit policy rule. | `adversarial8` `policy_edits::*` |
| BUG-561 | medium (**fixed**, round-8 closing wave) | FUSE mount / memory | **Fixed:** open files live on disk: the first write or `truncate` of a lower-only file copies it up (atomically, durably), then reads and writes go straight to the upper file opened in place (`mount::fs::UpperFiles`/`DiskFiles`: `pread`/`pwrite`/`ftruncate`, synced on `flush`/`fsync`/`release`), so a truncate is a hole and memory does not grow with a file's size; renaming an upper file moves it (O(1), holes kept) instead of copying it through memory. Only lower-only files are read into memory while open (one decryption per open, bounded by the object). Tests: `adversarial8` `mount::a_sparse_file_in_the_mount_costs_no_memory` (peak RSS of the serving process across a 2 GiB truncate plus writes, and an existing file truncated to 2 GiB), `vl` unit test `mount::fs::tests::open_files_are_their_upper_file`. Remaining part of BUG-536: a `truncate` (or sparse write) up to the 4 GiB object cap fills the file into memory; on a small machine the kernel OOM killer can take the mount process down (other open files lose unsaved writes). Open files should live on disk (the overlay's upper file), not in memory. Found by the round-8 mount wave. | `mount.rs` open-file buffers are in memory. | `adversarial8` `mount::a_sparse_file_in_the_mount_costs_no_memory` |

## Round 8 hypotheses (not demonstrated)

* **`vl restore --from <embargoed fix> PATH` on a public line** probably publishes the names and sizes of the files the fix touches (inferred from the code by the Git-parity threat review; untested). For the next adversarial pass.
* **Mount, gc'd `base`.** `Recorder::open` falls back to the current snapshot but `state.base` keeps the id gc removed; the next `follow` then has `old_tree = None` and skips the overlap check, so upper edits silently shadow the workspace's change. Needs gc to prune a snapshot the op log still references (`--keep-ops-days`).
* **Mount, unlink race.** A file deleted between `with_view` and `reconcile` of a recording comes back. (**Addressed** in the round-8 mount wave: the recording and its `reconcile` run under one lock, `MountFs::record_with`.)
* **Mount, whole-file buffers.** A large file is decrypted into memory under the global lock on open, stalling every other request meanwhile (a same-user slowdown; see also BUG-536).
* **Sandbox, `vouch_written`** re-stats by path right after the write, so a concurrent writer's edit (a watcher left running by an earlier command) between the write and the stat could be vouched for as checkout content.
* **Sandbox, `sweep_stale`** judges an ephemeral sandbox stale by its owner's pid, so a `vl` in another pid namespace could have its live sandbox removed; `unshare -U` is not permitted on this machine.
* **Sandbox, `FICLONE`.** The clone path falls back on ext4 and tmpfs, so the fstat-before-and-after guard of `try_clone` was only read, not run.
* **Sandbox, deleting `../lock` during a run** could admit a concurrent run (tampering by the command only).
* **Team vault, revocation by an admin who has not pulled the member's last write:** the entry falls back to the older value for everyone and the newer record is "kept but ignored" with a pull warning. Follows from self-asserted timestamps (documented); not filed.
* **Team vault, a revoked member's writes made while revoked** count again after a re-grant. Documented ("they would count again after a re-grant"), but a re-grant silently brings in writes made while the member was out, stamped up to a day ahead.

Leads that held up (no bug): no team-vault name or value reached a public remote, `push --dry-run` (text or JSON), `vl serve`, warnings or error text (op-log descriptions name secrets, but `.veil/ops` never syncs); compaction cannot change the visible value (grouping by signer id and key matches `check_record`'s verdict, and keys come only from the verified ring); replayed or compacted records are outranked again; `=`/NUL names and NUL values are refused at write and when a record is opened; `i64::MAX` and negative timestamps are refused on sync, and the floor saturates; the two-scope refusal, its local override and an explicit `--scope` that fails to load all behave as documented. In the sandbox: same-size rewrites with `touch -r`, inode reuse and `touch -d` into the past or future are caught (ctime is in the stamp; future stamps are never trusted); FIFOs, `chmod 000` and symlinks over tracked files are kept with a warning, nothing hangs or writes through; a command rewriting `../manifest.json` or `../statcache` is overwritten from memory at the end of the run; unreadable files and conflict entries outside an `--only` set are carried; ephemeral `--with-isolated` refuses symlinked parents. In the mount: a non-member's view of a sealed conflict side is the redacted rendering and `stat` matches `read`; `.veil` in any case, symlinks and hard links are refused; no `allow_other`, `default_permissions`, `nosuid`, `nodev`, `0600` files; renames of open files follow POSIX; the record-before-command hook records in-process (no deadlock); torn whiteout lines can only resurrect a file, never delete one; non-member deletes and renames keep the hidden sealed entries.

## Round 8 coverage notes

* **Sandboxes** (`adversarial8::sandbox`): injection cleanup, rebuild triggers, the reaper and signals, error paths, special files and odd permissions, stat-cache games, and for `--only`: spine directories, policy edits, kept hand edits, unreadable entries, conflicts. Not covered: concurrency beyond the existing `ws_sandbox_cli.rs` tests; gc does not consult sandbox manifests, so `--keep-ops-days` pruning is one more trigger of BUG-548's rebuild.
* **Mount** (`adversarial8::mount`): real kernel mounts through `fusermount3`. Not tested: another OS user (needs root; `default_permissions` and the absence of `allow_other` were checked in the mount options instead), macFUSE, and a `vl serve` client over a mounted cloaked workspace (`serve` does not call `record_live`, so a served command does not see the mount's unrecorded edits). BUG-553 and BUG-554 probably apply to mount recordings too: they use the same `snapshot_workspace_with` over a backend that is not the project directory. Trees deeper than `MAX_TREE_DEPTH` make the recording fail and `vl ws unmount` refuse (not mount-specific). `readdir` re-lists the whole directory per request; acceptable at 3,000 entries.
* **Team vault** (`adversarial8::vault`, `adversarial8_core::vault`): core attacks use in-memory peers and forged or planted records (`VaultRecord::seal`), never the global test clock; CLI attacks use the real binary with a path team remote and two identities (`BASH_ENV` exfiltration shown with `/bin/bash`; `LD_PRELOAD` and `PATH` by reflecting them). Not attacked: the SFTP transport of records (covered by `team_vault.rs`), legacy rings, two concurrent `vl secret set` (serialised by `lock_meta`). Design gaps noted, not filed: `ws exec`'s injected-secret guard and the builder never consider team-vault (or local-vault) *values*, so `vl run -- vl ws exec agent -- …`, or a `vl run` build writing `$DB_PASSWORD` into a tracked file, records the value unless a scanner pattern matches; `vl undo` of a team-vault overwrite or `rm` says "set it again", but the superseded value has been compacted away (own writes) or is unreachable by any command.

## Round 9 findings (Opus, Git-parity features)

Baseline: `integration` @ `4a62259`. Line numbers refer to it. Tests:
`crates/vl/tests/cli_adversarial/adversarial9/` (modules `hooks`, `tags`, `history`,
`attributes`, `embargo`, `symlinks`; the hook tests need `python3` and
`make`, the `/proc` test is Linux-only). Each `#[ignore = "BUG-NNN: …"]`
test asserts the correct behaviour and fails today:

```sh
cargo test -p vl --test cli_adversarial -- --ignored adversarial9::
```

Summary: 4 high, 3 medium (a fourth, BUG-706, was about Git-format patches,
since removed), 2 low, plus BUG-682 pinned (deterministic, root
cause below). No critical: the code-execution findings need the victim to
trust a teammate's `.veilhooks` once (after that, nothing more), and the
sandbox escapes need a teammate's tree plus an agent run in `ws exec`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-700 | high (**fixed**, Git-parity fix wave 3) | hooks / code execution | **Fixed:** a directory named in `files`, or given to a command whose program may run it (`python*`, `pypy*`, `node`, `bun`, as the program or behind a launcher), is pinned as `tree:<blake3>` of a manifest of every file below it (kind, path, content digest; at most 1024 entries, 64 MiB, no links, else trust refuses), and the command gets a private copy of the checked bytes (`hooks::read_tree`, `tree_digest`, `trusted_tree_copy`). Other directories stay the command's data (`ruff check src`), pinned as `directory` only, so editing them does not untrust a linter; `python3 .` is refused. Old `directory` records for such paths no longer match: re-trust. Property test `hooks::tests::every_repository_file_a_hook_runs_is_pinned_or_refused`. A `.veilhooks` command argument that names a **directory** is pinned as the word `directory`, never by content (`vl hooks trust` lists `tools  directory` under "Pinned files", which reads as pinned). `run = ["python3", "tools"]` runs `tools/__main__.py` (as `node tools` runs `tools/index.js`); once the victim trusts it, a teammate's later change to `tools/__main__.py` runs on their device at every commit, with no new trust and no warning. Design 5a threat 1 ("the digests of `.veilhooks` and of every file it names"). The same holds for `files = ["dir"]`. | `crates/vl/src/hooks.rs:349` (`path_state`: a directory is `PathState::Dir`, content not hashed) and `:1024` (`run_one` passes a `Dir`-pinned argument through as the live path). Suggested fix: refuse directories as arguments and in `files` (or pin a manifest of every file below, and copy the tree). | `adversarial9::hooks::a_changed_file_inside_a_trusted_directory_argument_does_not_run` |
| BUG-701 | high (**fixed**, Git-parity fix wave 3) | hooks / code execution | **Fixed:** `hooks::classify` normalises every argument against the project (`spelled`): `./a`, `a//b`, `a/./b`, `a/` are `a`, and the value of `--opt=a` and `VAR=a` is a path too; each is pinned and replaced by its trusted copy after its prefix. What cannot be pinned is refused by `vl hooks trust` (and never runs on an older record): a path through `..` that lands in the project, an absolute path into the project or through `/proc`/`/dev/fd`, a path under `.veil`/`.git`, a path glued to a short option (`-Iscripts/x`), a `PATH`-like list (`PYTHONPATH=lib:tools`), and a `VAR=x` whose whole spelling is also a project file. An argument that names a repository file in any spelling but the canonical one is a literal: neither pinned nor replaced by its trusted copy. `run = ["sh", "./scripts/lint.sh"]` (also `scripts//lint.sh`, `scripts/./lint.sh`, `--rcfile=scripts/x`, `env LD_PRELOAD=./lib/x.so true`) is trusted with **no** pinned file, and `sh` reads whatever the script holds at commit time: a teammate's later edit runs. The copy-then-exec guarantee (threat 2) never applies to it. | `hooks.rs:469-484` (`classify`: `repo_path` refuses `.` and empty components and anything starting with `-` is a literal, so the argument becomes `Arg::Literal`; `VAR=./lib/x.so` is pinned as an absent file of that literal name, which never changes). Suggested fix: refuse any argument that resolves (after normalisation) to a repository path unless it is written canonically, and treat `--opt=path`/`VAR=path` forms the same way. | `adversarial9::hooks::a_changed_script_named_with_a_dot_slash_does_not_run` |
| BUG-702 | medium (**fixed**, Git-parity fix wave 3) | hooks / code execution | **Fixed:** `hooks::programs` counts every argument after a known launcher (`hooks::LAUNCHERS`: `env`, `nice`, `nohup`, `timeout`, `sudo`, `stdbuf`, `flock`, `vl`, …) as a program that may run, so `nice make`, `timeout 60 make`, `sudo -u x make` pin the `Makefile` and need `--i-understand-indirect`. `hooks::refusal` refuses, flag or not, code given as text (`sh -c`/`bash -ec`/`-lc` anywhere after a shell, `python3 -c`, `node -e`/`-p`, `perl -e`, `ruby -e`, `php -r`, `awk` without `-f`, `env -S`, `deno eval`) and programs that run their arguments through a shell or take them from their input (`xargs`, `watch`, `parallel`, `hyperfine`, `entr`). Build-tool indirection (threat 3) is detected only when the build tool is argv[0] or follows `env`. `["nice", "make"]`, `["timeout", "60", "make"]`, `["nohup", "make"]`, `["xargs", "make"]`, `["sh", "-c", "make lint"]` are trusted without `--i-understand-indirect` and without pinning the `Makefile`; a teammate's later `Makefile` edit runs. (Related, documented-limit territory: `python3 -c "import x"` reads `x.py` from the project root unpinned.) | `hooks.rs:426-446` (`effective_program` skips only `env`; `indirect` matches the first other word). Suggested fix: treat every argument that is a known build tool (or any command whose argv[0] is a launcher: `nice`, `timeout`, `nohup`, `xargs`, `sudo`, `exec`, shells with `-c`) as indirect, or refuse launchers. | `adversarial9::hooks::a_build_tool_behind_a_launcher_still_pins_its_files` |

## Round 9 hypotheses (not demonstrated)

* **Merge-driver `%P` substitution.** `LocalDrivers::merge` and `textconv` (`attr_cmd.rs:487-508`) substitute the path raw into the device's argv. A driver defined Git-style as `["sh", "-c", "tool %A %O %B %P"]` (Git sq-quotes `%P`) runs a teammate's file name `x;touch pwned` as shell; a name starting with `-` reaches tools that permute options. Needs the user's own `sh -c` definition; not filed.
* **Recording under a sealed `.veilattributes`.** The BUG-705 class for recording: a member snapshotting a public CRLF file under a sealed `* text` records LF, a non-member CRLF. Design 7 threat 11 accepts conversion differences on checkout; the recorded-bytes case is the same one-bit leak and was not tested separately.
* **Rename detection cost per command.** Each detection is bounded (limit², 1 GiB hashed, 2^28 comparisons), but auto-rebase of many descendants, `log --follow` and `blame --follow` run it once per step, so a hostile change set multiplies the bound. Not timed.
* **`vl hooks` `files` and TOCTOU.** Files a command only reads (`files = […]`) are checked by digest before the hook starts, then read by the hook from the live tree (only the program and argv files are copied). A local race only.
* **Mount and relative links.** `MountFs` serves links as leaves and the kernel follows them from the mountpoint; a mountpoint inside the project lets `x -> ../.env` reach it. The mount promises nothing about escapes (design 6 threat 8 is about `MountFs` itself), so not filed.

Leads that held up (no bug): the no-follow writer (`vfs/beneath.rs`) for checkout, restore and sandbox writes; reserved names (`.veil` in any case or with HFS-ignorable characters) in checkout; `.veilpolicy` deletion followed by a file under its cloak (held back, `P`); cloaked annotated tags (kept cloaked over `--force`, never pushed public); release tags never auto-advance; escapes in symlink targets (every display path); bidi controls in `.veilhooks` as shown by `vl hooks trust`; CRLF conflicts resolved in a CRLF editor.

* **Tags** (`adversarial9::tags`): Veil-remote pulls of annotated tags. Forged and transplanted atags are refused by `remote::fetch_annotation` and `annotation_problem` (read, and covered by `tag_object.rs` unit tests); not re-tested.

It is timing-dependent; `serve.rs` last changed in the colocated merge (`217f997`).

## Findings from the local-tooling round

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |

## Findings from the colocated and final fix waves (native code)

The colocated Git mode and its findings (BUG-740 to BUG-756, BUG-759,
BUG-760) were removed with Git interop. Three findings of those waves are
about native code:

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-757 | low (**fixed**, final fix wave) | `vl restore` | **Fixed:** only a *cloaked* (sealed) file restored into a deleted directory failed: the restored entry is carried into the snapshot with `conflict::set_entry`, which refused a path whose directory the working copy's tree no longer had. It now creates missing directories (and removing under one is a no-op). `vl restore <path>` of a file whose directory was deleted (`rm -r`) puts the file back, then fails with `error: not found: <path>` (exit 1). | Not investigated; the restore itself succeeds, a later step reports the path missing. | `cli_basic::working_copy_cli::restoring_a_cloaked_file_into_a_deleted_directory_works` |
| BUG-758 | low (**fixed**, final fix wave) | tests | **Fixed:** the bound is 2× + 0.1 s over the best of five runs each (the quadratic regression it guards against is far slower than 2×). `core_engine::attributes::a_megabyte_of_patterns_slows_a_snapshot_little` asserts a 1.2× timing ratio and fails under full-suite load (206 ms → 399 ms seen twice); passes alone. Needs a looser bound, or a work counter instead of wall time. | timing assertion | the test itself |
| BUG-761 | critical (**fixed**, final fix wave; feature **removed**, format 8) | embargo / publication | **Fixed:** a line under an unreleased embargo stays under it. The builder keeps the wrapper even when the tree holds nothing to hide (`embargo::wrap_line`), and a working-copy tree that is not wrapped while an ancestor is an unreleased embargoed merge is wrapped at its next change, with its parent's public view as the fallback (`Repo::keep_line_embargo`, in every recording path: the snapshot, `build_amending_carried`, `commit_fs_as_child_with`); without the embargo's key, the edits are held back as before. Found in the final fix wave. Plain Veil: `vl merge fix@- --into main --embargo`, `vl new main`, delete the fix's file (`auth.rs`), any `vl` command, put the file back, `vl commit`, `vl tag set main -r @-`, `vl push` to a public remote: a clone of the remote has the fix in plaintext before the release. | `embargo::wrap` returns the bare fallback when the tree equals it, so a snapshot that deleted the fix's files took the working copy off the embargo; the builder judged "under embargo" by the parent *tree* only (`keep_embargo`), so a later re-add was a public edit. | `core_engine::embargo_release::deleting_and_putting_back_the_fix_never_publishes_it` |

## Findings from the scale round (benchmark baseline)

Baseline: `integration` @ `b549e1e`, measured by `crates/veil-bench` (`scripts/bench-scale.sh 1g`). Numbers and causes: `docs/design/scale/BASELINE.md`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-800 | medium (**fixed**, BUG-800 streaming wave) | store / memory | **Fixed:** the write and transfer side now streams (`docs/design/scale/4-background-cleanup-streaming.md`, G1). `StorageBackend::create_stream` writes a file in pieces and names it only at `finish` (disk: `O_EXCL` temp, fsync, rename, directory fsync; SFTP: pipelined writes, `fsync@openssh.com`, `posix-rename`; others buffer). `pack::PackWriter` writes `PackBuilder`'s exact bytes as objects come, keeping only the entry table and delta depths, and computes the trailer's BLAKE3 while streaming. gc and `PackSink` (pull and push) use it; sync's last versions per path are a 64 MiB LRU. A pull spools the remote's packs to `.veil/objects/incoming/pull` instead of memory, after checking free space (the error names the space needed). Publish order (`.pack`, then `.idx`, then the op head), the received objects' checks and the format are unchanged. Measured on the 1 GB benchmark: clone 367 MiB (SFTP 424), pull of one snapshot 171 MiB, pull with nothing new 139 MiB, gc 297 MiB first and 467 MiB again, initial push 220 MiB (SFTP 341): every case under the 512 MiB gate (`docs/design/scale/BASELINE.md`). Tests: `scale_findings::a_clone_of_a_large_store_does_not_hold_it_in_memory` (peak +33 MiB for a 195 MiB store; +402 MiB before), `durability::an_interrupted_pack_write_leaves_no_visible_pack`, `durability::pulled_packs_are_published_before_their_index_and_the_operation`, `sftp_backend::streams_are_published_whole_and_only_on_finish`, `sync_incremental::a_pull_that_would_fill_the_disk_says_how_much_it_needs`. Earlier, **partly fixed (orchestrator review):** the 1 GB benchmark after this wave measured `vl clone` at 12.1 s and **1,205 MiB** (was 54.5 s, 1,975 MiB), still over the 512 MiB gate. `pull` and `gc` were not measured: the run stopped early. What remains is the write and transfer side: `PullSource::prefetch` downloads remote packs into memory, and `PackBuilder` holds each pack whole before writing (`docs/design/scale/4-background-cleanup-streaming.md`, G1). It is next, as its own stream. What this wave did: packs held whole share one process-wide budget (`pack::SLURP_BUDGET`, 64 MiB, least recently used out; each store holds its own copy, so `--full` walks still read the remote's bytes), and only packs of at most 16 MiB are held whole (several hot packs fit; larger ones are always read by range, so they never thrash). `gc` closes a pack every 128 MiB of kept objects (`gc::GC_PACK_LIMIT`; `GcReport::packs`), so its builder never holds the whole store; pull and clone already split at 128 MiB. Measured with `scripts/bench-scale.sh 1g`: see `docs/design/scale/BASELINE.md`. **Memory grows with the store.** At 1 GB, `vl clone` peaks at 1.98 GB RSS, `vl gc` at 1.0 GB, `vl pull` of one snapshot at 950 MB, and `vl pull` with nothing new at 560 MB. Each is over the scale gate's 512 MiB, and they grow linearly with the store. Reading every object of a 117 MiB store in 4 packs grows RSS by 117 MiB. | `crates/veil-core/src/pack.rs:415` (`Pack::whole`) keeps a whole pack in memory once it has served 64 reads (`SLURP_AFTER`), for any pack of at most 256 MiB (`SLURP_LIMIT`). The limit is per pack, and nothing bounds the total, so any history walk (pull, clone, gc, log) ends up holding every pack. Suggested fix: one store-wide budget for slurped packs (LRU), or ranged reads only. | `crates/veil-core/tests/scale_findings.rs::reading_every_pack_does_not_hold_the_whole_store_in_memory` |
| BUG-801 | medium (**fixed**, final fix wave) | locking / concurrency | **Fixed:** `Repo::snapshot_workspace_with` scans the working copy before taking `.veil/lock`, with every new object staged in memory (`ObjectStore::begin_staging`, at most 32 MiB; an object already on disk is not adopted either, since another transaction may not have made it durable yet: stream O's threat 5). A clean working copy is then recorded without the lock at all. A changed one takes the lock, checks that the workspace, the accepted policy and the scanner's rules are what the scan saw, and publishes the staged objects (under the lock, unsynced, made durable by the transaction's barrier) with the tree; if anything moved, or the content was too large to stage, it builds again under the lock as before. Not stream O: the lock, the wait and the op log are unchanged; O replaces the in-memory staging with on-disk staging and the lock with a compare-and-swap of the op heads. Tests: the reproduction (64 concurrent `vl status` on 20,000 files) passes in about 4 s; `core_durability::adversarial_lock::racing_snapshots_of_one_directory_lose_nothing` (8 handles editing and snapshotting one directory: no fork, no lost edit) and `…::a_clean_snapshot_needs_no_lock_and_large_content_still_records`. **Concurrent commands fail instead of queueing.** Every `vl` command holds `.veil/lock` while it records the project directory. With enough commands at once, contenders give up after 15 s with `repository is locked: another process holds the lock`. The 64-agent profile at 1 GB failed 194 of 640 iterations (`ws exec`, `tag set` and `push` alike), and 64 concurrent `vl status` on 20,000 files fail 15 times. Nothing is lost, but agents and editors see random failures. | `crates/veil-core/src/workspace.rs:280` (`Repo::snapshot_workspace_with` opens its transaction, which takes the lock, before `build_tree_cached` scans the working copy at `:312`), together with `crates/veil-core/src/lock.rs:197` (`LockOptions::default().wait` = 15 s; polling with back-off, no fairness). The scale round's stream O (lock-free op log, compare-and-swap snapshot) removes the cause; a longer or fair wait would only hide it. | `crates/vl/tests/scale_findings_cli.rs::many_concurrent_commands_all_succeed`, `core_durability::adversarial_lock::racing_snapshots_of_one_directory_lose_nothing` |

## Scale round: adversarial pass on stream O

Branch `scale-o-oplog` @ `0c8fce4` merged into `integration` @ `58197ca`. Every finding below is a race between the member's own legitimate commands (an agent's `ws exec`, a long pull, `vl gc`, the human's commands): no attacker outside the trust boundary is needed, and none is involved. Reproductions: `core_durability::oplog_adversarial`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-802 | high (**fixed**, stream O adversarial fixes) | op log / undo | **Fixed:** `Repo::merge_plan` skips a side's rewrite whose old snapshot that side still shows, as a ref or as an ancestor of one (one walk from the side's refs down to the oldest rewritten snapshot, `GraphIndex::down_to`). **A merge re-applies a rewrite that its side undid.** `vl abandon X` (or `vl describe X`, any amend of a parent of `@`) then `vl undo` in one workspace, while any other command lands concurrently (an agent's commit, a `vl tag set`): the merge of the two heads applies the undone abandon again, so `@` loses X again (or moves onto the amended X the user undid). Recoverable from the op log, but the user's undo silently disappears. | `crates/veil-core/src/repo.rs` `Repo::merge_plan`: a side's rewrite is skipped as "undone since" only when its old snapshot is a *direct* ref of the side's view (`refs.contains(&old)`); an undone rewrite of a parent of `@` leaves the old snapshot visible only as an ancestor. | `undone_abandon_is_not_redone_by_a_concurrent_merge`, `undone_amend_is_not_redone_by_a_concurrent_merge` |
| BUG-803 | high (**fixed**, stream O adversarial fixes) | op log / merge | **Fixed:** `OpStore::split` has no time floor: it walks common operations too (the classic merge-base walk, ancestors of a common operation marked stale and never taken as the base) and stops once everything still queued is common, so it finds the fork point however old, and stays cheap (a timestamp out of order, a merge's, no longer sends one side to the root). The floor stays in `drop_ancestors`, where a miss only costs an extra merge. **The merge base is lost when one side's history spans more than an hour.** A command that runs over an hour (a long pull, a suspended `vl`, a clock step) lands beside a line of commands that started right after it: `OpStore::split` stops an hour below the newest heads, finds no common operation, and the merge runs against an empty view. Tags and workspaces deleted on one side come back (and the next `vl push` publishes a withdrawn tag), concurrent moves of every tag and workspace become conflicts decided by operation id (the stale side's values win about half of the time), and snapshots abandoned on one side become visible again. | `crates/veil-core/src/oplog.rs` `OpStore::split`: the walk stops expanding at `ts < floor` (oldest start minus `ANCESTRY_SLACK_MS`), so the operation the long command forked from is reached by one side only; `merge_plan` then uses `View::default()` as the base. | `merge_base_is_found_below_the_ancestry_slack` |
| BUG-804 | medium (**fixed**, stream O adversarial fixes) | op log / gc | **Fixed:** `Transaction::recheck` fails the commit ("… was pruned by `vl gc --keep-ops-days` while it ran; run the command again") when an operation of its base is gone. **An operation whose base was pruned meanwhile is merged against an empty view.** A long command starts from operation H; two commands land, and `vl gc --keep-ops-days 0` (which keeps only the heads and their parents) prunes H; the long command then publishes an operation whose parent is gone. Its merge with the heads has no common operation: same harm as BUG-803 (here, a deleted tag returns). Threat 13 assumed unknown ancestry only costs "a harmless extra merge". | `crates/veil-core/src/transaction.rs` `Transaction::recheck` does not check that the base still exists; `merge_plan` falls back to `View::default()`. | `transaction_whose_base_was_pruned_does_not_merge_against_nothing` |
| BUG-805 | medium (**fixed**, stream O adversarial fixes) | op log / embargo | **Fixed:** in a merge transaction, a policy refusal of `Repo::rebase_tree` leaves that snapshot (and what is built on it) on its old parents, and the merge warns "change … was left on its old parents: moving it onto a concurrent rewrite was refused (…)"; the confinement check still runs on the result. **A merge whose rebase is refused makes every later command fail.** One side moves change Y onto an embargoed merge (Y joins embargo E1); the other merges a second fix into Y's line under its own embargo E2. Each is allowed on its own view. The merge's rebase of E2's merge onto the moved Y combines two unreleased embargoes, which `merge_trees` refuses with a policy error; every command merges the heads first (at `Repo::open`), so every command fails from then on, `vl embargo release` (which the error suggests) and `vl op restore` included. Threat 18 covered only confinement failures. | `crates/veil-core/src/transaction.rs` `Transaction::rebase_descendants` propagates the policy error of `Repo::rebase_tree` out of `merge_rebase`, `Transaction::commit` and `Repo::settle`. | `merge_combining_two_embargoes_degrades_instead_of_failing_forever` |
| BUG-806 | medium (**fixed**, stream O adversarial fixes) | op log / compare-and-swap | **Fixed:** for a transaction that recorded a working copy (`expect_wc`), `recheck` and `OpStore::publish` run under one process-wide mutex, so a second recorder in the process checks only after the first published, and is superseded (and builds again). Across processes the CLI's recorders already hold the workspace's `WcLock` for the whole recording. **Two recorders of one workspace in one process both publish.** The compare-and-swap is a check (`Transaction::recheck`) followed by a separate publication: A passes the check; B scans (seeing A's edit and its own), checks and publishes; A then publishes over the workspace B moved. The merge keeps one working copy (by operation id) and warns; the other's edit is only in a visible change. Threads of one process (an embedder, `vl serve` paths that do not serialise, a mount's threads) are not kept apart by `WcLock`, which is re-entrant within a process. BUG-801's `adversarial_lock::racing_snapshots_of_one_directory_lose_nothing` failed this way 2 times in 120 runs under load (0 in 150 after the fix). | `crates/veil-core/src/transaction.rs` `Transaction::commit`: `recheck()` and `ops.publish()` are not atomic, and nothing serialises them between threads. | `two_recorders_of_one_workspace_never_both_publish` |

## Scale round: stream P (two-phase pushes)

Found while building stream P, from the hypothesis "push racing an undo of a staged embargo release" (stream-O adversarial pass). Like stream O's findings, a race between the member's own commands: no attacker is needed. Reproductions: `core_sync::push_two_phase`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-807 | high (**fixed**, stream P) | push / embargo | **Fixed:** phase B of the two-phase push, under the remote's lock, first makes the staged releases permanent (`publish_staged_releases`), then checks that every embargo the plan treated as released (recorded with the staged packs) still is. If one is not, the staging is removed under the lock and the push plans again, withholding the fix. A push journal staged under a release that was taken back since is discarded with its staging. `vl push --full` makes the staged releases permanent before it decides what to withhold. Residual: bytes uploaded to the push's staging before the undo reached the remote's disk (removed under the lock; unreadable through vl), as an aborted upload always did. **A push racing an undo of a staged release publishes the embargoed fix.** `vl embargo release E`, then `vl push` to a public remote, and while it uploads, `vl undo` of the release in another terminal: the undo succeeds (the release was only staged), the push still sends the fix's history (plaintext, here), and the remote's record of E stays unreleased. Readers of the public mirror get the fix before its release. Predates stream O: push never held the local lock. | `crates/veil-core/src/remote.rs` `push_with`: `sendable_tags` computes the withheld history from the release state at the start (`Keychain::embargo_released` counts a staged release); the objects are sent; only then `publish_staged_releases` makes the releases permanent, skipping one taken back meanwhile. Nothing checks that what was treated as released still is. | `push_racing_an_undo_of_a_staged_release_never_publishes_the_fix`, `a_published_fix_always_comes_with_its_released_record`, `nothing_withheld_is_ever_staged` (property: releases and take-backs between the phases) |

## Scale round: adversarial pass on stream P

Adversarial pass on the two-phase push (`t3/a6c6d6aa` @ `167ffc1` merged onto `integration` @ `beeff23`). Attackers: readers of a public mirror (they read whatever a push publishes there, and can never be made to forget it); the trigger for BUG-808 and BUG-809 is a sequence of the member's own commands. Reproductions: `core_sync::push_two_phase`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-808 | high (**fixed**, stream P adversarial fixes) | push / resume / embargo | **Fixed:** the walk takes each reused object out of the set of staged ones as it meets it (`ResumeSource`); if anything is left and the plan sends something, the staging is removed and the attempt plans again with a new journal. A plan that sends nothing publishes nothing, so a team push rejected meanwhile still keeps its staging for the merge. **A resumed push publishes packs that an earlier attempt staged and that its own plan no longer sends.** A push to a public mirror (tag `wip` at a change) is interrupted after staging. The member then finds the change is a security fix: they delete `wip` and merge the change under an embargo instead. The next `vl push` resumes the journal (same remote and tags) and renames every staged pack into `objects/pack/`, so the embargoed fix's plaintext is published on the mirror, beside a plan that withholds it. The same happens for a change withdrawn or cloaked between attempts, and on team remotes. | `crates/veil-core/src/remote.rs` `push_with`: `Journal::reusable` counts every journalled pack whose files are whole, and `publish` renames all of them. The journal is discarded only when `public` or the released embargoes changed, not when the plan changed (the design sketch: "The staged packs are still reused as known objects if they are present"). | `a_resumed_push_never_publishes_what_its_plan_no_longer_sends`; `a_rejected_team_push_reuses_its_staging_after_the_merge` (reuse kept) |
| BUG-809 | high (**fixed**, stream P adversarial fixes) | push / embargo | **Fixed:** `sendable_tags` reads the release state once (`released_embargoes`) and decides the withheld history from that reading (`embargo_withheld_given`). It returns the reading, which becomes the journal's `released`, the list phase B checks after `publish_staged_releases`. **BUG-807's fix checked a different reading of the release state from the one the plan was made from.** `push_with` decided the withheld history from live reads of the keychain inside `sendable_tags`, then read the released embargoes again for the journal. A `vl undo` of a staged release in another terminal, landing between the two reads, left the fix unwithheld and unchecked, so it was published on the public mirror (the third read of the release state in the sweep). The same happened for a release and its undo, both during the push. | `crates/veil-core/src/remote.rs` `push_with` (before the fix): `sendable_tags` → `embargo_withheld` called `Keychain::embargo_released` live; `released_embargoes` ran afterwards. | `an_undo_landing_anywhere_in_phase_a_never_publishes_the_fix`, `a_release_and_its_undo_during_phase_a_never_publish_the_fix` (sweeps over every read of the release state) |
| BUG-810 | low (**fixed**, scale stream G2) | push / staging expiry | **Fixed:** expiry no longer compares another machine's clock with ours: each host keeps, on the remote, when it first saw each staging directory with its current `touched` stamp (`.veil/local/push-expiry/<host>.json`, by its own clock), and removes one only after it has seen it unchanged for a week of that clock. A live push rewrites `touched` whenever it writes, so its week starts again; hostile or skewed stamps are only compared for equality. **A pusher whose clock is more than a week fast removes other pushes' live staging.** Expiry compares the `touched` stamp, written with the staging pusher's clock, with the clock of whoever cleans up (every push, without the lock, and gc). The fast-clock member's push removes the staging of every push in phase A at the time. Each of those pushes then plans and uploads again, and fails after three attempts ("what was uploaded is kept for it", although it was removed). No data is lost. A clock that slow on the staging side has the same effect. | `crates/veil-core/src/remote.rs` `expire_push_staging`: `now.saturating_sub(t) > PUSH_STAGING_EXPIRY_MS` with `t` from another machine's clock. SFTP metadata carries no server-side time (`Metadata::unstamped`) to compare with instead. | `a_teammate_with_a_fast_clock_never_removes_a_live_push_staging` (un-ignored), `only_week_old_staging_is_removed` (changed to the new rule) |
| BUG-811 | critical (**fixed**, scale stream G2; **pre-existing**: reproduces on `integration` @ `beeff23`) | local gc / lock-free op log | **Fixed:** on a lock-free repository gc deletes only under a fence (`crates/veil-core/src/maintenance.rs`). Every lock-free transaction registers itself (`objects/incoming/live-<owner>`) before it reads the heads and until it has published its operation; gc raises `.veil/local/gc/fence` only once none is registered (waiting up to 5 s for a quiet moment, then up to 60 s with the fence raised; otherwise it deletes nothing that run and says so), and transactions that meet a raised fence wait for it. Under the fence gc reads its roots again (the head files, every operation, keep markers, the checkout pointer) and marks what they reach; only the first listing's operations are pruned, and an object that became reachable survives (with a loose copy if its old pack goes). A commit also checks that every object its view gained and its new objects name is still present ("… was removed by `vl gc` while the command ran; run the command again"), for ids carried from an older view. gc takes the gc lease (`.veil/gc.lock`, an `flock`) instead of `.veil/lock` there, so a recording that writes metadata under `.veil/lock` never waits for gc. `--prune-now` is safe beside running commands (help and guide changed). Load run: 12 copies × 8 rounds, 96/96 pass (63/96 on `2a337ee`, the same binary and load). **`vl gc --keep-ops-days 0 --prune-now` racing `vl ws exec` loses objects under load.** Found while verifying this pass; not in stream P's code. `cli_conformance::conformance_sync::gc::gc_concurrent_with_commits_loses_nothing` passes alone (0/30) but fails when 12 copies run at once: 31/96 on `beeff23`, 44/96 with stream P. Seen: `vl fsck` reports "directory snapshot …:/: tree … is missing" (a recorded snapshot's tree pruned); and `ws exec` / `ws exec --record-only` failing with "object … is not present in this store". Also (found by the deterministic reproduction): the operation itself pruned, written but not yet named by its head file, so the head names a missing operation. | `crates/veil-core/src/gc.rs` `gc`, against `Transaction::commit` (`transaction.rs`): a transaction renames its staged objects into the store (`ObjectStore::publish_tx_staging`) and only then writes its operation and head file. A gc whose inventory came after the renames and whose head read came before the head file saw those objects (and the operation file) as unreachable and deleted them at once with grace 0. The same for an object the transaction found already present and reused, and for an operation older than the window that is about to become a head. Marking what live staging directories reference covered only objects still staged. | `core_durability::gc_concurrency::{prune_now_never_deletes_what_a_transaction_published_but_not_named, prune_now_never_deletes_an_object_a_transaction_reused, prune_now_beside_many_writers_loses_nothing, a_tag_carried_from_an_older_view_is_checked_at_commit}` (fail on `2a337ee`), `…::{prune_now_never_deletes_what_a_transaction_is_renaming, a_transaction_whose_base_gc_prunes_records_whole_or_refuses, gc_on_a_thread_holding_a_transaction_defers_deletion}`; `gc_concurrent_with_commits_loses_nothing` (un-ignored; 12 × 8 under load) |
