## Scale round: adversarial pass on stream G2

Adversarial pass on incremental maintenance and the BUG-811 deletion fence (`t3/2b0ff3fc` @ `529a22c` merged onto `integration` @ `2a337ee`). gc is the one component that deletes, so the attacker is the member's own concurrent commands (agents run many at once) and crashes: the trigger is always a sequence of the member's own commands, a `kill -9` or an I/O error. Reproductions: `core_durability::gc_concurrency`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-814 | critical (**fixed**, stream G2 adversarial fixes) | gc / remotes / deletion fence | **Fixed:** with its fence raised and no transaction registered, gc also takes `.veil/lock` before it marks again and deletes (`maintenance::raise_fence`); if it cannot within the lock's usual wait, it deletes nothing that run and says so. Writers that take `.veil/lock` instead of registering are then finished (their operation is a head, read by the second marking) or not started. **`vl -R ../hub gc --prune-now` deletes what a push over SSH is publishing.** The guide's way to collect a remote opens the bare hub as a lock-free repository, so G2's gc takes the gc lease and the fence, not `.veil/lock` (which it held for the whole run before). A push over SSH (a network backend: no staging, so no registration; it holds only `.veil/lock`) that has renamed its packs into `pack/` and not yet written its operation is invisible to the fence: gc drops those packs as garbage and the push then records a tag whose history is gone on the hub (`Missing` reading the pushed file, fsck: missing snapshot). The same for every transaction over a network backend and every writer that holds `.veil/lock` without registering. A push over a path registers and was safe (the control). | `crates/veil-core/src/maintenance.rs` `raise_fence` excluded only registered transactions; `GcHold::take` decides by `Repo::lock_free()`, which is true for a bare repository opened as a project, while its pushers use the remote protocol (`.veil/lock`). | `gc_concurrency::hub_gc_never_deletes_what_a_push_over_ssh_is_publishing` (fails on `529a22c`; 96/96 under 12 × 8 load with the fix) |
| BUG-815 | high (**fixed**, stream G2 adversarial fixes) | gc / prune epoch / crash | **Fixed:** the prune epoch moves under the fence before anything is deleted, not after; a spurious move only makes commands check what they carried. **A gc that dies after deleting (`kill -9`, EIO, a full disk) leaves the prune epoch unchanged, so a command carrying an id from its older view records it unchecked.** BUG-811's fix checks carried ids (a revision `vl tag set` resolved before gc ran, a long command's base) only when the epoch changed since the command read its view, and gc wrote the epoch as its last step. A gc killed or failing anywhere between its first deletion and that write (removing pruned operations, loose objects, packs, keep markers, writing the pending list) made the next such commit record a tag (or a parent) that names a deleted snapshot. | `crates/veil-core/src/gc.rs` `prune_store`: `bump_prune_epoch` after step 7, conditioned on what was deleted. | `gc_concurrency::a_gc_that_dies_after_deleting_still_makes_carried_ids_checked` (fails on `529a22c`; 96/96 under 12 × 8 load with the fix) |
| BUG-816 | low (**removed**, SFTP remotes removed) | push staging / hub gc | **Removed:** the two-phase push to plain-file remotes, its staging and its expiry were removed with SFTP and path remotes in the simplification pass, part 1. Seen in the stream G2 adversarial pass, not filed there. Hub gc no longer holds `.veil/lock` for its whole run, so it can remove a push's staging directory (untouched for a week) while that push is publishing. The push fails and uploads again; nothing is lost. | Expiry of `push-*` staging runs during hub gc outside the lock that phase B holds. Suggested fix: skip staging whose journal shows a phase-B publish in progress, or expire staging only under `.veil/lock`. | none yet |

## Hub milestone S1

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-817 | low (**fixed**, Hub S1; **pre-existing**: `integration` @ `cbfe9ee`) | docs / guide | **Fixed:** `docs/guide/embargoes.md` line 10 showed the planned `vl merge … --embargo-for … --until …` as a runnable command, so `guide_commands_parse` failed on `integration`. It is now marked as planned, with placeholders the check skips. | The docs rewrite (`8a585eb`) added a command of a later milestone without the placeholder syntax that marks it | `vl` `docgen::guide_commands_parse` |
| BUG-818 | medium (**fixed**, BUG-818 fix; **pre-existing**: `integration` @ `cbfe9ee`) | checkout / speed | **Fixed:** checkout stages every file beside its path (`StorageBackend::write_staged`: a temp file, unsynced, with the mode set on it), makes them all durable with one barrier (the object store's parallel `fsync`s), renames them into place, and makes the names and its removals durable with a second barrier; only then does it return and the caller save `checkout.json`. A power loss leaves each path old or new, never torn; an EIO barrier fails the checkout with the move still pending, and finishing it rewrites every file already holding the target; resuming removes the staged debris. The 10k clone went from 10,044 to 1,014 ms through the server (10,363 to 1,178 ms from a path remote), with 10,155 `fsync`s instead of 20,154 (`docs/design/scale/OPENSCION.md`). `syncfs` was 0.2 s faster on a quiet disk but was not used: before Linux 5.8 it does not report writeback errors, and it waits for every other process's dirty data. **Checkout makes every file durable on its own**: a temporary file, `fsync`, rename, `fsync` of the directory, so a 10,001-file clone makes 20,154 `fsync`s, 7.3 s of a 9.4 s clone on an ext4 NVMe disk (`strace -f -w -c`). Cloning through the server and from a path remote take the same time (`docs/design/scale/OPENSCION.md`); the OpenScion "clone everything" gate (544 ms) is out of reach until checkout batches its durability. `OVERVIEW.md`'s 483 ms does not reproduce on this machine. | `checkout` writes through the durable `StorageBackend::write` per file instead of `write_unsynced` plus one barrier | `veil-bench openscion` (the "Veil, path remote" column); `core_engine` `checkout_speed::checkout_of_many_files_is_one_barrier_not_one_fsync_per_file`; `core_durability` `crash::crash_during_workspace_switch` (power loss tears staged copies), `crash::eio_during_workspace_switch` |
| BUG-830 | medium (**fixed**, post-S1 fix round; **pre-existing**: `integration` @ `cbfe9ee`; found by the BUG-818 fix) | clone / crash | **Fixed:** both clones check out through `Repo::check_out_new`, which journals the checkout like every other move (`move_working_copy` from the root snapshot: `pending` before the first file), so the next command finishes it. A `--only` clone journals from the target tree without its directory (`Materialised::shown_as`): finishing it writes only that directory, whose objects are the only ones fetched. The reproduction now kills a real `vl clone` (path and `--only` through the server) as soon as its checkout starts. **A `vl clone` killed during its checkout is recorded as deleting the files it had not written.** Clone writes `.veil/` and the new change, checks the files out, and saves `checkout.json` only afterwards. Killed in between (`kill -9`, power loss), the next command finds no record, takes the directory for one holding its change, and records every file not yet written as deleted (`vl status` shows them as `D`). Both clones (`main.rs` from a path, `hub_cmd.rs` from the server). | The clone's checkout is not journalled (`working_copy` does it for every other move: `pending` before the first file). A plain journal does not fit `--only`, whose tree is a restriction with no snapshot to resume to. | `cli_sync` `clone_crash_cli::a_clone_killed_during_its_checkout_never_records_deletions`; `server_hub` `sync::a_one_directory_clone_killed_during_its_checkout_is_finished` |
| BUG-831 | low (**fixed**, post-S1 fix round; **pre-existing**: `integration` @ `cbfe9ee`; found by the BUG-818 fix) | tests / flaky | **Fixed:** the liveness half no longer depends on the scheduler: once the swapper stops, a second checkout must complete the whole tree; the safety half (nothing outside, no abort) is checked on every attempt as before. 96 of 96 runs pass, 32 at a time beside 16 busy loops. **`symlinks::a_directory_swapped_for_a_link_mid_checkout_receives_nothing_outside` fails under load on its liveness half** ("no attempt wrote anything"): once in a full `verify-fast` run; 22 of 96 on `ab4304a` and 7 of 96 with the BUG-818 fix, run 32 at a time beside 16 busy loops. Its safety half (nothing written outside) held in every run. | A swapper thread that wins every race, on a loaded machine, makes every one of the 400 writes refused in all 5 attempts: a liveness assertion that depends on scheduling. | `core_working_copy` `symlinks::a_directory_swapped_for_a_link_mid_checkout_receives_nothing_outside` (under load) |
| BUG-832 | high (**fixed**, adversarial pass on the post-S1 fixes; **pre-existing**: `integration` @ `b78e52d`; found by the post-S1 fix round) | clone `--only` / secrets | **Fixed:** a sealed entry is kept as recorded against a rule that isolates or ignores its path, unless this snapshot's own edit of `.veilpolicy` reclassifies it (`Builder::keeps_sealing`); nothing of the local file is recorded (under such a rule it may be the member's own: sealing it would hand it to the scope, `adversarial::a_view_without_the_policy_never_seals_a_local_only_file`), so an edit there stays local and `vl status` says so. A `.veilpolicy` the working copy never showed (`--only`) is not a policy change. **A clone without the project's `.veilpolicy` on disk records the folder's secret as deleted, and its next push deletes it for everyone.** Not only `vl clone --only DIR`: a whole clone by anyone who cannot read the root `.veilpolicy` (the project root is private to admins by default) too. `vl status` shows `D DIR/.env [cloaked:team]` and `L DIR/.env [isolated]`. | The working copy's policy is what classifies files; without the project's `.veilpolicy` it is the built-in rules, which keep `.env` local-only (`isolated`): the builder returned no entry for an isolated path (`plain_file_entry`), so the sealed entry counted as deleted. "Sealed content keeps its audience" (`Builder::audience`) covered public classifications, not isolated or ignored ones. An `--only` clone also took its never-materialised `.veilpolicy` for a deleted one. | `server_hub` `sync::bug_832_a_one_directory_clone_keeps_the_folders_secrets` (fin `--only`, fin whole, admin `--only`), `adversarial::a_view_without_the_policy_never_seals_a_local_only_file` |

## Server S1: adversarial pass

Independent adversarial pass on milestone S1 (`t3/7a33597b` @ `ab4304a` merged onto `integration` @ `c3e425a`): the server is the one thing between private code and the internet, so attackers are anyone on Earth, a signed-up stranger, a participant without a folder, the operator of another Veil server, and (for secrets only, HUB.md §13.6) a compromised server. Reproductions: `veil-server` `server_hub::adversarial` (Docker: `scripts/verify-server.sh`), `vl` `cli_security::policy_cli`. Fixes: "server S1 adversarial fixes".

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-819 | critical (**fixed**, server S1 adversarial fixes) | sign-in / relay | **Fixed:** sign-in also requires the server name the device signed for to be one this server's TLS certificate is valid for (`tls::names`, rustls-webpki: the check the client made before it signed). **Another Veil server's operator signs in as anyone who signs in to theirs.** Attacker: the operator of server E. When a victim's `vl` signs in to E (`vl login`, or silently after any 401 E answers), E asks this server for a challenge for the victim's key and hands it to the victim, whose `vl` signs `E-name ‖ challenge`; E sends that login here with `Host: E-name`. The only check was `hub == Host`, and the relaying server writes both. Harm: a session as the victim: every private folder, push, group changes. | `crates/veil-server/src/auth.rs` `login` compared the signed name with the request's `Host` header, which the caller controls | `server_hub::adversarial::bug_819_a_login_relayed_by_another_server_is_refused`, `veil-server` `tls::tests::names_are_the_certificates_own` |
| BUG-820 | high (**fixed**, server S1 adversarial fixes) | push / write access / merges | **Fixed:** a path the pusher may not write is accepted from a merge's other parent only where that parent's side changed it since a common ancestor of the two (`sync::common_ancestor`, walked only when needed); taking the version the first parent replaced is a write. **Anyone in the project reverts any file they can read but not write.** Attacker: a participant who reads a public folder (`src/  public devs`) but is not in `devs`. They push a merge of the tip and an older snapshot whose tree takes the older version of `src/lib.rs` (a security fix undone); "taken unchanged from another parent" let it through, and `.veilpolicy`'s non-access lines the same way. | `crates/veil-server/src/sync.rs` `check_changes`: `from_other` accepted any path equal to another parent's, and the pusher chooses the parents | `server_hub::adversarial::bug_820_a_merge_cannot_revert_a_file_the_pusher_may_not_write` (also checks that merging a dev's branch still lands) |
| BUG-821 | high (**fixed**, server S1 adversarial fixes) | permissions / names | **Fixed:** creating a group rebinds an accepted access line that names it to the new group, in the same transaction ("a group always wins", now also for groups created after the line). **A stranger who signed up under a group's name keeps that group's folder.** Attacker: anyone on Earth who registers likely group names (`ops`, `finance`). An admin writes `ops-area/  ops`, pushes (the push says "→ person ops"), then runs `vl group create ops` and `vl group add ops …`, the order a team often uses. The binding stayed with the person until the access lines changed again: the stranger read the folder and the group's members did not. Remaining (documented): between that push and the group's creation the person named has the folder, as the push listed. | `crates/veil-server/src/perm.rs` `bind_names` ran only when an admin's push changed the access lines; `api.rs` `create_group` left the stored bindings alone | `server_hub::adversarial::bug_821_a_group_created_after_its_access_line_takes_the_name` |
| BUG-822 | high (**fixed**, server S1 adversarial fixes) | secrets / key rings | **Fixed:** only an admin of the project may post the first ring of a scope; later changes still verify against the ring's own signed log. **Any participant starts a secret scope's key ring and is its only ring admin.** Attacker: a group member. For a scope the server has no ring for yet (`team` when an existing project turns on `vl upgrade --sync-secrets` after people joined; any later scope) they post their own ring. The admins' ring for that scope is then refused for ever ("unrelated history"), and a new member's device adopts the attacker's ring from its first pull and seals under the attacker's key: the admin's signature is no longer what grants the key. | `crates/veil-server/src/api.rs` `post_ring` accepted any participant's ring, and `merge_ring` stores an incoming ring when none exists | `server_hub::adversarial::bug_822_only_an_admin_starts_a_key_ring` |
| BUG-823 | medium (**fixed**, server S1 adversarial fixes) | push / projections | **Fixed:** the branch a push moves wins over the default branch when both look the same to the pusher. **A push to a branch whose only change since `main` is in a folder the pusher cannot see is refused at random** ("not a fast-forward", whatever they pull): its projected parent was resolved to `main`'s tip or the branch's, in `HashMap` order. | `sync.rs` `push`: `tip_projection` filled from a `HashMap` of all candidates | `server_hub::adversarial::bug_823_a_push_builds_on_the_tip_of_the_branch_it_moves` (8 attempts) |
| BUG-824 | medium (**fixed**, post-S1 fix round) | push / existence oracle | **Fixed:** every object a push introduces must carry the pusher's **upload receipt** (a server MAC over project ‖ person ‖ object id, returned by `POST …/objects`), unless it is the entry at the same path in one of the snapshot's parents (or a pushed directory the pusher sees there). Anything else gets the answer a missing object gets, stored or not, for files and for whole directories (`Graft::proving`, `sync::push`). Uploading a guess lands it either way, so the push says nothing. **A push confirms guesses of whole files it cannot see.** Attacker: a participant who may write somewhere. A tree they push may name an object id without uploading it: the push lands if the project stores that object (in any folder) and is refused "missing object" if not. A right guess of a short hidden file (a password file, a salary) gets a different answer from a wrong one. Folders under access lines are plain text, so their ids follow from their content; secrets are sealed and not exposed this way. Suggested fix: the server records who uploaded each object (or the push carries what it names that the pusher cannot read), and treats a named object that neither the pusher uploaded nor can read like a missing one. | `sync.rs` `check_changes` / `Graft::diff` read any object of the project by id | `server_hub::adversarial::bug_824_a_push_does_not_confirm_guesses_of_hidden_content` |
| BUG-825 | medium (**fixed**, server S1 adversarial fixes) | server / denial of service | **Fixed:** the TLS handshake and each request's head must arrive within 20 s (`IDLE_LIMIT`), and a failing `accept` backs off. **Anyone on Earth holds idle connections open for ever**: a TCP connection that never starts TLS kept a task and a file descriptor; enough of them exhaust the descriptors, and then `accept` failed in a busy loop. HTTP/2 connections idle between requests are not bounded yet. | `crates/veil-server/src/lib.rs` `serve_tls`: no timeout on `acceptor.accept`, no hyper timer; `Err(_) => continue` | `server_hub::adversarial::bug_825_a_silent_connection_is_closed` |
| BUG-826 | low (**fixed**, post-S1 fix round) | projections / ids | **Fixed:** a projection's predecessors are projected too (`sync::projected_predecessors`): a stored predecessor becomes the viewer's version of that change, or is dropped if the viewer's history has no version of it; one the server never stored is kept. This also covers a version served as is whose predecessor touched a hidden folder. **A projected snapshot keeps its real `predecessors`**, so a viewer learns the real id of an earlier version of a change that touched a folder they cannot see (an id, never its content or names: fetching it is checked like any other). Suggested fix: leave `predecessors` out where the server signs a projection. | `sync.rs` `projected` rewrites only `tree`, `parents` and `conflicts` | `server_hub::adversarial::bug_826_a_projection_names_no_hidden_predecessor` |
| BUG-827 | high (**fixed**, post-S1 fix round) | secrets / compromised server | **Fixed** (design in HUB.md §13.11): `vl` wraps a secret key only for devices vouched for outside the server: a person's first device confirmed by the admin by its fingerprint (`vl group add … --confirm 4F2A-…`), later devices signed by one of the person's own (`vl identity confirm`, signature context `hub-device`), or devices a verified key ring already records under the person. A device signing in under a taken name is pending (no session) until vouched for. Removal also revokes every ring member recorded under the person. **A compromised server obtains the project's secret key at the next admin's `vl group add`.** Attacker: whoever controls the server (outside the boundary for secrets, HUB.md §13.6). `GET /v1/people/{name}/devices` is the only source of a person's devices, and the admin's device wraps the key for every identity it returns (each is only checked to be self-consistent, never to be the person's). The server lists its own device under the person being added and receives the key; every `.env` it stores then opens. HUB.md §13.6's "a compromised server's group change gives no key" holds only for changes without an admin. Needs what S2 plans (§13.6 step 3): a person's later devices vouched for by their existing devices, and the first one confirmed outside the server. | `crates/vl/src/hub_cmd.rs` `sync_secret_keys` trusts `client.devices(person)` | `server_hub::adversarial::bug_827_a_server_cannot_slip_its_own_device_into_a_key_grant`, `adversarial::a_later_device_is_confirmed_by_its_person` |
| BUG-828 | medium (**fixed**, server S1 adversarial fixes) | secrets / removal | **Fixed:** a removal by someone who is no ring admin says the key was not rotated and asks an admin to run the removal too. **A manager's removal of someone from their last group silently leaves them the secret key** (only a ring admin's device rotates it; HUB.md said removal rotates). The folder closes at once; the key opens later secrets only if their ciphertext reaches the removed person. | `hub_cmd.rs` `sync_secret_keys` skips scopes this device is not a ring admin of, and said nothing | `server_hub::adversarial::bug_828_a_managers_removal_says_the_key_was_not_rotated` |
| BUG-829 | medium (**fixed**, server S1 adversarial fixes) | `vl access` / policy | **Fixed:** `vl access PATH WHO` edits the last line for PATH, the one that decides. **With two lines for one path (a hand edit, a merge), `vl access billing/ finance` rewrote the first and said "Updated"**, while the last (`billing/ public`) still decided: the folder stayed public. | `crates/vl/src/hub_cmd.rs` `access` replaced the first matching line; the server applies the last | `cli_security::policy_cli::access_edits_the_line_that_decides` |

What held up in this pass (tested, no finding): replayed, forged and cross-key logins; tokens after expiry and after device removal; anonymous and stranger access to private projects; every route crawled for whole markers by each viewer (the builder's `leaks` plus this pass's walks); writes into hidden folders through partial views and grafts; non-admin access-line edits on any branch; a pulled `.veilpolicy` that would expose `.env` (the member's device holds the weakening back and keeps sealing: `adversarial::a_pulled_policy_never_unseals_a_members_secret`); `kill -9` of the server mid-push (6 rounds, 2 killed mid-push: branches always name recorded snapshots, clones and re-pushes work); 300 concurrent requests on a one-connection pool (all answered, none hung).

## Adversarial pass: post-S1 fixes + perf round 1

Branches `t3/87cfa3a3` @ `ad37828` (post-S1 fix round) and `t3/4fc6d273` @ `8f315d0` (performance round 1), merged onto `integration` @ `b78e52d`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-833 | medium (**fixed**; **pre-existing**: `integration` @ `b78e52d`, a regression from the BUG-818 fix `713e1b3`) | checkout / symlinks | **Fixed:** the barrier opens a recorded directory with `O_DIRECTORY \| O_NOFOLLOW` and takes one replaced since by a link or a file (`ELOOP`, `ENOTDIR`) as removed: the replacement's directory is synced instead, and a link there is never followed. **Checking out `[a → a]` over `[a/a]` failed the whole checkout** with `ELOOP` (`Too many levels of symbolic links`), the proptest `checkouts_over_hostile_states_never_write_outside_or_through_a_link` with random seeds. Attacker: anyone whose tree a member checks out (a self-referencing link replacing a directory). Harm: the checkout cannot complete; a link to a FIFO would also have made the barrier's `open` block. | Checkout records the parent of each removal for the end-of-checkout barrier (`sync_parent_later`); when the removed directory is then replaced by a link, `barrier_sync_dir` opened the path, following the link. | `core_working_copy` `symlinks::a_directory_replaced_by_a_link_to_its_own_name_is_checked_out`; the seed is pinned in `symlinks.proptest-regressions` |
| BUG-834 | medium (**fixed**; BUG-824's class, routes its fix missed) | push / existence oracle | **Fixed:** every object a pushed entry names (its object, its `fallback`, a conflict's terms and their fallbacks: `sync::named_ids`) needs the pusher's upload receipt, unless the entry at that path in a parent names it. **A push lands a guess of a hidden file inside a conflict or as a secret's fallback, and `fetch` then serves it back.** Attacker: a participant who may write somewhere (dev writes `src/`). Controls: a conflict object at `src/c.txt` whose term names an object id, or a sealed `src/.env` whose `fallback` does. Receipts were checked for the entry's own object only, and `fetch` serves any id a conflict or fallback at a readable path names: a right guess of `billing/…` comes back, a wrong one is not found. | `sync::push` checked receipts for `Change::new.id` only; `fetch` accepts `e.fallback` and `Conflict::referenced_ids` | `server_hub` `adversarial::bug_834_a_conflict_names_no_hidden_object`, `adversarial::bug_834_a_fallback_names_no_hidden_object` |
| BUG-835 | medium (**fixed**) | secrets / compromised server | **Fixed:** `--confirm` takes one person (`vl group add finance alice --confirm …`). **A device confirmed in a `vl group add` of several people is recorded in the key ring under whichever person the server lists it for,** so removing its owner later does not rotate the key away from it. Attacker: a compromised server helping someone keep the key after their removal. Controls: the device lists: when an admin runs `vl group add finance one two --confirm <two's fingerprint>`, it lists two's device under one. Harm: after `vl group remove finance two` (the server hides two's device), two's device still holds the secret key. | `confirmed_devices` matches the `--confirm` fingerprints against every person of the command | `server_hub` `adversarial::bug_835_a_confirmed_device_is_recorded_under_its_persons_name` |
| BUG-836 | medium (**fixed**) | secrets / removal | **Fixed:** a removal that leaves someone in another group says so: `keys: fin is still in security: the secret key was not rotated away from them`. **Whether a removal rotates the key is decided by the server's group list, silently.** Attacker: a compromised server keeping a removed person the key. Controls: the group list `vl group remove` reads; it lists the person in another group, so no rotation happens and nothing is shown. (The admin can see and check it now; signed membership statements are S2's, `HUB.md` §13.6.) | `hub_cmd::group` `Remove` rotated only for people the server lists in no group, and said nothing about the others (BUG-828's class) | `server_hub` `adversarial::bug_836_a_removal_that_does_not_rotate_says_so` |

Tests: `server_hub` `startup::servers_starting_together_migrate_once`, `a_server_on_a_current_schema_runs_no_ddl` (a role without DDL rights), `requests_survive_a_schema_change` (failed on YugabyteDB before: sign-ins answered `busy`). **Servers starting together make requests fail with `busy` on YugabyteDB.** Each `veil-server` runs the schema migrations at start-up (`db::migrate`), and the DDL races with the other servers' (`40001`, `Restart read required`, `type schema_migrations already exists`). YugabyteDB aborts concurrent transactions while the catalog version changes, so `vl` requests to the servers already running fail after the 45 s deadline (`the database is busy`). It was seen as 7 of 36 failures in `verify-server.sh`'s YugabyteDB suite when merging `t3/4bf2a483` (PostgreSQL and both load steps were green), and once before in that branch's own run. In production this is a rolling restart of several servers. | Migrations run in every server process with no coordination, and requests outside `db::serializable` aren't retried across a schema change. Suggested fix: apply migrations once (a `veil-server migrate` step, or one holder of an advisory lock, with others waiting for the schema version); a server that finds the schema current runs no DDL; retry `40001` and catalog-version errors on every request path. | `verify-server.sh` YugabyteDB suite (intermittent) |

**Held up** (no finding): pending devices (no session, no signature accepted, no key; vouching by another person refused); vouches moved to another device or signed by another key; `--confirm` with a fingerprint the server chose (matches nothing the person reads); renamed people (ring roots are the names the admin typed); a forged X25519 key under a ring member's signing key (the binding is verified); upload receipts replayed across people or projects (the MAC binds both); the receipt key file (0600, created once); the lazily compiled scanner (a `OnceLock`: a scan waits for a compilation in progress, a failed one panics loudly, nothing catches it into "no secret"); the pack path under `kill -9` (60 of 60 kills of a 2,000-file `vl commit`: fsck clean, the retry records everything); packing writers beside `gc --prune-now` on a disk (96 of 96 under load); racy stat-cache records (stamps include ctime, a racy record never vouches).

**Hypothesis (seen once, not reproduced, not filed):** on YugabyteDB, one `verify-server.sh` run failed `adversarial::bug_824_a_push_does_not_confirm_guesses_of_hidden_content` (35 of 36 passed; the next run was green, 36 of 36): its server's request got `40001 schema version mismatch for table …` while other test servers, starting on the fresh database at the same moment, were still applying migrations (the log shows the `schema_migrations` race and a `40001` retry of migration 1). A migration whose losing copy re-runs DDL (`IF NOT EXISTS`) may bump YugabyteDB's catalog version under a server already serving, and a query outside `db::serializable` is not retried. In production this would be a rolling start with a new migration; a fix would retry `40001` on every query, or start serving only once `schema_migrations` holds every version.

**Out of scope (trusted):** an admin who confirms a fingerprint without comparing it; a person who vouches for a device that is not theirs.

**Residual (design, not filed):** a device fingerprint is 80 bits: a server that wants its device to match one person's needs a second preimage, about 2^80 key generations, between the person's sign-in and the admin's check.

## Confinement verification review

Independent verification of `vl ws exec` confinement (`t3/267b9531` @ `c2fe202`, merged onto `integration` @ `bfa691a`), against `docs/design/scale/9-confinement.md`. The attacker is the confined command (an agent, a test suite, a dependency's build script): outside the trust boundary for files (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, "Threat model"). Owner decisions, not findings: the environment passes through, the network is on by default, the allow-list is read-only. Reproductions: `crates/vl/tests/cli_workspaces/confine_cli.rs`, after "Confinement verification review".

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-848 | high (**fixed**, confinement review fixes) | confinement / allow-list | **Fixed:** the Veil home, the real project and cargo's credentials are hidden under every name an allowed path gives them (`base_args` maps each canonical target through each allowed bind), cargo's credentials in `$CARGO_HOME` too, and an allowed path inside the Veil home or the project is refused. **An allowed link to a folder that holds the Veil home or the project showed the command the person's identity with its secret keys, the real `.veil` (the store, other workspaces' sandboxes) and the real working copy**; an allowed link to `~/.cargo`, or an allowed `$CARGO_HOME`, showed the crates.io token. Attacker: the confined command. Controls: what it reads. Harm: personal private keys and every workspace's files reach a command that the design says cannot read them, for an ordinary setup (`--allow ~/src` where `~/src` links to a data disk). | the masks were applied only at each target's own path, while an allowed link binds the target's canonical folder under the link's name | `an_allowed_link_to_a_folder_holding_keys_or_the_project_still_hides_them` |
| BUG-849 | medium (**fixed**, confinement review fixes) | confinement / limits | **Fixed:** `systemd-run` gets `--expand-environment=no` where it knows it (systemd 254 and later; probed). **With a limit that uses a systemd scope, the command was rewritten:** `systemd-run` expands `$VAR`, `${VAR}` and `$$` in everything after `--` (the `bwrap` arguments and the command), so `sh -c 'echo $$ > f'` wrote `$`, and a project path with a `$` in it was bound under another name. | systemd 254 made expansion the default for `--scope` | `a_command_with_dollar_signs_runs_as_given_under_a_systemd_scope` |
| BUG-850 | medium (**fixed**, confinement review fixes) | confinement / limits | **Fixed:** every `systemd-run` and `systemctl` call has a 5-second deadline (`output_within`); a user manager that does not answer means the polling fallback before the run, and never delays recording after it. **A slow or hung systemd user manager hung `vl ws exec`:** with a limit, before anything ran (the probe), and after a scoped run that was killed (`systemctl show`, `reset-failed`), before the run was recorded. | the probe and the post-run queries waited without a limit | `a_slow_systemd_user_manager_does_not_hang_vl`, `a_hung_systemctl_after_a_scoped_run_does_not_keep_vl_from_recording` |
| BUG-851 | medium (**fixed**, confinement review fixes) | confinement / clean-up | **Fixed:** `vl` arms `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` (SIGKILL) in the child before it execs `systemd-run` or `bwrap` (it survives both execs) and refuses to start if `vl` is already gone. **`kill -9` of `vl` while `systemd-run` or `bwrap` was starting left the command running**, orphaned, in the sandbox, after the reaper had taken the injected files out and without the sandbox's lock (the next run could start beside it). | `bwrap`'s `--die-with-parent` only holds once `bwrap` has armed it | `killing_vl_while_bwrap_or_systemd_run_starts_leaves_nothing_running` |
| BUG-852 | medium (**fixed**, small fixes 1) | confinement / clean-up | **Fixed:** what a dead `vl` left of a confined run is stopped: the processes still running a `bwrap` (or `systemd-run`) that binds the sandbox, found by their command line in `/proc` and killed through a pidfd (killing the sandbox's init ends its pid namespace), and the `veil-exec-<pid>-*` scopes of `vl` processes that are gone (killed, stopped, and their failed state cleared). The reaper does it as soon as `vl` dies; the next `vl ws exec` in the workspace, `vl ws rm`, and the sweep of throwaway sandboxes do it for a run with no reaper (or whose reaper died too), always under the sandbox's lock or for a dead owner's throwaway directory, so no live run is touched. Under load (16 busy CPUs, 8 copies at once), the reproduction passed 32/32 and failed 23/24 with the stopping turned off. **`kill -9` of `vl` in the moment between `bwrap` creating the sandbox's first process and that process arming its own parent-death signal still leaves the command running** (seen for kills 50–100 ms after the start, also in a plain `verify-fast.sh` run; under load, 4 of 416 kills with 8 copies of the test at once; with 8 copies of a 64-kill loop, every loop hit it at least once, 5 leaving the command running and the others an empty or failed scope), and `systemd-run` killed while systemd starts its scope can leave the empty scope active, or failed (the scope is not `--collect`ed, so that `vl` can read why it failed; the design's sketch said it was). Smallest fix: the next run of the workspace stops what an earlier, dead `vl` left (its `veil-exec-<pid>-*` scope, or the processes whose root is the sandbox), or `bwrap` checks its parent after arming the signal (upstream). | inside `bwrap`'s start-up, and systemd missing the empty cgroup | `killing_vl_at_any_moment_leaves_nothing_and_the_next_run_recovers`, `the_next_run_and_ws_rm_stop_what_a_dead_run_left_running` |
| BUG-853 | medium (**fixed**, confinement review fixes) | confinement / doctor | **Fixed:** `vl doctor` looks for `bwrap`, `systemd-run` and `systemctl` outside the project, as `vl ws exec` does. **`vl doctor` ran a `bwrap` or `systemd-run` from the project** when `PATH` names a folder of it (a direnv `PATH_add bin`). Attacker: whoever adds `bin/bwrap` to the repository (a hostile pull). Harm: their program runs as the person. | `confine::doctor` searched `PATH` without the project root | `doctor_never_runs_a_bwrap_from_inside_the_project` |
| BUG-854 | low (**fixed**, confinement review fixes) | confinement / allow-list | **Fixed:** without a usable `HOME` there is no default allow-list. **With `HOME` unset, relative or `/`, the default allow-list was read from `/tmp/home`**, which any user of the machine can create: another OS user's `/tmp/home/.claude` (an agent's settings and hooks) reached the confined agent. | the stand-in home was used for the defaults too | `confine::tests::without_a_home_there_is_no_default_allow_list` |
| BUG-855 | low (**fixed**, small fixes 1) | `vl serve` / tests | **Fixed (the test's timing; the cap is right):** `Server::start` learns that the server listens by connecting, and that probe is a client too. The server may accept it only after the test's connections have started arriving, and it holds a slot until the server's thread for it has seen it leave, so under load the 32nd connection was refused. `connections_are_capped` now waits for the server's `Serving` line instead (`Server::start_unprobed`). Under load (32 busy CPUs, 24 copies at once): 50 of 96 runs failed before; 144/144 passed after, and 144/144 with no probe and nothing else changed. **`cli_sync::serve_cli::connections_are_capped` fails intermittently in the full parallel suite:** one of the first 32 connections is refused. It has been seen in three separate full runs (perf round 1, the BUG-818 fix, the confinement merge). It passes in isolation (150/150) and under targeted load (48/48), and none of those changes touched `vl serve`. | The test harness's own readiness probe connection, accepted late and released late, held one of the 32 slots. | `cli_sync::serve_cli::connections_are_capped` |

What held up (tested, no finding): writes through `..`, absolute paths, absolute and relative symlinks, `/proc/self/root`, `/proc/1/root`, `/proc/self/cwd`, renames and hard links across the boundary, `mknod` and `mkfifo` into an allowed folder, and the allow-list itself (outside files hash the same before and after); links, FIFOs and sockets the command plants in its sandbox (replacing an injected file or its folder) never make `vl` read, write or delete outside it, on the next sync, injection, take-out or sparse clean-up, nor hang it; keys and other home files, the Veil identity, the real `.veil` and other workspaces' sandboxes stay unreadable; the command inherits no descriptor of `vl`; project paths with spaces, newlines, leading dashes and `$`; hostile `--allow` values, `HOME` and configuration; a `bwrap` inside the project; 6 and 2 workspaces run at once stay separate (96 of 96 runs of each under load, 12 copies at a time); signals (32 of 32 under load); limits under both mechanisms.

**Out of scope (trusted):** an explicit `--allow` of a folder that holds the home (it shows `~/.ssh`; the person's deliberate command), or of a folder that holds `$TMPDIR` (other `--ephemeral` runs' sandboxes); a hostile `PATH` that names a hostile `bwrap` outside the project.

## Server benchmarks (2026-11-06)

Found by the 1 GB profile through the server (`scripts/bench-server.sh 1g`, `integration` @ `bfa691a`; `docs/design/scale/BASELINE.md`, "Through the Veil server"). The reproductions need the server, PostgreSQL and MinIO, so they are the benchmark's cases for now; the stream that fixes each adds an ignored-then-passing test to `server_hub` (the container suite).

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-857 | medium (**fixed**, server bench fixes; **pre-existing**: S1) | client / push to the server | **Fixed:** a push sends what each new snapshot introduces at each path, walking a tree once for each set of parent trees it is compared with (`hub::Introduced`); it sends exactly what check 7 asks a receipt for. The 1 GB initial push now succeeds in one push (`BASELINE.md`, "After the server bench fixes"). **A push of a history of more than a few snapshots is refused:** `missing object 7a8b7c15 (server: bad_request)`, after uploading everything (the initial push of the 1 GB profile: 121 s, 2.4 GB uploaded; of the `tiny` profile, 200 snapshots, the same). Pushes of a few snapshots at a time succeed. This blocks moving a repository with history onto the server (`HUB.md` §5.7, §13.8). Nothing is lost: the server refuses the whole push. | `hub.rs` `collect_tree` skips an entry equal to the same path's entry in one of the snapshot's parents, and stops at any tree already in `seen`, whatever parents that tree was walked against. A tree first walked under a later snapshot (against a parent that already had a file) is not walked again under the snapshot that introduced the file, so the file is never sent; the server requires every object a snapshot introduces at a path to carry the pusher's receipt (check 7, BUG-824). Suggested fix: keep `seen` for what is sent, not for where the walk stops (each snapshot's walk is bounded by the parent comparison already), or walk each changed subtree once per parent context. | `server_hub` `sync::bug_857_a_push_of_a_history_that_reuses_a_tree_is_accepted`, `sync::random_histories_pushed_in_one_push_are_accepted`; `vl` `hub::tests::a_push_sends_exactly_what_the_server_lacks` (proptest: sent = what the server lacks, over random histories); `scripts/bench-server.sh tiny` and `1g` |
| BUG-858 | medium (**fixed**, server bench fixes; **pre-existing**: S1) | client / push memory | **Fixed:** the push uploads each object as the walk finds it, about 8 MiB per request (`hub::Uploads`). **`vl push` to the server holds every new object in memory:** the initial push of the 1 GB profile peaked at **2,410 MiB**; one push of its import (11 snapshots, 20,883 files) at 867 MiB. The memory gate is 512 MiB per command. | `hub.rs` `push` collects the raw bytes of every object it introduces (`objects: Vec<(ObjectId, Vec<u8>)>`) before uploading them in 8 MiB frames. Suggested fix: upload each 8 MiB batch as the walk fills it (receipts are per object, so nothing else changes). | `scripts/bench-server.sh 1g` (`push, initial (all tags)`) |
| BUG-859 | medium (**fixed**, server bench fixes; **pre-existing**: S1) | client / clone and pull memory | **Fixed:** a level is fetched in parts of at most 2,500 objects and about 8 MiB (by the sizes tree entries carry), at most 8 in flight, and each part's objects are written as it arrives (`Client::fetch_each`). **`vl clone` from the server peaks at 979 MiB** on the 1 GB profile (792 MiB with `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`), over the 512 MiB gate. Path clones measured 503 MiB before path remotes went away. Pull of one snapshot, and a clone of one directory, stay under 110 MiB. | `pull` fetches every new snapshot's trees and files a level at a time; a level is up to 20,000 objects (many versions of many files), fetched by `Client::fetch_all` as 8 parts whose response bodies are all kept until the last arrives, then copied object by object (`raw.to_vec()`) before any is written; checkout's staging threads then add theirs on top. RSS climbs level by level to ~600 MiB during the fetch, then to 974 MiB during checkout. Suggested fix: hand each part's objects to `Incoming` as it arrives, without copying, and size a level's requests by bytes (tree entries carry sizes), not by count. | `scripts/bench-server.sh 1g` (`clone, full`) |
| BUG-860 | medium (**fixed**, server bench fixes; **pre-existing**: S1) | server / memory | **Fixed:** a fetch checks its wants a snapshot at a time (dropping that snapshot's projected trees), then streams its answer with at most 64 objects or about 8 MiB read ahead; uploaded objects are copied out of the request (a slice kept the whole 8 MiB body alive in the object cache); decoded trees are weighed by the memory they hold. The projection is unchanged (every `server_hub` leak and adversarial test passes). **The server's memory grows to several GB serving one project:** a fresh server serving one full clone of the 1 GB profile peaked at **2.5 GB** (1.95 GB with `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`), growing steadily through the clone; it reached 3.1 GB over the benchmark and kept it; a push of the whole history peaked at 1.5 GB. Its caches are bounded at 512 MiB by weight. Thousands of agents cloning at once would multiply the per-request part. | `sync.rs` `fetch` builds each response's whole body in memory (8 concurrent requests per level, up to 2,500 objects each), and keeps the projected root and directory trees (`roots`, `Dirs`: decoded `Arc<Tree>`s) of every snapshot its wants name (with revision 1, most of the history in one request), outside the bounded tree cache; decoded trees are weighed at twice their encoded size, which is likely below their real size. The push path was not profiled. Suggested fix: stream a response's frames; drop a snapshot's directory trees once its wants are served; weigh decoded trees by their real size. | `scripts/bench-server.sh 1g` (server RSS column) |
| BUG-861 | low (**fixed**, server bench fixes; **pre-existing**: S1) | server / S3 | **Fixed:** every S3 request (all idempotent) is tried again for up to 10 s (jittered waits doubling from 25 ms to 1 s; a request's deadline is 45 s) when its connection closes or resets, before or during the answer, or the store answers 5xx; idle connections are dropped after 15 s. A first try with 6 tries in about 1.5 s was not enough: under the load profile's 100 projects the local MinIO stayed unreachable for longer. **A reset S3 connection fails the request with HTTP 500:** under the load profile with MinIO, 1,239 uploads at 100 projects answered `HTTP 500 internal error` (`scripts/bench-server.sh load`, first run); a second run's server log shows the cause, five S3 requests failing with `connection closed before message completed` and `Connection reset by peer`. S3 services close idle keep-alive connections (AWS after about 20 s), so production sees the same. | `store.rs` `S3Store` sends each request once on a pooled `reqwest` connection (`pool_max_idle_per_host(64)`), with no retry; a request on a connection the store has closed fails, and the error becomes a 500. Suggested fix: retry idempotent S3 requests (GET, HEAD, PUT of a content-addressed key) on connection errors, with backoff, and drop idle connections before the store does (`pool_idle_timeout`). | `server_hub` `sync::bug_861_a_closed_object_store_connection_is_tried_again` (a proxy in front of MinIO drops connections without answering); `scripts/bench-server.sh load` |
| BUG-864 | medium (**fixed**, mem864; found by the server bench fixes) | server / memory | **Fixed:** `veil-server`'s global allocator is jemalloc (`tikv-jemallocator` 0.7.0), with two arenas, background purging and a 1 s decay (`src/main.rs`). Of glibc, glibc capped at 1 or 2 arenas, mimalloc and jemalloc, it kept the least on the 1 GB profile, with no throughput loss under `bench-server.sh load`: the push peaks at 984 MiB (was 2,367), the full clone at 1,579 MiB (was 2,877), and the server keeps 948 MiB at the end of the run (was 2,880). `veil-bench run` gates the server's peak under 1 GB; the clone's remaining excess is BUG-1000 (`BASELINE.md`, "The server's allocator"). **The server's resident memory is two to three times what it holds:** after the server bench fixes its data is bounded (two 256 MiB caches, a request's tables), yet a push of the 1 GB history leaves it at 1.5–2.6 GB (`BASELINE.md`, "After the server bench fixes"). Measured by hand on a fresh server, the same push peaks at 0.84 GB with `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1` and 1.1 GB with `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`; pinning glibc's mmap threshold changes nothing. Thousands of agents on one server would multiply it by its threads. | glibc gives each thread its own arena (up to 8 per core) and never returns an arena's memory below its high-water mark: the server runs 32 runtime workers and up to 512 blocking threads (each snapshot of a push is checked on one; `FsStore` writes on them), 34–146 threads in these runs, and `/proc/PID/smaps` shows the memory in their 64 MiB arena heaps. Suggested fix (a dependency or deployment choice for the owner): an allocator with bounded per-thread caches (jemalloc or mimalloc as the global allocator), or a cap on arenas (`mallopt(M_ARENA_MAX)` at start, or `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` in the deployment), measured against the load profile. | `scripts/bench-server.sh 1g` (server RSS column) |
| BUG-865 | low (**fixed**, S28; **pre-existing**: S1; found by the server bench fixes) | server / push speed | **Fixed** by S28: a push checks up to 8 new snapshots at once, 64 ahead at a time, on the guess that each new parent is completed to itself (exactly the inputs of checking one at a time when the guess is right; a wrong guess is checked again in order; results and the first error taken in order). The 1 GB profile's initial push: 354 s → **138 s** end to end (the server's part 57 s: the walk 8 s, the checks 47 s); on `bench-server.sh 1g` after S28 cycle 2, 252.7 s on `integration` @ `6fa552c4` → **99.3 s**, same client, MinIO, machine loaded (`HUB.md` §13.20, "Measured"). **An initial push of a long history takes minutes on the server:** the 1 GB profile's 10,022 snapshots and 2.4 GB take 337 s to push in one push (before the fixes, the refused upload and the 54 fast-forward steps of the workaround took 316 s together). Moving a repository with history onto the server is slow, never wrong. | `sync::push` completes and checks the new snapshots strictly one after another, each in its own blocking task: its graft and change checks read every changed tree and the parents' entries at each changed path (`entry_at` from the root, per path and parent), and the object store is S3. Suggested fix: check independent snapshots in parallel (a snapshot needs only its parents' real trees), and reuse the parents' decoded paths across a snapshot's changes. | `scripts/bench-server.sh 1g` (`push, initial (all tags)`) |

A commit that timed out may have committed, so `db::transaction` never runs `f` again after one (it answers 500, as before) and `retry_requests` already stops once a commit was tried. The stall itself cannot be caused on demand; `error::tests::bug_890_a_yugabytedb_rpc_timeout_is_retryable` checks the classification. **A YugabyteDB RPC timeout fails the request with HTTP 500:** in one run of the `server_hub` suite on a freshly started YugabyteDB (base `1f9f880`, 2026-11-07), 27 tests failed on `internal error`; the server's log shows `database error [XX000]: … Rpc timeout, passed: 15.0s, timeout: 15.000s`. With a single glibc arena the clone still adds 857 MiB (928 → 1,785), so this is the fetch path's memory, not arenas (`BASELINE.md`, "The server's allocator"). | Not profiled yet. ## Performance round 3 (2026-11-07)

Found while changing the order of a transaction's durable writes (`docs/design/scale/OPENSCION.md`, round 3), and by its verification. All three are gaps in the tests, not in the product.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-905 | medium (**fixed**, performance round 3; **pre-existing**: the crash harness since format 6) | tests / crash ordering | **Fixed:** `FaultyBackend` keeps the unsynced renames of every other directory at a power loss (by first appearance), keeps the renames into one directory together, and drops staged names. **The crash harness could not catch a name made durable before what it depends on.** At a simulated power loss it undid every unsynced rename together, as if they all reached the disk or none did; a real disk may keep a rename into one directory and not into another. | BUG-970 | low (**fixed**, fix1; **pre-existing**: `integration` @ `0fbe207`) | tests / flaky | **Fixed, for the class (BUG-1007, 1010, 1085 and `bug_1053` too):** a claim about work is counted, not timed. In `core_durability`, "taken over at once" is a lock acquisition on a simulated clock that only its own back-off moves (`acquire_counting_wait`: waited zero), the memory peak is measured in a process of the test's own (`in_own_process`), a writer that must not wait for a slow snapshot commits while the scan is held until it has (no bound), and gc's "did not wait" is the reason it gives (refused at once, not "kept running for 65 s"). Every `elapsed() <` bound in the binary is gone; what is left times only a hang guard or waits that load can only lengthen (`>=`). **Held up** (no finding; by the builder's tests, this pass's tests, or by reading the code), by attack surface:
- **Invites (8):** a join under a key that is not the invite's, under a key the server chose, or moved onto another device (the replay and the server refuse); a second use, in the ring and on the server; use after expiry (the share's signed time against the admin-signed `expires_at`); a join for another person, or by a device signed in as another person; a server-substituted invite key (the ring's admin-signed `invite` names the real one); the link's secret in the server's tables, files, audit log, `vl` errors and the op log (`vl join` runs outside a repository); a name squatted before the invitee joins (refused join, noticed: denial of service only, as any first-come name).
- **Proofs (7):** a vouch by another person's device, by a revoked device, or moved onto another device; a share to a device or signing key the ring ever held; cross-ring and cross-project replay of a change (the signature covers the scope and the previous hash); `hub-invite` and `hub-device` signatures used for each other or for `hub-login` (separate contexts and messages); the server's and the devices' replays agree (same `verify`, the share's own signed time).
- **Per-rule keys (6):** `billing/` cannot open `infra/.env` or a nested rule's secret; last-match ordering and nested lines (the device's `rule_scope` and the server's `deciding` are the same function); a line edited to name another group rotates the key away from the old one; a line made `public` (names nobody) moves new secrets to `team`; a hand-written access line with no ring keeps its secret on the device, with a warning; non-admins cannot write `.veilpolicy` (the server's access check on the root).
- **Background sharing (5):** hostile listings (forged joins and vouches, re-listed removed devices) share nothing the replay refuses; shares racing a removal (the builder's concurrency test, under load: 8 copies on PostgreSQL, 3 on YugabyteDB); `VEIL_KEY_SHARE=0`; the detached child (no stdin, its own process group, a 0600 log, `VEIL_KEY_SHARE=0` in its environment); a pass never shares to a device without a proof.
- **Device removal (3):** a device hidden by the server is found among the rings' members; a removed device re-listed with its old vouch is not shared to again; a member's `revoke_own` reaches only their own devices.
- **Formats (3):** rings that say format 3 but hold shares, format 5, or malformed JSON, are refused or dropped; a format-6 clone keeps its own ring and warns.

**Accepted by design** (`docs/HUB.md` §13.12, rows 15–16; not filed): a server that misreports group members or admins can make an admin's `vl access` or `vl group add` grant a *real teammate* a rule's key (never its own device); a manager's removal does not rotate, and a member's background pass may still share to a person a manager removed before anyone shared to them.

**Out of scope (trusted):** a member who shares their key to a device that is not the person's (they hold the key); a person who vouches for a device that is not theirs; an admin who confirms a fingerprint without comparing it.

**Residual (not filed, no practical test):** the invite link is a command-line argument of `vl join`, which other OS users of the same machine can read (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`) while it runs. For a name nobody has yet, one who reads it and registers the name before `vl join`'s own sign-in (a window of milliseconds) joins in the invitee's place; the invitee's join then fails ("a name somebody has"), so it is noticed. **Done** (secrets S2 owner fixes): `vl join -` reads the link on standard input, and `vl invite` and the guide say to use it (`server_hub` `projects::an_invite_names_the_projects_fingerprint`).

**Nits** (not filed; **both fixed** in secrets S2 owner fixes): `Keychain::check_with_keys` checks that a `Revoke` or `Rotate` generation unlocks the previous one, but not a `RevokeOwn`'s (`keychain.rs`, the one match the new kind was not added to; now checked, `core_security` `ring_shares::a_revoke_own_rotation_must_unlock_the_previous_generation`); unbounded pending devices (no cap per person since S2) let anyone grow the `devices` table, which only a sign-in under the same name prunes (now at most 32 per person, the oldest pushed out, never one whose fingerprint the person looked for in the last hour: `server_hub` `secrets2::pending_devices_made_by_others_never_hide_the_real_one`, with floods in parallel).

**Not filed (no failure shown):** `vl status --json` and `vl ls --json` on a change k first parents above an embargoed merge take O(k²) (`api::EmbargoTiers` → `remote::embargo_base` asks `Withheld::of_snapshot` once per first parent walked, each a graph walk down to the merge's first parent): 9 ms at k = 51, 24 ms at 201, 334 ms at 801 (release). `82429c6` also queried once per step (traced, not measured). **Not filed (seen under load, no failure tied to this diff):** `scripts/verify-server.sh` failed its YugabyteDB step in both runs, each time a different test and with a contention error, while the machine's load average was about 50: `startup::a_server_on_a_current_schema_runs_no_ddl` (`40001 Restart read required` in its own setup DDL, `CREATE ROLE`/`GRANT`), then `projects::an_admin_bars_a_device_from_their_project_only` (`vl identity confirm`: "the database is busy … (server: busy)"). The other steps (unit, clippy, PostgreSQL, both load runs) passed. Neither route is changed by `82429c6..7b3456a`. To file if it recurs on a quiet machine (the class of BUG-890).

**Out of scope (trusted):** none new. Withdrawal by `vl undo` of the merge, or abandoning it bare, stays as cycle 3 recorded it.
## Adversarial pass: S12 derived data

Security review (layer 3, tier A) of milestone S12 (`t3/be6d12dc` @ `c2e2c28` on `integration` @ `d9f221b`): `crates/veil-server/src/derive/`, `migrations/0004_derived.sql`, the hook in `sync::push`. All are introduced by S12. Reproductions are in `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/derived.rs` (module `s12_adversarial`; the container suite, `scripts/verify-server.sh`). Today only the hook reaches the deriver: `derive::landed` after every push, then `memo_tips`. No route serves `view::Reader` yet (S13), so BUG-869 and BUG-871 are latent until S13 serves it.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-866 | medium (**fixed**, S12 fixes) | server / derived graph | **One far-future timestamp stops, or corrupts, the project's derived history:** a member with write access to one folder pushes a snapshot with `timestamp = i64::MAX` (the push accepts it), then any snapshot on top. In debug builds every derive run panics (`attempt to add with overflow`), so no branch of the project is derived again. Release builds wrap instead: generations no longer decrease along parent edges, and `is_ancestor`, `merge_bases` and the paint-down give wrong answers. This contradicts §10's "a hostile timestamp only lengthens a walk". | `derive/graph.rs:70` `p.generation + 1` on an unbounded client timestamp. Push checks no timestamp. Suggested fix: clamp the timestamp used for the generation (e.g. to `i64::MAX / 2`) and add with `saturating_add`, so the generation stays strictly decreasing. **Fixed:** `GraphRow::compute` clamps the timestamp it takes to `MAX_STAMP` (`i64::MAX / 4`) and adds with `saturating_add` (depth too), so generations strictly decrease along every edge whatever a pusher chose. No other arithmetic in `derive/` takes a client value unbounded (similarity counts are capped by the 1 MiB file limit; depths and row numbers are counts). | `bug_866_a_far_future_timestamp_breaks_the_commit_graph` (through `Craft::push_edited`) |
| BUG-867 | medium (**fixed**, S12 fixes) | server / derive memory | **One push can drive the server out of memory:** a batch holds every queued `file_history` row, list row, changed-paths object and per-path map entry of up to 512 snapshots before writing anything. A member alternating one folder between two trees uploads a few hundred bytes per snapshot, yet each snapshot changes tens of thousands of paths. Memory rose **432 MiB / 1,156 MiB / 2,247 MiB** over 16 / 48 / 96 snapshots of 50,000 paths each, about 22 MiB per snapshot. A full batch of 100,000-path changes would need about 23 GiB, and the whole server process (every project) goes down with it. | `derive/mod.rs:536` flushes by snapshot count only (`FLUSH_EVERY`). `Writes` and `Batch::history` grow with the paths each snapshot changed. Suggested fix: also flush when the queued rows or object bytes pass a bound (e.g. 100,000 rows or 64 MiB). **Fixed:** a batch is written every 512 snapshots, 100,000 queued `file_history`/`rule_history` rows or 64 MiB of queued objects, whichever comes first (`Writes::full`), so its memory is bounded whatever the snapshots changed; one snapshot's own rows are queued whole, as its change list is in memory anyway. | `bug_867_a_derive_batch_holds_unbounded_memory` (`VEIL_BUG867_SNAPSHOTS`, `VEIL_BUG867_FILES`) |
| BUG-868 | medium (**fixed**, S12 fixes) | server / derive work | **`many` snapshots slow every later landing, everyone's:** each snapshot of more than 100,000 changed paths is kept in `Batch::many`. For every path of every later change, and per parent, each `many` snapshot on the line is checked against the trees (`at_depth` plus two `entry_at`). They cost a member next to nothing to make (one folder alternating between two trees; up to 100,000 snapshots per push). After 30 of them, an unrelated landing of 5,000 files took **58 s instead of 0.48 s** (the same history with the folder just under the cap). Work grows as paths × `many` snapshots: row 10's "within 2× linear" does not hold. | `derive/mod.rs:639`–`656` (`last_changes`) scans all of `self.many` per (path, parent); `changed_path` (`:734`) reads two trees each time. `Batch::new` also loads every `*` row on each run. Suggested fix: write `file_history` rows for `many` snapshots too (only the object is capped), and drop the per-path tree check. **Fixed:** every changed path of a `many` snapshot gets its `file_history` row like any other change's (only the object is capped), so `last_changes` finds it by path; the `many` list, its per-path tree checks and the `*` rows are gone. | `bug_868_many_snapshots_slow_every_later_landing` (`VEIL_BUG868_MANY`) |
| BUG-869 | medium (latent until S13 serves `Reader`, **fixed**, S12 fixes) | server / derived reads | **`Reader::visible` overflows the stack on a chain of merges, aborting the process:** `visible` of a merge calls `rep` of its parents, which calls `visible` of the next merge down: one frame pair per merge. A member pushes 20,000 merges that each take an old snapshot in again; 100,000 are allowed per push. The first `visible(tip)` then dies with `thread 'tokio-rt-worker' has overflowed its stack` / `fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting`. That takes down the whole server, not one request. Any S13 log, `rep` or `merge_bases` on such a branch would trigger it, for any viewer. | `derive/view.rs:94`–`128`: `visible` and `rep` recurse into each other, one level per merge on the first-parent line, with the memo filled only on the way back. Suggested fix: compute visibility iteratively (an explicit stack, children after parents) and memoise as it goes. **Fixed:** `Reader::visible` and `rep` are iterative: a snapshot waiting on an older one's visibility goes on an explicit stack, and representatives are memoised as they are walked. The rest of `derive/` has no recursion over history (`changes::walk` recurses over one tree's depth, capped at 1,024). | `bug_869_a_chain_of_merges_overflows_the_readers_stack` (runs the reader in a child process; `VEIL_BUG869_MERGES`) |
| BUG-870 | medium (**fixed**, S12 fixes) | server / derive work | **Every landing does work in proportion to the project's branch count:** each run upserts one `derive_progress` row per branch, and `memo_tips` projects every branch tip for every view key, whether or not the branch moved. Any participant may create branches with no limit (one push can create thousands, all naming one snapshot). With 3,001 branches, one landing took **2.76 s instead of 15 ms** (two view keys). It costs thousands of statements per view key on every push by anyone, on the database every project shares. | `derive/mod.rs:375`–`391` (every branch, every run) and `:872` (`memo_tips`: every branch × every view key). Suggested fix: write progress only for tips that changed, and memoise only the branches the landing moved (`push` knows them: `moved`). **Fixed:** `derive::landed` takes the branches the push moved (`moved`), and the run (`Scope::Branches`), its `derive_progress` rows (one statement) and `memo_tips` touch only those; `Scope::All` is a full catch-up. | `bug_870_branches_multiply_the_work_of_every_landing` (`VEIL_BUG870_BRANCHES`) |
| BUG-871 | low (latent until S13 serves `Reader`; needs a crafted push from someone who may write the folder, **fixed**, S12 fixes) | server / derived visibility | **A tree change with no leaf change is shown to every viewer:** a change that only adds an empty folder in `fin/` (or changes only a hidden directory entry's metadata) is derived as `none`. `Reader::visible` shows a one-parent `none` change to everyone; `sync::projected` hides it from whoever cannot read `fin/`, where it collapses into its parent. The reader then disagrees with the projection, so S13 would list a change of `fin/` only, with its description and author, to anyone on Earth. `vl` never writes empty folders; a finance member's crafted push does (`Graft` accepts the empty tree). This falsifies §10's equivalence claim, which `projection_equivalence` misses because its trees never hold empty folders. | `derive/mod.rs:577` sets `none` whenever no leaf changed, even when the tree did; `derive/view.rs:106` treats `none` as visible to all. Suggested fix: `none` only when the tree equals the first parent's. Otherwise list the change under the lines deciding the directories whose entries changed (or treat it as unlisted). **Fixed:** `none` is only a change whose tree is its first parent's. `changes::diff` also reports the folders that changed with no leaf changing below them (deepest only; `Changed::dirs`), and they are listed under the lines deciding them (`Lines::dir_key`, as `Projector` shows them). `projection_equivalence`'s generator now makes empty folders in every folder. | `bug_871_a_change_of_an_empty_hidden_folder_is_visible_to_all` |

### S12 cycle 2

Security review (layer 3, tier A, cycle 2) of the S12 fixes (`git diff 30d828e 614576f`, `t3/be6d12dc` @ `614576f`) merged onto `integration` @ `0fbe207`. All three findings are introduced by the fixes. Reproductions: `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/derived.rs`, module `s12_adversarial` (`bug_980`–`bug_982`, ignored).

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-980 | medium (latent until S13 serves `Reader`; introduced by BUG-869's fix; **fixed**, S12 cycle 2) | server / derived reads | **The iterative `Reader` is quadratic over a run of changes the viewer cannot see:** a merge on top of `k` one-parent changes of `fin/` only (ordinary work by finance; no crafted push needed) costs anyone outside finance `k²/2` steps for the first `visible`, `rep` or `merge_bases` of it, where the recursive reader took `k`. Measured (one `visible` of the merge, anyone on Earth): 2,000 hidden changes **47 s**, 8,000 **603 s** on PostgreSQL; 500 **4.6 s**, 2,000 **52 s** on YugabyteDB (linear would be 4× per 4× changes; it is 11–13×). At 20,000 that is about an hour. Every S13 log of such a branch for anyone on Earth pays it, on a blocking thread. | `derive/view.rs:178` `known_rep` walks the first-parent line down to the first snapshot whose visibility is undecided, returns `Err(that)` and drops `walked` (memoising only on success); `visible` (`:111`) then decides that one snapshot and calls `step` on the merge again, which walks the whole run again from its top. `rep` (`:203`) loops the same way. Suggested fix: decide one-parent snapshots inline as `known_rep` reaches them (they need nothing else), so that it only stops at an undecided merge, and memoise the walked prefix when it stops. **Fixed:** `known_rep` decides one-parent snapshots as it reaches them (listed, withheld, or an equal tree: `Reader::simple`), stops only at a merge not decided yet, and leaves every snapshot it walked pointing at where the walk ended, so no snapshot is walked twice. Measured with `Reader::work` (steps: snapshots walked and list lookups): 4,004 steps for 2,000 hidden changes, 16,004 for 8,000 (553 ms and 1.10 s on PostgreSQL, under load); the test asserts the steps, which do not depend on the machine's load. | `bug_980_a_run_of_hidden_changes_makes_the_reader_quadratic` (`VEIL_BUG980_HIDDEN`) |
| BUG-981 | medium (introduced by BUG-871's fix; **fixed**, S12 cycle 2) | server / derived storage | **The folders a change lists are not counted against `MAX_PATHS`, so a changed-paths object has no size bound:** a snapshot that adds 100,001 empty folders and changes no file is not `many`; its object lists all 100,001 folders (1.9 MB). A member who may write a folder uploads such a tree once, then alternates it, changing one file each time so that no two objects are equal: each snapshot of a few hundred bytes writes an object of megabytes (a million folders: tens of MB each; 100,000 snapshots a push), and every later line rebuild (`prepare_lists`) and S13 read of the change decodes it whole. | `derive/mod.rs` `derive_one`: `ch.len() > changes::MAX_PATHS` decides `many` on the leaves only; `changes::diff` returns `dirs` unbounded and `Changed { paths, similar, dirs }` is encoded whole. Suggested fix: decide `many` on `ch.len() + dirs.len()`. **Fixed:** `derive_one` decides `many` on the leaves and folders together (`ch.len() + dirs.len() > MAX_PATHS`), so no changed-paths object lists more than `MAX_PATHS` entries. | `bug_981_empty_folders_are_not_capped` |
| BUG-982 | medium (introduced by BUG-870's fix; **fixed**, S12 cycle 2) | server / derive worker | **A landing whose run is skipped, fails or is cut by a restart is never resumed by a later landing:** a run now derives and memoises only the branches its own landing moved, and nothing derives the others: no caller runs `Scope::All`, there is no start-up scan, and `derive_progress` is written but never read. A landing that waits out another server's lock (60 s, e.g. behind a long backfill), meets a busy database, or is lost to a restart leaves its branch's tip underived and its projections unmemoised until the same branch moves again (a release branch may never move). Queries still derive on demand (`ensure`) and pulls project on their own, so nothing wrong is served; but the design (phase-3 §S12, "The worker": "leave it to the holder or the next landing"; "the next landing, or the first query, resumes") no longer tells the truth. | `derive/mod.rs` `run`: `Scope::Branches` reads only the named branches; `landed` drops the branches of a run that returned `skipped` or an error. Before the fix, every run derived every tip. Suggested fix: keep the class bounded per landing and still resume: a run also takes the branches whose `derive_progress` row differs from their target (one indexed statement), or a skipped or failed run puts its branches back for the next one. **Fixed:** every landing's run (`Scope::Branches`) also takes each branch whose `derive_progress` is not its target, in the same statement that reads the moved branches, and memoises what it derived; a server catches up at start (`Config::catch_up_at_start`, `derive::resume`, in the background, one project at a time). The reproduction also covers a landing lost to a restart. | `bug_982_a_skipped_landing_is_resumed_by_the_next` (holds the project's lock for the 60 s wait) |

## Adversarial pass: S27

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of S27, compressed objects (`t3/e1a8e8ad` @ `d7d28e3`, on `integration` @ `d58a952`). Anyone who can sign in can create a project, and so is a participant who may upload objects.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1009 | medium (**fixed**, S27 review cycle 1; introduced by S27) | server / uploads | **Fixed:** a compressed frame a client sends may expand at most 64 times its own size (any frame up to 64 KiB decoded may expand more: `encoding::within_ratio`); the server refuses anything else before decoding it, and `vl` sends such an object plain (`encode_to_send`), so its size is the sender's to pay, as before S27. Decoding in uploads also holds a server-wide budget of 256 MiB of decoded bytes (`sync::DECODING_IN_FLIGHT`, a semaphore by bytes), and a blob is no longer copied for its canonical check. Sixteen uploads at once, each decoding 48 MiB within the ratio, raise the server's memory by 301 MiB (821 MiB without the budget). **Small uploads exhaust the server's memory.** Anyone signed in (in a project of their own) sends a few KiB that decode to an object of up to 1 GiB, which the server holds decoded, about twice, while it checks it. Nothing bounds this across requests: eight 4 KiB requests at once (128 MiB of zeros each, 33 KB sent in all) raised the server's peak memory by 1.33 GiB, one by 262 MiB. 1 GiB objects (32 KiB requests) need only a few dozen at once to kill a shared server. Before S27, each such object cost the sender its size in upload. §13.13's accepted risk ("up to 2 GiB per request") is bounded per request only. | `sync::upload` decodes each frame (`encoding::decode`, bounded only by the object limit and the 2 GiB body limit, per request) and runs `Object::decode` on it (a blob is copied), on a blocking thread per request: tokio's blocking pool allows 512 at once. Suggested fix: refuse a frame that expands more than a fixed ratio (`vl` then sends such an object plain, so its cost is the sender's), or bound decoded bytes in flight server-wide. | `server_hub` `sync::bug_1009_a_small_upload_cannot_make_the_server_decode_a_large_object` |
| BUG-1008 | medium (**fixed**, S27 review cycle 1; introduced by S27) | server / encoding / web client | **Fixed:** `encoding::decode` refuses a frame declaring a window above 2^27 (`MAX_WINDOW`, what every decoder reads) on every path, before decoding; and an upload is stored as the server's own `encode` of what it decoded, never as the client sent it, so no client chooses the stored bytes of an object others share (an S3 PUT replaces what the key held). **A participant can make another folder's object unreadable to the web client.** A zstd frame may declare a window far larger than its content (2 GiB here). libzstd's one-shot decoder, which the server and native `vl` use for objects up to 64 MiB, reads it. The pure decoder of the WASM web client refuses any window above 2^27. `dev` (no billing access) uploads such a frame, as encoded frames, for a file billing also holds (the same object: a licence, a vendored file). The server checks it, gives a receipt, and stores it as sent over the admin's encoding. Every snapshot naming that object, billing's included, now serves a frame the web client can't decode. | `encoding::decode` checks the declared size but not the window, and `sync::upload` keeps a client's encoding (`_ if encoded => enc`) under an id the project may already hold. Suggested fix: `decode` refuses a frame whose window is above `MAX_DELTA_WINDOW_LOG` (2^27, what both decoders accept), or the server stores only its own `encode` of what it decoded. | `veil-core` `hub::encoding::tests::bug_1008_a_frame_every_decoder_reads_or_none` (with `--features ruzstd` it also shows the pure decoder refusing); `server_hub` `sync::bug_1008_an_upload_cannot_store_a_frame_the_web_client_cannot_read` |

## Confinement: the allow-list is writable per workspace (2026-11-07)

Found by the owner. Attacker: none; a confinement that breaks the tools it is for (`docs/design/scale/9-confinement.md`, "Writes to the allow-list").

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1025 | high (**fixed**) | confinement / allow-list | **Fixed:** each allowed folder is an overlay whose lower layer is the real folder and whose upper layer is the workspace's own (`.veil/local/sandboxes/<ws>/layers`, `0700`); an allowed file is a per-workspace copy (`0600`) bound read-write; `--ephemeral` and `--with-isolated` runs get throwaway layers (`--tmp-overlay`); the masks are mounted on top; a folder that holds the project, or anything hidden below its top level, stays read-only; without overlayfs the run goes on read-only and says what breaks. The real folders are never written. **`vl ws exec` showed the allow-list (`~/.cargo`, `~/.rustup`, `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json`, `~/.codex`, `~/.nvm`, …) read-only, with no writable layer, and `HOME` was a tmpfs gone after the run:** `cargo build` after an agent added a crate failed (`failed to create directory ~/.cargo/registry/cache/…: Read-only file system`, seen with the real cargo), Claude Code, Codex and Gemini could not save their settings or sessions, npm and pyenv installs failed, and nothing a tool wrote survived to the next run. | the design made the allow-list read-only and left the overlay sandboxes for later | `bug_1025_a_confined_cargo_writes_its_home_and_the_next_run_has_it`, `bug_1025_coding_agents_save_their_settings_and_sessions`, `bug_1025_what_a_run_writes_to_the_allow_list_stays_with_that_workspace_only` |
| BUG-1030 | medium (**fixed**, layers verification) | confinement / layers | **Fixed:** before the layers are mounted, whatever the upper layer holds at a masked path is removed (`remove_tree`, links never followed), so the mask lies on the real entry; the warning names the cause it found (overlayfs, tried on `/usr`, or the workspace's layers). **A run that left folders in its layer at `~/.cargo/credentials` and `credentials.toml`, before the real files existed, made every later run of the workspace read-only** once they did: the masks (`/dev/null` bound on a file) could not be mounted onto folders, and the warning said "overlayfs does not work here".
