| BUG-1070 | low (**pre-existing**: S1; needs the real id of a hidden snapshot, a 256-bit hash) | server / sync routes | **`POST …/history` and `POST …/fetch` answer a real snapshot id from someone who sees that snapshot differently:** asked by a dev for the real id of a change of billing only, `history` answers 200 with the dev's projected history below it, where any other id gets 404 `no snapshot … that you can see`. That confirms the change exists (phase-3 design §6, row 6: "real ids are never accepted from a viewer without full view"; `docs/HUB.md` §13.4: such a change "is not in `v`'s history at all"). The query API (S13) takes only ids of the viewer's own history. | `sync::resolve` returns any committed snapshot as itself, whoever asks; `history` and `fetch` then project it for the caller. Suggested fix: for a viewer who is not an admin, accept a committed id only when it is its own projection for them (or found in their memo), as `query::resolve` does. | `query::bug_1070_sync_routes_accept_real_ids_of_hidden_snapshots` |

## Adversarial pass: S13

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of milestone S13, the query API (`t3/dd667ae9` @ `589e368` on `integration` @ `d58a952`): `crates/veil-server/src/query/`, `migrations/0010_view_graph.sql`, the routes in `api.rs` and the change to `derive::memo_tips`. All three findings are introduced by S13. Reproductions: `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/query.rs`, module `s13_adversarial` (the container suite, `scripts/verify-server.sh`; all three fixed, S13 fixes). No leak was found: answers, errors, cursors and `work` matched what the viewer's own copy gives on every probe, and the view key reaches no client (below). All three are resource bounds that §11 states and the code does not keep.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1072 | medium (denial of service of the whole server; anyone on Earth; **fixed**, S13 fixes) | server / query `diff`, `show` | **Fixed:** rename and copy detection (`changes::sources_with`, also what `sources` and the deriver run) holds at most 16 MiB of deleted files' lines (`SIMILAR_MAX_HELD`) and reads at most 64 MiB for one change (`SIMILAR_MAX_READ`); past either, similarity is skipped for the whole change (`similar: false`, the diff says `renames_skipped`), a function of the change alone. Each added file is read, compared and dropped in turn. The query API passes `G::tick`, so every file read counts as work and stops at the deadline. Measured (anyone on Earth): 400 + 400 files of 256 KiB, memory rose 18–23 MiB and the request failed with `deadline` at 0.51–0.53 s (deadline 0.5 s); at the caps, 1,000 + 1,000 files of 1,023 KiB, 21–31 MiB, and 59 MiB for the same diff given 120 s, which answered with `renames_skipped`. **One anonymous `diff` holds hundreds of MiB to gigabytes and runs far past its deadline:** `Trees::diff` runs S12's rename and copy detection (`changes::sources`) on whatever pair of revisions the caller names. That pass loads every deleted and added plain-text file of up to 1 MiB, up to 1,000 of each, and keeps every file's table of line hashes until it ends. It never calls `G::tick`, so neither the 2 s deadline nor `work` sees it. Measured, as anyone on Earth, `diff?from=X&to=Y&base=from` over 400 deleted and 400 added files of 256 KiB (two blobs and two trees of copies: about 600 KB uploaded): **memory rose 654 MiB, and the answer came after 14.7 s against a 500 ms deadline, with `work` 10**. At the caps (1,000 + 1,000 files of 1 MiB) that is about 10× as much: several GB per request, so a few concurrent requests take the process, and every project on it, down. Content like this is ordinary: moving a folder of a thousand text files makes it, and `diff` between any two distant revisions of a large public project reaches it. A member who may write a public folder can plant it with a few hundred KB. The deriver runs the same function once per landed change (S12, pre-existing at landing); S13 makes it repeatable, concurrent and anonymous. | `query/trees.rs:220` calls `changes::sources(&self.g.cx.src, …)` on the viewer's change list; `derive/changes.rs:285`–`291` builds `texts` for every candidate before comparing any; nothing on the path checks the deadline. Suggested fix: bound the pass by what it reads, not only by file counts. Count the bytes `text_lines` reads against a budget (e.g. 64 MiB of text per answer, then `similar: false`, a function of the viewer's part, so the copy cuts at the same place), tick per file read, and keep only the added side's table at a time (compare each deleted file as it is read). | `s13_adversarial::bug_1072_a_diff_holds_gigabytes_past_its_deadline` (in a child process; `VEIL_BUG1072_FILES`, `VEIL_BUG1072_KIB`) |
| BUG-1073 | medium (denial of service of the whole server; anyone on Earth, given enough cold view keys; **fixed**, S13 fixes) | server / viewer-graph fills | **Fixed:** no connection is held across a fill. One server at a time fills a view key by a lease row (`view_fills`, migration 0010: taken, renewed every 30 s and given back by single statements; it expires 120 s after its last renewal), and at most `MAX_FILLS` (4) fills run at once on a server, each running its statements one at a time. A query past the cap waits for a slot until its deadline, then answers `warming`; a landing waits for one. Measured: 24 cold fills at once on a pool of 16 all answered within 0.5 s, and an unrelated statement meanwhile took 0.4–0.5 ms (PostgreSQL and YugabyteDB). **Concurrent first fills hold every pooled connection and stall every request on the server:** `locked_fill` takes a connection from the pool for the session advisory lock and holds it through the whole fill, and the fill's own statements (`sync::projected`, `G::present`, `G::add`) need further connections from the same pool. Fills run one per (project, view key), with no limit on how many at once, and a query starts one whenever its viewer's graph is cold. That is the case for every graph once S13 is deployed on existing projects, after a policy or group change, and for a key no landing warmed. With as many cold fills as the pool has connections (32 by default), every connection is held by a fill waiting for another. Measured with the tests' pool of 16: 24 anonymous `log` requests to 24 cold public projects gave **22 internal errors (`filling a viewer graph: PoolTimedOut`) after 60 s**, and an unrelated `SELECT 1` waited **29.5 s** (the pool's acquire timeout). With 6 projects, everything answered in 0.5 s. The next requests start the fills again, so a crawler can repeat it. | `query/graph.rs:866` (`hub.db.acquire()` held until `:877`, around `extend` at `:875`); `start_or_join` (`:837`) starts a fill per key with no limit. Suggested fix: never hold a pooled connection across the fill. Take the lock in a transaction-scoped form per batch, or as a lease row (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT`, with an expiry) that needs no held connection. Also cap concurrent fills per server (a semaphore well under the pool size), so queries beyond it get `warming`. | `s13_adversarial::bug_1073_cold_fills_exhaust_the_connection_pool` (`VEIL_BUG1073_PROJECTS`) |
| BUG-1071 | medium (denial of service of a branch's log; needs one snapshot dated far behind; **fixed**, S13 fixes) | server / query `log` | **Fixed:** the log walks newest first by generation (the corrected commit date), ties by id: generations strictly decrease from child to parent, so children still come first, and each step reads one snapshot's parents and nothing more, with the budget checked at every step; the cursor names the walk's frontier, which is all that is left. The order is `vl log`'s (Kahn's, newest first by timestamp) wherever every snapshot is dated after its parents; with clocks skewed, the order follows the corrected dates. Measured: a page of 1 entry with a budget of 100 reads 7 rows, on a line of 400 and of 1,600. **A log page's work budget is not a bound:** `log` checks `Limits::work` only between emitted entries, but one `Topo::step` can explore without limit. Settling a snapshot explores every snapshot with a higher generation (`explore_to`), so a merge that takes in one snapshot dated far behind (timestamp 0: a crafted push, which push accepts, or a device with a wrong clock) makes the first page of every log above it walk the whole first-parent line below. Measured, as anyone on Earth, a page of `n=1` with a budget of 100 reads: **807 reads over a line of 400, 3,207 over 1,600**, linear in the history. With the default budget (20,000) and a history of hundreds of thousands of snapshots, each page reads rows one statement each until the 2 s deadline. The default branch's log then fails with `deadline` for everyone, whatever `n`, and every attempt costs the server 2 s of a blocking thread. §11 lists "a log page's work budget (20,000 reads)" among the bounds, and says "others hardly can" reach it. | `query/mod.rs:385`–`388` checks the budget per entry; `Topo::settle` (`:302`) → `explore_to` (`:288`) and `step` (`:314`) explore without checking it. Suggested fix: check the budget inside `explore_to`, and end the page there with a cursor. The cursor must then carry the walk's frontier, not only the heads, so the next page continues the same order. Alternatively, explore by generation from the heads (the order Kahn's algorithm needs only requires a snapshot's children to be emitted first). Either way it is a function of the viewer's graph, so the copy cuts at the same place. | `s13_adversarial::bug_1071_a_log_page_walks_past_its_work_budget` (`VEIL_BUG1071_LINE`) |

### S13 cycle 2

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of the S13 fixes (`t3/dd667ae9` @ `1ec85dc`: `ff46dce` and `1ec85dc`, on `integration` @ `d981dba`), the new diff only: the log walk by generation, the caps on rename detection in `derive/changes.rs` (S12's code, also the deriver's), and the fill lease and cap. Reproductions: `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/query.rs`, module `s13_adversarial`; all five failed on PostgreSQL + MinIO and on YugabyteDB + MinIO, and pass since S13 cycle 3 (fixed, below). No leak was found: the log's order, cursors, page boundaries and `work` are functions of the viewer's own graph. Merging with today's `integration` (`d8cf2b2`, S4) conflicts in `crates/veil-server/src/db.rs` (S4's migrations 5 and 6 against S13's 10) and in this file; not resolved here.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Measured: a fifth key's query answered `warming` while four fills of a line of 400 ran; its fill started on its own once a slot was free (5 fills started). **A query whose view key is cold gets its fill only if a slot frees up before the query's own deadline; if none does, it leaves nothing queued and the key stays cold.** `ensure` promises "a query's deadline never bounds, nor pays for, a first fill", but the query now waits for one of the server's `MAX_FILLS` (4) slots *before* the fill exists, and gives up with `warming` at its deadline (2 s). The semaphore is first in, first out, and a landing waits for a slot with no deadline. So with a steady supply of fills (landings in any project, or the first fills of existing projects when S13 is deployed: minutes each on a long history), every query of a key that only queries need gets `warming` indefinitely: the keys of a policy or group change, and dormant public projects. | `query/graph.rs:863`: `start_or_join` takes the slot (`acquire_owned` under the caller's deadline) before `fills.insert` (`:875`) and the spawn. **Held up, as tested or traced:**
* **The walk by generation:**
  * **Children before parents on every graph shape.** A child's generation is strictly above each parent's (`VRow::compute`: `max(parent + 1, stamp)`; stamps clamped to `MAX_STAMP` = `i64::MAX / 4`, so no saturation). So every snapshot on a path from a root to `x` is popped before `x`. Skewed clocks and merges of merges change only the generations, never this ordering.
  * **Cursors.** The popped generations never increase, so no frontier snapshot has an emitted ancestor or descendant still to come. The walk from the frontier is exactly the rest of the walk: same set, same keys, and no snapshot emitted twice. `queued` stops loops and duplicates, also for a cursor naming a snapshot and its own ancestor.
  * **Crafted cursors.** Each id must have a row in the caller's own `view_graph` and not be withheld. `FLAG_EMBARGO_LINE` is inherited from every parent, so a snapshot that is not withheld has no withheld ancestor: a walk from a cursor stays inside the viewer's graph and outside embargo lines. A 1,000-id cursor costs 2,000 reads before the first step.
  * **Equivalence.** `query_projection_equivalence` and `query_graph_matches_direct_walks` pass on fresh seeds 7720 and 31337 (PostgreSQL), and the five reproductions above leak nothing by construction. The order and `work` come from `view_graph` rows only; the generation is never output.
* **The deriver's caps (S12):** the bytes read, the bytes held and the comparison budget all grow with the files a change holds, and each is checked as it accumulates. So whenever the whole change passes all three, every viewer's part (a subset, in the same order) passes too, with the same pairwise scores. When the whole change fails one, `Reader::changes` recomputes on the viewer's part (`derive/view.rs:297`). Either way the result is what the viewer's copy would derive. S12's `projection_equivalence` passes on fresh seeds 9341, 52001 and 77013 (PostgreSQL). The query `diff` computes from the viewer's part only, with `G::tick` per file read.
* **The lease:**
  * **Two fills of one key** happen only after a lease expires: a server's clock more than 120 s ahead of another's, or a renewal missed for 120 s. Rows are written `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and are a function of the projection, so the duplicate costs work only.
  * **Renewal and give-back** match on `holder`, a random 128-bit value, so a server that lost its lease never extends or deletes the new holder's.
  * **A stopped server's leases** expire after 120 s.
* **BUG-1071..1073's own reproductions** pass on both databases. Under load, `bug_1073`, `query_first_fill_runs_once_in_the_background`, `query_concurrent_extensions_agree` and `query_landing_fills_the_viewer_graphs` passed 32/32 with 8 copies at once on PostgreSQL and 12/12 with 3 on YugabyteDB.

**Not filed:**
* **Interaction with BUG-911's fix (the deriver pool, not landed).** `memo_tips` waits for a fill slot with no deadline (`derive/mod.rs:949`) inside the landing's task. If that fix holds a pool permit across `memo_tips`, four long fills (or BUG-1075's waits) would stall every project's derivation. Check it when both land.
* **The order departs from `vl log`'s with skewed clocks** (documented in the phase-3 design, §3.3). The two orders are the same only where each snapshot is dated *strictly* after its parents: a child in the same millisecond as its parent gets the parent's generation + 1 and may tie with an unrelated snapshot, which the walk orders by id. Thin and full clones can then list such snapshots in different orders. Whether to accept this is the owner's call (phase-3 design §2: "`vl log` … work the same in a thin clone as in a full one").

## Adversarial pass: S3

### S3 cycle 1

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of milestone S3, fetch on demand (`t3/ebed8889` @ `d4aa8ae`, 3 commits on `260605c`, merged for the review onto `integration` @ `3f84531`): `veil-core` `promisor.rs`, the store's read path and cache, `Repo::exact`/`deepen`, format 9, the thin pull and `vl partial`, the server's history pages. All six findings are introduced by S3. The merge conflicted in `docs/HUB.md` (both sides kept) and in the doc comment of `wire::REVISION` (both texts kept; BUG-1140). Reproductions: `crates/veil-core/tests/core_sync/thin.rs` and `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/thin.rs`, tests named `s3r_…`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1142 | important (fixed; **introduced** by S3; threat 1 of the partial-clone design) | thin clones / read path | **An object whose place the process did not record reads as `Missing`, a redaction, although the server would serve it.** The locator stops recording at `LOCATOR_CAP` (8,000,000 objects met in one process); `promisor.rs` says that reads of objects met later "fail with `VeilError::Unavailable`, never as hidden", but `read_partial` answers every object without a location as a snapshot beyond the boundary: `Missing`. The checkout's fetch-ahead swallows that `Missing` (`ensure_held`), and the checkout leaves the file out and records it as hidden. A scratch run with the bound lowered to 6, 9 and 12 checked out 0, 3 and 6 of the project's 12 files with the server up, and called the rest hidden. With a checkout or a `vl mount` session meeting more than 8 million entries (S3's target scale), files the person may read vanish from the working copy as if withheld. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 1): a store read knows whether it asks for a snapshot; a tree or file with no recorded place is `Unavailable`, only a snapshot is the boundary (`Missing`, recorded); the fetch-ahead propagates it. The locator records every tree and only the files no pack holds, bounded at 2,000,000 places (about 90 MiB). `thin::every_producer_of_missing_is_audited` lists each place that makes a `Missing`. | `promisor.rs:122` (`note` stops at the cap) and `promisor.rs:392–396` (no location: `Missing`, for any kind of object); `promisor.rs:505` takes that `Missing` for hidden. Fix: no location is `Unavailable`, except for an id met as a snapshot's parent (the boundary). | `core_sync` `thin::s3r_an_object_without_a_recorded_place_is_never_hidden` (a tree the process never met stands in for one met past the cap) |
| BUG-1141 | important (fixed; **introduced** by S3) | thin clones / history beyond the boundary | **Commands that read snapshots beyond a thin clone's boundary outside `Repo::exact` fail or answer wrongly.** `vl show X` of a snapshot whose parent the clone does not hold fails with `object … is not present in this store`; `vl show` of a merge whose other parent is beyond the boundary takes that parent for a withheld one and lists the other side's files as added by the merge (a full clone shows an empty diff); `vl blame` stops at the boundary and gives every line to the tip (`visited: 1` instead of 4). Same class, not tested: `vl evolog` ("older versions were removed by `vl gc`"), `vl bisect`, the parent trees of `log -p`/search, the rewrite bookkeeping in `transaction.rs` (`snapshot_opt` sites). No leak: wrong results and errors. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 1): `Repo::snapshot`/`snapshot_opt` fetch a page of history where the clone's boundary is (one place); the history index alone reads only what is held (`snapshot_held`), and `Repo::exact` pages history in for its walks. `thin::every_snapshot_read_that_does_not_fetch_is_audited` lists the reads that skip it. | The boundary reads as `Missing`, which `snapshot_opt` and `parents_tree` (`repo.rs:1034–1046`, `api.rs:1463`) and blame (`blame.rs:573`) take for a redacted snapshot; only `is_ancestor`, `merge_bases`, `common_ancestor`, revision lookup and `vl log` run through `Repo::exact`. The audit test counts `is_unreadable()` and `Missing(` but not the 30 `snapshot_opt` call sites. Fix (the class): fetch the snapshots a command reads beyond the boundary (`snapshot`/`snapshot_opt` deepen on a boundary hit, as `Ctx::rev` does), rather than wrap more call sites. | `server_hub` `thin::s3r_show_of_a_snapshot_whose_parent_is_beyond_the_boundary`, `thin::s3r_show_of_a_merge_whose_other_parent_is_beyond_the_boundary`, `thin::s3r_blame_in_a_thin_clone_is_the_full_clones` |
| BUG-1143 | important (fixed; **introduced** by S3) | thin clones / fsck, gc | **In a thin clone, `vl fsck` reports the loss of unpushed local work as a note.** Every missing object becomes "not fetched: this thin clone reads it from the server", including a file of a commit that was never pushed, whose only copy was in the main store: fsck finds "nothing wrong". gc has the same assumption: its mark skips a missing tree in a thin clone instead of recording the walk as incomplete, so `may_delete` stays true and gc deletes the objects below a lost local tree that a full clone's gc would keep. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 1): fsck and gc classify a gap (`ObjectStore::classify_gap`): the server's when its snapshot is in the remotes' history, or a parent down to one there names the same object at the same path (fsck: a note; gc: skipped); lost when only this clone's snapshots name it (fsck: corrupt; gc: incomplete, nothing deleted); unknown when the trees that would tell are not held (fsck: a warning; gc: incomplete). | `fsck.rs:485` downgrades every `Corrupt` missing object when `is_partial()`; `gc.rs:452`, `466`, `520` (`Missing if self.partial`). Both assume "nothing local sits only below what is on the server", which holds for objects of the server's history, not for those of local snapshots. Fix: downgrade only objects reached from snapshots on the server (the remote tags' history); what only local snapshots reach stays damage. | `core_sync` `thin::s3r_fsck_in_a_thin_clone_reports_lost_local_work` |
| BUG-1140 | important (fixed; **introduced** by the merge of S3 onto `integration`; a broken convention) | protocol / `wire::REVISION` | **Protocol revision 3 announces two releases:** S5 (on `integration`) bumped `REVISION` to 3 for read grants and the object routes, and S3 bumped it to 3 for history pages (`HistoryRequest::limit`). The merge conflicts only in the doc comment; the value merges silently. A client that sees revision 3 cannot tell whether `history` pages (`hub.rs:799`, `hub_cmd.rs:204` test `revision < 3`): a server of S5 alone would ignore `limit` and send whole histories to thin clones. Nothing is deployed yet. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 1): history pages are revision 4 (`hub::HISTORY_PAGES`); a server below it gets a full clone (clone) or a clear refusal (pull of a thin clone). | Two streams took the same next revision. Fix: history pages are revision 4 (`REVISION`, the doc, and the two client checks). | `core_sync` `thin::s3r_each_protocol_revision_announces_one_thing` |
| BUG-1144 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3) | thin clones / read path | **A local commit's unchanged directory cannot be read once the server's tip has moved on.** After a pull of a teammate's commit that changed that directory, and an eviction (the working copy checked out elsewhere), the read asks for it under the local commit (unknown to the server), then under the server's current tips (where the path holds the teammate's version), never under the local commit's own parent on the server, which holds it. It fails with `Unavailable` and advises `vl pull`, which cannot help; `vl new` of the local commit fails the same way. `vl partial full` recovers it (its widening pull fetches all history first). **Fixed** (S3 cycle 1): an object met under a local commit is asked for under the commit's nearest ancestors on the server (up to 8), then the server's tips. | `promisor.rs:408` tries `server_tips()` only; `on_server` (`promisor.rs:419`) is asked about the local snapshot only. Fix: ask under the nearest ancestor of the snapshot where the object was met that is on the server. | `core_sync` `thin::s3r_a_local_commits_unchanged_directory_is_found_after_the_server_moved_on` |
| BUG-1145 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3; threat 11) | thin clones / cache bound | **A checkout's fetch-ahead fills the cache past its bound:** `vl new big` in a clone made with `--cache-size 100K` left 204 KiB in the cache (all pinned), where the design says the fetch stops at the bound with an error, as the clone's refusal does. A batch is up to 1,000 objects of any size, so the overshoot grows with the files (gigabytes for large files). **Fixed** (S3 cycle 1): a fetch-ahead batch is at most 1,000 objects and about 8 MiB (by the sizes tree entries carry); bytes in flight count in the bound with those on disk, and a batch that cannot fit fails before it is asked. `vl new` and `vl edit` fetch ahead before they record anything, so a failed move leaves nothing to retry. | `ensure_held` charges each object (`charge`, `promisor.rs:564`) before its batch's pack is published; the eviction `charge` triggers counts only what is on disk and resets the running total to that (`promisor.rs:761`), erasing the batch's charges. Fix: count the batch's bytes in the bound (charge them after the trim, or trim against on-disk plus in flight). | `server_hub` `thin::s3r_a_checkout_past_the_cache_bound_fails_before_writing` |

### S3 cycle 2

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of the S3 cycle 1 fixes (`t3/ebed8889` @ `cea201b` on `integration` @ `3f84531`; new diff `5b6e9b9`, `cea201b`): BUG-1140 to 1145's fixes, `classify_gap`, history paging in `Repo::snapshot_opt`, the locator's bound, the fetch-ahead. All five findings are introduced by S3; BUG-1146 is BUG-1145's second half (the gap the builder named), BUG-1260 is introduced by the BUG-1141 fix. Reproductions: `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/thin.rs` and `crates/veil-core/tests/core_sync/thin.rs` (tests named `s3r2_…`), `crates/veil-core/src/promisor.rs` (`s3r2_tests`).

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1146 | important (fixed; **introduced** by S3; BUG-1145's class; threat 11) | thin clones / working-copy moves | **A command that moves the working copy records the move, then fails to fetch it, and the clone is wedged: every later command fails, including the recovery its error advises.** In a clone bounded at 100 KiB, `vl rebase -s @ -d big`, `vl merge big`, `vl new main big` (a merge), `vl cherry-pick big`, `vl undo` and `vl op restore` (back to a working copy on `big`, evicted) each record their operation, then fail with "the object cache … is full … Raise the bound (`vl partial limit SIZE`)". Then `vl status`, `vl undo` and `vl partial limit 1G` all fail the same way: each command first brings the stale directory up to the recorded working copy (`ctx.rs:569–617`), which fetches the same 400 KB. Only hand-editing `repo.json` gets out. The same route with a lost server instead of a full cache would stop local work (`vl status`, `vl commit`), which the threat review says goes on (not tested). `HUB.md` §13.21 and threat 11 say "a too-large move [is refused] before it is recorded". `vl new REV`, `vl edit REV`, `vl ws switch` and `vl restore --from` hold. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 2): `Transaction::commit` fetches ahead, before publishing, whatever the operation does to the project directory's working copy (any command: `new` of one or several parents, `edit`, `rebase`, `merge`, `cherry-pick`, `restore`, `undo`, `op restore`), so a full cache or a lost server fails it with nothing recorded. A stale directory a command cannot bring up to `@` (the start-of-command catch-up, the end-of-command move) stays as it is with a warning, nothing recorded, so `status`, `undo`, `op restore` and `partial limit` run; a commit stops. `server_hub` `thin::every_working_copy_move_past_the_cache_bound_records_nothing` runs each kind past the bound. | The cycle 1 fix fetches ahead in two commands (`api.rs:2250`, single parent only; `main.rs:350`); every other operation that changes the attached workspace's `wc` publishes first, and `Ctx::finish` fetches after (`ctx.rs:887–893`). The catch-up at the start of every command then has no way out. Fix (the class, rule 6): key on what the operation does, not on the command. Before an operation that moves the attached workspace's working copy is published, fetch ahead its target (one place, e.g. where `Ctx` commits the transaction, or a hook in `Transaction::commit` for thin clones), and let the start-of-command catch-up leave the directory where it is (as BUG-830's recovery does) when the fetch fails, so `vl undo` and `vl partial limit` can run. | `server_hub` `thin::s3r2_a_rebase_past_the_cache_bound_records_nothing`, `s3r2_a_merge_…`, `s3r2_a_new_merge_…`, `s3r2_a_cherry_pick_…`, `s3r2_an_undo_…`, `s3r2_an_op_restore_…` (controls: `s3r2_a_workspace_switch_…`, `s3r2_a_restore_…`) |
| BUG-1260 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by the BUG-1141 fix; scale, S3's purpose) | thin clones / history | **A tag whose name could be an id makes a thin clone fetch the project's whole history.** A pull checks each new remote tag against every change and snapshot id (BUG-105) when its name is only the letters k–z (`lts`, `trunk`, `work`, `root`) or four or more hex digits (`2025`, `cafe`). The check walks every visible snapshot (`RevisionNames::shadows`, `revset.rs:289`, via `topo_children_first`), and since cycle 1 each snapshot read pages in 2,000 snapshots at the boundary. So the first `vl clone` of such a project, and each pull that brings such a tag, holds all history, as a full clone does. Here a clone of a 7-commit project tagged `lts` shows the whole `vl log` with the server gone; a clone before the tag needs the server. At S3's scale it is every snapshot of the project, page by page, inside the pull's transaction. Same class, not tested: `vl embargo release` (`main.rs:1210`) and `vl bisect reset` (`history.rs:733`) walk `visible_snapshots()`. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 2): whole-graph walks read only what is held (`topo_children_first`, `ancestors`, `common_ancestor`, `ancestors_of`, `merge_bases_naive`, the rewrite bookkeeping's walk); their exact answers still run through `Repo::exact`. `thin::every_snapshot_read_that_fetches_is_not_a_whole_graph_walk` lists every read that pages history in. | `snapshot_opt` now fetches at the boundary (`repo.rs:894–907`). The audit (`every_snapshot_read_that_does_not_fetch_is_audited`) lists reads that do *not* fetch; nothing lists the whole-graph walks that now *do*. Fix: such a walk reads what is held (`snapshot_held`), and asks the server where its answer depends on what lies beyond. For `shadows`, check the name against held history plus the server's own id lookup, rather than walk it in. Add these walks to the audit table. | `server_hub` `thin::s3r2_a_tag_named_like_an_id_does_not_fetch_the_whole_history` |
| BUG-1148 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3, the BUG-1143 fix) | thin clones / gc | **gc in a thin clone never completes once the server's trees are evicted, which is the normal state.** A local commit `L` on the server's tip `T` keeps `T`'s unchanged directories by id. After a pull of a teammate's `Q`, a checkout of `Q` and a trim, those directories and `T`'s root tree are gone from the cache. gc's mark meets them missing under `L`, and `classify_gap` must read `T`'s evicted root tree to compare, so it answers `Unknown`. The mark is incomplete (`tree … at 'src': … is not present in this store`), and gc deletes nothing on every run while `L`, or any older working-copy snapshot the op log keeps, is in a root. Safe (nothing is lost), but in steady state a thin clone's gc never runs. `vl fsck` should give the same gaps as warnings ("not fetched, or lost"; not tested). **Fixed** (S3 cycle 2): eviction pins the trees (not the files) of the server-side bases of the snapshots only this clone holds (from the view's heads, tags and working copies, and the remotes' tips), so `classify_gap` can always compare. | `classify_gap` (`promisor.rs`, the `entry_held` of a parent's tree) needs trees of the server's history that the cache evicts. Fix: pin in the cache the trees (not the files) of the server-side parents of the snapshots gc and fsck walk as local (the heads' bases), or keep the trees on the way to each local snapshot's paths, so the comparison always has them. | `core_sync` `thin::s3r2_gc_in_a_thin_clone_completes_after_an_eviction` |
| BUG-1147 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3, the BUG-1142 fix; latent until a long-lived process) | thin clones / read path | **A file in a cache pack when its tree was decoded, evicted later in the same process, cannot be read for the rest of that process.** The fix leaves out of the locator every file a pack holds when its tree is decoded, including the packs of the *cache* area, which is evicted. Once a trim removes such a pack, the file has no place, and its reads are `Unavailable` ("run the command again"). Reading its tree again does not help: the decoded tree stays in the store's tree cache and is never noted again. A one-shot command recovers in the next process; `vl mount`, or the S6 daemon, never does. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 2): only files the main store's packs hold (never evicted) go unnoted; files in the cache's packs get a place. | `note_decoded` (`promisor.rs`: `self.in_loaded_packs(&e.id) \|\| p.cache.in_loaded_packs(&e.id)`). Fix: skip only files the main store's packs hold (never evicted), and record those in cache packs (they count against the cache's own bound). | `core_sync` `thin::s3r2_a_file_whose_cache_pack_was_evicted_is_read_again_in_the_same_process` |
| BUG-1149 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3, the BUG-1142 fix; a doc that lies, the client memory gate) | thin clones / locator | **The locator at its bound holds two to four times the "about 90 MiB" the code and `HUB.md` state.** `LOCATOR_CAP` is 2,000,000 places "about 46 bytes each: at most about 90 MiB", "under the 512 MiB client gate". A hash map grows by doubling and is at most 7/8 full, so at the bound the `at` map alone has room for 3.7 million entries. The parents' map and vector come on top. A counting allocator over the same structures held 166 MiB (100 entries a tree), 181 MiB (10) and 376 MiB (1) at the bound, with peaks of 248 to 458 MiB while a map grows: most of the client gate, before the rest of the command. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 2): a compact locator (8-byte keys, 16 bytes a place; a collision is caught by checking that the parent names the object, now also for roots and conflict terms), bounded at 1,500,000 places and parents together: measured with the counting allocator (`core_security` `thin_locator_memory_at_its_bound`) at 35 to 66 MiB held and 51 to 82 MiB at the peak, for 1 to 100 entries a tree. | The estimate counts the entry's bytes, not the map's capacity, the parents' map, or a rehash. Fix: a bound computed from the real footprint (about 1,000,000 places for 90 MiB), or `with_capacity` for the bound and a measured figure in the docs; re-run `bench-scale.sh 1g` with a thin case. | `veil-core` (lib) `promisor::s3r2_tests::s3r2_the_locator_at_its_bound_is_about_90_mib` (from the maps' capacities: at least 155 MiB) |

### S3 cycle 3

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep), the last cycle, of the S3 cycle 2 fixes (`t3/ebed8889` @ `59153c1` on `integration` @ `1b00bee`; new diff `a376dfd..59153c1`: BUG-1146..1149 and 1260's fixes, the server-tips refresh). The merge conflicted in `docs/BUGS.md` only (both sides kept). Seven findings, all in S3: BUG-1261, 1262 and 1265 are introduced by the cycle 2 fixes (they pass on `a376dfd`); BUG-1263, 1266 and 1267 are older S3 routes that the cycle 2 fixes and audits claimed to cover; BUG-1264 is a route of BUG-1148 its fix left open. Reproductions: `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/thin.rs` and `crates/veil-core/tests/core_sync/thin.rs`, tests named `s3r3_…`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1261 | important (fixed; **introduced** by the BUG-1260 fix; BUG-105's class) | thin clones / revision names | **A pulled tag named like the id of a change the thin clone does not hold hides that change.** A full clone's pull refuses to create a local tag whose name is a change or snapshot id prefix of its history ("the name is also a change or snapshot id of this repository"), so whoever can push a tag cannot redirect `vl edit <change>` (BUG-105). Since cycle 2 the check (`RevisionNames::shadows`) walks only the held snapshots (`topo_children_first` is held-only), so in a thin clone, which holds the tips, a tag named after an old change's id is created, and from then on that id names the tag's target, as tags resolve first (`revset::resolve_base`): `vl show <first change>` shows "commit 5" where a full clone shows "first", also after the change's history was fetched. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 3, the redesign of names, `HUB.md` §13.21): the pull's check asks the server's id lookup (`q/resolve`, revision 5) for each new tag name that looks like an id, with the held history; such a name never becomes a local tag. | The BUG-1260 fix made the check held-only without the server lookup its row asked for ("check the name against held history plus the server's own id lookup"). Fix (with BUG-1266, one root): an id-prefix lookup the server answers over this person's history (change and snapshot ids), used by the pull's check for what lies beyond the boundary, and by revision resolution when held history has no match. | `server_hub` `thin::s3r3_a_pulled_tag_never_hides_the_id_of_a_change_the_thin_clone_does_not_hold` |
| BUG-1262 | important (fixed; **introduced** by the BUG-1260 fix) | thin clones / bisect | **`vl bisect` in a thin clone searches only the held snapshots and names the wrong first bad snapshot.** `bisect::candidates` reads `Repo::ancestors` and `topo_children_first`, which the BUG-1260 fix made held-only, and `vl bisect` calls it outside `Repo::exact`. A project where `data/f3.bin` arrives in "commit 3": a full clone's bisect finds commit 3, a thin clone's says at once "The first bad snapshot is … commit 11" (the oldest it holds). The fix's claim "their exact answers still run through `Repo::exact`" does not hold for this caller. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 3): history reads are typed (`Held`/`Exact`); bisect's candidates are `Exact::range(bad, goods)`, paging in only that range. | Callers of the held-only walks that need the whole answer were not all moved into `Repo::exact`. Fix: run `bisect::next` (its candidate walks) inside `Repo::exact`, and check every other caller of `ancestors`/`topo_children_first`/`visible_snapshots` outside it (`vl embargo release`'s listing, `bisect reset`). | `server_hub` `thin::s3r3_bisect_in_a_thin_clone_finds_what_a_full_clone_finds` |
| BUG-1265 | important (fixed; **introduced** by the server-tips refresh of cycle 2; BUG-1142's class) | thin clones / on the server, working-copy moves | **A second remote's snapshots count as the thin clone's server's; a move onto one wedges the clone.** `pin_working_copies` hands every remote's tags (`remote_tags.values()`) to `set_local_heads`, and `server_tips_now` judges "on the server" from them, where the connection's tips were the clone's own remote's only (`thin::attach` filters `origin/`). A thin clone that also pulls from a fork (another project, `vl remote add fork …`) takes the fork's snapshots for its server's. Once the fork's checked-out file is evicted, it is asked of the clone's server, which never had that snapshot, and the "nothing there" reads as a redaction: `vl show fork/main` fails with "object … is not present in this store"; `vl new fork/main` passes its fetch-ahead (a refusal is left for its reader), records and journals the move, and fails half way. From then on every command (`vl status`, `vl op log`, `vl undo`) fails with "'/' is not fetched, and the server has no copy of it" until `.veil/local/checkout.json` is edited by hand. On `a376dfd` the same steps leave a working clone. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 3): "on the server" is the `partial` remote's tips only (`promisor::own_tips`), in the read path, eviction's pins, gc and fsck; a pull from another remote is a full pull into the main store. | `repo.rs` `pin_working_copies` (no remote filter); `promisor.rs` `server_tips_now`. Fix: hand `set_local_heads` the partial remote's tips only (the prefix `thin::attach` uses). Separately, the fetch-ahead lets a refused object through for a reader that then fails rather than hides it: a move whose read fails after its journal must not wedge every command (check that class with this test). | `server_hub` `thin::s3r3_a_second_remotes_snapshot_is_never_the_servers_and_never_wedges_the_clone` |
| BUG-1266 | important (fixed; **introduced** by S3 before cycle 2, not reported; same root as BUG-1261) | thin clones / revision names | **A thin clone does not find the change id of a change beyond its boundary:** `vl show <change>` of an old change, as a teammate's message or a full clone's `vl log` gives it, fails with "revision … not found" (a full clone shows it), until a command that pages history in (`vl log`) has run; a short snapshot id likewise. `revset::resolve_base` matches change ids and short snapshot ids against the history index (`entries_matching`), which reads what is held and records no boundary hit, so `Repo::exact` in `Ctx::rev` has nothing to page in; only a full 64-digit snapshot id is asked of the server. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 3): the change id and short snapshot id steps of revision resolution take the held matches and the server's (`q/resolve`), one request, a full clone's order and rules. | Revision lookup by id prefix answered from held history only. Fix: the server's id-prefix lookup of BUG-1261, asked when held history has no match (bounded: one request, never a page per snapshot; `s3r3_a_revision_that_names_nothing_does_not_fetch_the_whole_history` keeps a typo from fetching history). | `server_hub` `thin::s3r3_an_old_change_id_names_the_same_change_as_in_a_full_clone` |
| BUG-1263 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3; BUG-1146's class, which its fix claimed closed: "any command") | thin clones / working-copy moves | **`vl ws switch` past the cache's bound records the switch, says it switched, and does not.** The switch leaves the view as it is (the attachment is device-local), so `Transaction::commit`'s fetch-ahead, keyed on a change of the view, skips it, and the end-of-command move falls back to "the working copy stays as it is". The command exits 0 with "Project directory attached to workspace other" while `checkout.json` still says `default`; the warning advises `vl undo`, which in `default` undoes an unrelated earlier operation (here the creation of `other`). Before cycle 2 the switch failed but was recorded too. The cycle 2 control `s3r2_a_workspace_switch_…` passes because the command now succeeds. `vl undo`/`vl redo` of a switch take the same route. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 3): a switch's operation names the workspace it attaches the directory to (`Transaction::attaches`), and the fetch-ahead before publishing fetches that workspace's working copy: a switch that cannot move fails and records nothing. (The reproduction's last step checks `vl undo` only after a switch that succeeded: a failed one records nothing and advises `vl partial limit`.) | The fetch-ahead is keyed on the view changing; a switch moves the directory without changing the view. Fix: fetch ahead in `record_switch` (or key `Transaction::commit`'s fetch-ahead on the attached workspace the operation leaves, not only on the view), so a switch that cannot move records nothing and fails. | `server_hub` `thin::s3r3_a_workspace_switch_past_the_cache_bound_switches_or_records_nothing` |
| BUG-1264 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3; a route of BUG-1148 its fix left open) | thin clones / gc | **gc in a thin clone never completes after a local commit is rebased onto a new server tip.** The BUG-1148 fix pins the trees of the server-side bases of the *view's* heads; after `vl pull` and a rebase of the local commit `L` onto the new tip `Q`, the base is `Q`. `L`'s old version, and every working-copy snapshot the op log remembers on the old tip `T`, are still gc roots through the op log (kept whole by default); `T`'s trees are evicted, `classify_gap` cannot compare, and gc is incomplete ("tree … at 'src' … is not present in this store") on every run while the op log holds them. Safe (nothing deleted). **Fixed** (S3 cycle 3): eviction pins the trees of the server-side bases of the local snapshots of every operation's view (gc's roots), not the current view's alone. | `pinned()` takes its local heads from the current view only (`set_local_heads`), while gc's roots are every retained operation's view. Fix: pin the trees of the server-side bases of the local snapshots gc roots (the retained operations' views), or let `classify_gap` compare against a held server snapshot that names the same object at the same path. | `core_sync` `thin::s3r3_gc_in_a_thin_clone_completes_after_a_rebase_onto_the_new_tip` |
| BUG-1267 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3 cycle 1, the BUG-1141 fix; BUG-1260's class, not in its fix or its audit) | thin clones / history | **The short id of a hidden snapshot (an earlier version of a change, as `vl evolog` and `vl op log` show it) makes a thin clone page in the project's whole history.** `revset::recorded_snapshots_with_prefix` walks every operation's view through parents and predecessors with `Repo::snapshot`, which pages history in at the boundary, and descends the server tip's ancestry to the root before it reaches the working copy's predecessors (always for a change since abandoned, whose versions only older operations name; otherwise as the ids fall). With 40 snapshots and a server page of 2, resolving a held earlier version read 80 pages. The cycle 2 audit (`every_snapshot_read_that_fetches_is_not_a_whole_graph_walk`) counts `snapshot_opt(` sites only: none of `Repo::snapshot(`'s callers (which fetch the same way) is audited, so its claim "lists every read that pages history in" does not hold. **Fixed** (S3 cycle 3): the hidden-version lookup reads held only, and `vl` resolves names without paging (held history and the server's lookup); the text audits of snapshot reads are replaced by the `Held`/`Exact` types. | A whole-graph walk reading with the fetching `Repo::snapshot`. Fix: the walk reads held only (`snapshot_held`; a hidden snapshot it names is local, held); and the audit counts `Repo::snapshot(` call sites (or `snapshot` delegates to a held read and fetching becomes the named exception). | `core_sync` `thin::s3r3_a_hidden_snapshots_short_id_does_not_page_in_the_whole_history` |

**Guarantees that hold (tests):** a directory behind `@` that cannot be brought up to it (an interrupted move, the cache emptied and bounded at 100 KiB) lets `vl status`, `vl undo`, `vl op restore` and `vl partial limit` run, each with the warning, and keeps an edit made meanwhile (`server_hub` `thin::s3r3_a_directory_behind_at_…`); a revision that names nothing pages in no history (`thin::s3r3_a_revision_that_names_nothing_…`); the held-only walks page in nothing on a 40-snapshot history (`core_sync` `thin::s3r3_the_whole_graph_walks_page_in_nothing`).

**Not filed:** with the directory left behind `@`, `vl status` prints "The working copy has no changes" beside the warning while an edit in the directory is unrecorded; the edit is kept (checkout keeps local edits) and lands in `@` once the directory catches up, not in a "recovered working-copy edits" change as in a full clone.

### S3 redesign

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep), cycle 1 of the revised design (`HUB.md` §13.21 "Revised: names and fetching"), of `t3/ebed8889` @ `423f688` (`59153c1..423f688`) merged for the review onto `integration` @ `0584d06`. The merge conflicted in `docs/HUB.md` and `docs/BUGS.md` (both sides kept) and in `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/main.rs`, the module list (`mod thin;` against `mod cache;`: both kept, a hand resolution of two added lines). Six findings, all in S3: BUG-1268 and 1269 are in the redesign's `q/resolve`; BUG-1290 and 1291 are routes of the type split the redesign claims closed (guarantee 3); BUG-1292 and 1293 are older S3 routes. Reproductions: `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/thin.rs`, `server_hub/query.rs` and `crates/veil-core/tests/core_sync/thin.rs`, tests named `s3rd_…`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1268 | important (fixed; **introduced** by the S3 redesign, `q/resolve`) | thin clones / revision names | **After a change is rewritten and pushed, a thin clone names its old versions: `vl show <change>` fails with "change … is divergent (2 visible snapshots)"**, where a full clone made at the same time shows the new version; `vl evolog -r <change>` fails the same way; and `vl show <old snapshot id>` of an old version (of the change, or of a descendant it moved) shows it, where the full clone says "revision … not found". Here the admin runs `vl describe -r <first change>` and `vl push --force`; any amend, rebase or describe of a pushed change does the same. `query::resolve_prefix` reads change ids from the real `graph` table, which keeps every snapshot ever derived (old versions included), projects each with `ensure` (filling viewer-graph rows for snapshots no branch reaches), and keeps every row that is not withheld; its snapshot-id step reads `view_graph`, which keeps the rows of old tips. Neither is "the caller's own projected history" (what the branches reach). **Fixed** (S3 redesign, cycle 1): `q/resolve` counts a snapshot only if the viewer's branches reach it (a reachability check in the viewer graph), in both steps; and a history page (the thin-clone form of `history`) starts only from snapshots the branches reach, so an old version is "not found" and `evolog` ends where a full clone's does. (Cycle 2 moved the second half to the client, where names and pages can be told apart: BUG-1319.) | The server's lookup answers from every snapshot it has a row for, not from the history the branches reach. Fix: keep only snapshots reachable from the viewer's projected branch tips (a reachability check in the viewer graph, bounded like the rest of the query), in both steps. | `server_hub` `thin::s3rd_a_thin_clone_names_what_a_full_clone_names_after_a_rewrite` |
| BUG-1269 | important (fixed; **introduced** by the S3 redesign, `q/resolve`; guarantee 2: "the cap and its truncation reveal nothing hidden") | server / `q/resolve` | **`q/resolve`'s caps count rows the caller cannot see, so hidden and embargoed snapshots change the answer for a prefix they match.** *Snapshot ids:* it reads at most 17 `view_graph` rows with the prefix, withheld (embargo-line) rows among them, sets `more` from that count, keeps the first 16, and only then drops the withheld. With 16 visible snapshots `abcd…` and one embargoed `abcd0…` (withheld from everyone, admins too), the admin gets 15 snapshots and `more: true`, against 16 and `more: false` without the embargoed one: the answer tells that a withheld snapshot exists in that id range. *Change ids:* it reads at most 64 rows of the real `graph` (in no stated order; hidden changes among them), projects them and drops the hidden, and `more` says nothing of the rows it did not read. With 70 changes of `fin/` (hidden from devs and anyone) whose change ids share the prefix of a visible change, anyone and a dev get "nothing matched" for that prefix, where the same project without the hidden changes names the visible one. A thin clone then says "revision … not found" or resolves a prefix a full clone calls ambiguous. Attacker: a person without access to `fin/` (or anyone, for an embargo); they control the prefix; they learn how many hidden or withheld snapshots fall in an id range. **Fixed** (S3 redesign, cycle 1): `q/resolve` reads rows in a fixed order a chunk at a time, drops what the caller cannot see (withheld rows in the query, unreached ones, hidden changes) before counting, and stops at 17 matches that count: the answer, its bound and `more` depend only on what the caller sees. | A limit applied to rows before the visibility filter (the class of a cap counted on what the caller cannot see). Fix: filter first and cap after, over rows of the caller's own history only (for change ids, an index of the viewer graph by change id rather than the real graph), and set `more` only from rows the caller may see. | `server_hub` `query::s3rd_resolve_caps_reveal_no_withheld_snapshot`, `query::s3rd_resolve_of_a_change_prefix_ignores_hidden_changes` |
| BUG-1290 | important (fixed; **introduced** by S3; guarantee 3 of the redesign: "no code outside `repo.rs` can read history without choosing `Held` or `Exact`; every `Held` use may differ without being wrong") | thin clones / history types | **Rewrites of history a thin clone does not hold leave the change's descendants behind, `vl split` of it refuses, and the served `log` lists only what is held.** In a fresh thin clone of 8 commits, `vl describe -r <commit 1>` makes a new "commit 1, renamed" and leaves commits 2 to 7, `main` and `@` on the old one (a full clone rebases them all); `vl abandon`, `vl squash -r` and `vl rebase -s` of an old change likewise move nothing above it; `vl split -r <commit 1> data` fails with "snapshot … is no longer in the history (it was rewritten meanwhile)". `vl serve --local`'s `log` method lists 3 entries where `vl log --json` lists 9 (the reference promises the same document). The type split is not closed: `Repo::graph` (and `repo.graph` inside `veil-core`), `visible_among`, `visible_embargoed` and `store().snapshot` read held history without choosing a type. `Transaction::rebase_descendants` finds what to move with `graph.down_to` from the view's refs (held: it stops at the boundary, `transaction.rs:556`); `commands::check_current` asks `visible_among` (held, `commands.rs:201`); `api::log_entries_with` with no ids walks `held().visible_iter()` (`api.rs:917`), which `serve.rs:1611` reaches through `api::log` outside any `Exact`. **Fixed** (S3 redesign, cycle 1): `Repo::graph`, `visible_among`, `visible_embargoed` and the index are private to `repo.rs`, and `ObjectStore::snapshot` to the engine; `Held` and `Exact` carry them (`visible_among`, `visible_embargoed`, `range`, `reachable_among`, `entries_matching`, `embargoed_among`, `generation`, `down_to`). `rebase_descendants` uses `Exact::generation` and `Exact::down_to`, `check_current` `Exact::visible_among`; the served log is `vl log`'s (`api::log_entries_with`). | History reads outside the two types, and a `Held` read where the answer is shown. Fix: make `Repo::graph` and the untyped walks (`visible_among`, `visible_embargoed`, `merge_bases`…) private to `repo.rs` behind `Held`/`Exact`; the descendant walk of a rewrite and `check_current` run under `Exact` (bounded by the rewritten snapshots' generation, BUG-1291); `api::log` takes the exact walk `vl log` takes. | `server_hub` `thin::s3rd_rewrites_of_unheld_history_match_a_full_clone`, `thin::s3rd_serve_log_in_a_thin_clone_is_vl_log` |
| BUG-1291 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3; the redesign's claim "a walk pages only what its own range reaches (bisect: from `bad` down to `good`)"; scale, S3's purpose) | thin clones / history paging | **Every `Exact` walk that reaches a snapshot beyond the boundary pages in that snapshot's whole ancestry, however small the range.** In a thin clone of 40 commits whose server pages 2 snapshots at a time, each in a fresh clone: bisect's candidates between the tip and 5 below, `x..y` over the same 6 snapshots, `Exact::range`, `is_ancestor` either way, `merge_bases` and `common_ancestor` of the tip and a snapshot 4 below each read 20 pages, the whole history. At real scale (2,000-snapshot pages) `vl bisect --good <a recent snapshot>` in a 1M-snapshot project fetches 500 pages. The history index's walks stop by generation, and a snapshot's generation is computed from every ancestor, so the first walk that needs the lower bound's generation pages its ancestry down to the root. **Fixed** (S3 redesign, cycle 1): a thin clone's history index takes the generation of each snapshot at its boundary from the server (`q/generations`, protocol revision 6: the viewer graph's, the same arithmetic), so a walk never needs the ancestry below, and pages in only what its range reaches. Without the server an `Exact` walk fails; a `Held` one goes on with a lower bound it never persists. `is_ancestor` of a snapshot outside the person's history is false without a walk; `common_ancestor` is the newest merge base. | A held history index whose stopping rule needs generations, which a thin clone can only have for snapshots whose whole ancestry it holds. Fix: take generations from the server's history pages (the viewer graph has them) or stop range walks by reaching the excluded snapshots rather than by generation; test the page count of each `Exact` walk on a short range. | `core_sync` `thin::s3rd_exact_walks_page_in_only_their_range` |
| BUG-1292 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3; guarantees 4 and 5; a confusing failure, recoverable) | thin clones / remotes | **`vl remote rm origin` in a thin clone leaves it without a server, and the same project added back under another name cannot be read either.** The removal succeeds; `partial.remote` still names `origin`. `vl remote add up <same URL>` and `vl pull up` (another remote: "a full pull", §13.21) pull 0 objects, because the snapshots are held while their trees and files are in the cache or evicted. After an eviction, `vl cat -r up/main <file>` under local work fails with "'/' is not fetched yet, and this command has no connection to the server of this thin clone", `vl show main---` with "has no connection to its server"; `vl gc` and `vl fsck` report nothing wrong; only `vl partial full` names the remedy (`vl remote add origin …`). **Fixed** (S3 redesign, cycle 1): `vl remote rm` of the remote a thin clone fetches from is refused ("make it a full clone first, `vl partial full`"); a full pull from another remote walks what its snapshots reach even when it holds the snapshots. | Removing a remote does not look at the `partial` marker, and "a pull from another remote is a full pull" fetches only what the main store lacks by snapshot, not their trees and files. Fix: refuse to remove (or follow a rename of) the remote a thin clone fetches from, saying how to make it a full clone first; and make another remote's full pull fetch what the snapshots reach into the main store, as the design says. | `server_hub` `thin::s3rd_removing_a_thin_clones_remote_leaves_it_readable_or_is_refused` |
| BUG-1293 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3; threat 11, the cache's bound; scale) | thin clones / cache bound | **A `vl ws switch` away from a workspace whose files were fetched copies all of them into the main store, which is never evicted.** A thin clone switches to workspace `other` on `big` (400 KB fetched into `.veil/cache/`), then back to `default`: `.veil/objects/` grows by about 400 KB; `vl ws rm other` and `vl gc` keep them (the op log reaches them). `vl new big` and `vl new main` in the same clone copy nothing. The snapshot taken of the directory as it leaves a workspace writes files the cache already holds into the main store (`put_raw` "always writes it"), so the cache's bound does not bound what a thin clone keeps on disk, and every workspace an agent switches through stays. **Fixed** (S3 redesign, cycle 1): a working-copy snapshot reuses an unchanged plain file (the parent's id at that path, held in either area) without writing it, also when it rescans; `vl partial full` then copies into the main store what only the cache holds, for every tree the history it keeps reaches. | The leaving snapshot writes unchanged fetched files as if they were local work. Fix: the working-copy snapshot of a switch writes a file only when no area holds its id (the cache counts), as the snapshots of `vl new` here evidently do (they copy nothing; the write path that differs was not traced); local work, which is new content, still goes to the main store. | `server_hub` `thin::s3rd_a_workspace_switch_does_not_copy_fetched_files_into_the_main_store` |
| BUG-1294 | important (open; **pre-existing**: reproduced on `integration` 6fa552c as on the S3 branch, found by `verify-fast.sh s3e`; a lost update) | op log / lock-free commits | **Under load, a lock-free commit's tag names a tree without the file the commit wrote.** `core_durability` `metadata_lock::grant_racing_lock_free_commits` (three workspaces each commit three new files and tag each commit, while key-ring grants and a pull run in other handles) fails about one run in 70 with the machine's load near 100, always on the memory backend: tag `c0-1` names a tree of `["f0-0", "f0-2"]`, `c1-2` one of `["f1-0", "f1-1"]`. Stress, six runs at a time: 3 failures in 360 runs of the branch, 1 in 330 of `integration`. It passes alone. Not traced: a concurrent operation's merge of op heads that either resets a workspace's working copy to an older one (so the next commit lacks the previous file) or moves a tag onto a rewrite that does. | Not traced. | `core_durability` `metadata_lock::bug_1294_lock_free_commits_keep_their_files` (200 rounds of the race; under load) |

**Guarantees that hold (tests):** a thin clone answers as a full clone for `@-`, `..x`, `x..`, long `-` steps past the boundary, an ambiguous and a unique change id prefix of unheld history, a tag named like an id, `vl evolog` of an old change and `::x` (`server_hub` `thin::s3rd_a_thin_clone_answers_as_a_full_clone_for_more_revision_forms`); `vl status`, `vl log` and `vl files` after a pull (`thin::s3rd_status_and_log_after_a_pull_match_a_full_clone`); `vl new`, `vl edit`, `vl duplicate`, `vl cherry-pick`, `vl restore --from`, `vl rebase -s @` and a merge onto unheld history (in `thin::s3rd_rewrites_of_unheld_history_…`); `vl redo` and `vl undo` of a switch whose target's files were evicted fetch within the bound or record nothing, and the directory holds what it is attached to (`thin::s3rd_redo_of_a_switch_past_the_cache_bound_records_nothing`); a full pull from a fork, a local commit, a pull of the clone's own server, a rebase onto it, an eviction and the fork's removal leave `vl gc` complete and `vl fsck` clean, with everything named readable (`thin::s3rd_gc_completes_across_a_second_remote_…`).

**Not filed:** the CLI's revsets are `X`, `A..B`, `::B`, `..B` and `A..` only (`docs/reference/log.md`): `x::y` and `heads()` do not exist in either kind of clone, so there is nothing to compare.

### S3 redesign, cycle 2

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep), cycle 2 of the revised design, of the cycle 1 fixes (`t3/ebed8889` @ `23319df1`; new diff `57ec179..23319df1`: `5156b670`, `197c326d`, `23319df1`). The merge with `integration` @ `6fa552c4` conflicted in code (`crates/veil-server/src/api.rs`, the route list: `q/generations` against `q/search` and `q/grep`; `crates/veil-core/tests/core_security/adversarial_remote.rs` and `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/adversarial_s2.rs`, guarded tests the integration sweep rewrote against this branch's `exact()` and `store().snapshot` renames; `docs/HUB.md`), so it was aborted and the branch reviewed alone. Four findings: BUG-1316 is introduced by the BUG-1291 fix and BUG-1319 by the BUG-1268 fix (it passes with that fix's `sync.rs` hunk undone), BUG-1317 is a route of BUG-1269's class its fix left open, BUG-1318 is BUG-1292's second half, not fixed (the cycle 1 reproduction returns early when the removal is refused, so it never ran that half). Reproductions: `server_hub` `thin.rs` and `query.rs`, tests named `s3rd2_…`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1316 | important (fixed; **introduced** by the BUG-1291 fix, `q/generations`; BUG-866's class; guarantee 2: a thin clone answers as a full clone) | thin clones / history index | **Past a far-future timestamp, a thin clone's rewrite leaves the change's descendants behind.** A member (a dev, write access to `src/` only) pushes a snapshot dated `i64::MAX` (the push accepts any timestamp, BUG-866), then three ordinary commits `after 0..2` on top. In a fresh thin clone, `vl describe -r <after 0>` makes `after 0, renamed` and leaves `after 1`, `after 2`, `main` and `@` on the old version; a full clone rebases them all. The server's generations clamp a timestamp to `MAX_STAMP` (`i64::MAX / 4`, `query/graph.rs:105`) and the client's do not (`graph_index.rs` `Walker::entry`, `above.max(s.timestamp.max(0))`). A thin clone takes its boundary's generation from the server (`Repo::boundary_generation`) and computes everything else itself: the tip gets the server's `MAX_STAMP + 3`, the commit below it, paged in later, the client's `i64::MAX + 1`. A parent's generation above its child's breaks every walk that stops by generation: `Exact::down_to` from the view's refs stops at the tip, below the floor of the rewritten change (`transaction.rs` `rebase_descendants`), and `reachable_among` (so `is_ancestor` and `check_current`) stops at a child whose generation is below the one it looks for. The two also differ for a snapshot with no parents (client 1, server 0), so a chain of snapshots dated 0 is off by one the same way. Attacker: a member who can push to any folder; they control the timestamp; the harm is a wrong result in everyone's thin clone (a rewrite that loses descendants, wrong ancestry), never in a full clone. **Fixed** (S3 redesign, cycle 2): one function, `veil_core::graph_index::generation` (the timestamp clamped to 0 ..= `MAX_STAMP`, `saturating_add`, a root 0), used by the client's history index, the server's real graph (`GraphRow::compute`) and every viewer graph (`VRow::compute`); index layers of the older arithmetic void the index (`VEILCG02`, cycle 3: BUG-1381). | Two arithmetics for one value: the server's (clamped, root 0) and the client's (unclamped, root 1), mixed in one index by the BUG-1291 fix. Fix: one arithmetic, the server's (clamp the timestamp to `MAX_STAMP`, `saturating_add`, no parents 0) in `graph_index.rs`, with a format note if persisted entries change; or take every generation of a thin clone from the server. | `server_hub` `thin::s3rd2_a_far_future_timestamp_does_not_split_a_thin_clones_history`, `thin::one_generation_arithmetic::client_and_server_generations_agree` (a property test: the three agree on random histories, far-future, negative and equal timestamps, several roots) |
| BUG-1317 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by the S3 redesign, `q/resolve`; a route of BUG-1269's class its fix left open; guarantee 1: errors and timing reveal nothing beyond the caller's history) | server / `q/resolve` | **A hidden snapshot no branch reaches changes `q/resolve`'s answer for a change id prefix it matches: `warming` instead of the visible change.** In a project where `fin/` (hidden from security) has a change `abcd00…` that was rewritten (its first version stays in the real `graph`; no branch reaches it), while another fill of security's view key runs (another server's lease, a long first fill), `resolve_prefix` with the prefix of a visible change `abcdff…` answers `503 warming` after its deadline; the same project without the hidden change names the visible change at once. The change step still reads the real `graph` by change id (every snapshot ever derived, hidden changes and old versions among them) and projects each row it reads (`ensure`) before it drops what the caller cannot see: a row with no projection for the caller starts a fill and waits for it. What does not count costs work and fills in proportion to the hidden rows with the prefix, bounded only by the deadline (2 s), whose error then also depends on them. Attacker: a person without access to `fin/` (or anyone, on a public project); they control the prefix; they learn whether hidden history they cannot see matches it (and cause fills of hidden snapshots no branch reaches). **Fixed** (S3 redesign, cycle 2): every viewer graph row has a row of `view_changes` (migration 21, `view_graph_changes`: keyed by project, view key, change id and snapshot, with its flags, written by the fills first; viewer graph rows written before it are emptied and filled again), so the change step reads the caller's own rows by change id, never the real `graph`, and starts no fill but the branch tips' that every query makes; each step reads at most `Limits::work` rows, past which the request fails asking for more of the prefix. | Rows of the real graph read and projected before the caller's visibility is known (BUG-1269's class: the fix moved the count after the filter but kept the real graph as the source). Fix: the cycle 1 suggestion, an index of the viewer graph by change id (`view_graph` rows carry the projected snapshot; add its change id), so only the caller's own rows are read, and none is projected on demand. | `server_hub` `query::s3rd2_resolve_answers_alike_whatever_hidden_history_it_meets`, `query::s3rd2_resolve_reads_a_bounded_part_of_the_callers_graph` |
| BUG-1318 | medium (fixed; **introduced** by S3; BUG-1292's second half, which its fix claims: "a full pull from another remote walks what its snapshots reach even when it holds the snapshots") | thin clones / remotes | **A pull from another remote whose tips the thin clone holds fetches nothing.** In a thin clone of a project with a branch `big` (400 KB of files the clone never read), `vl remote add up <same URL>` and `vl pull up` put 0 bytes into the main store. `hub::pull_with` walks held snapshots of such a pull (`held && !main_only`), but asks the server only for the tips the store lacks (`want_tips`: `widen || !store.has(t)`), and a thin clone holds every tip of its own server: nothing is asked, nothing walked. Reads still work through `origin` (its removal is refused now), so the harm is the claim: what such a pull brings is in the cache or nowhere, and `HUB.md` §13.21 says it is a full pull. **Fixed** (S3 redesign, cycle 2): a pull into the main store (a widening one, or a full pull from another remote) asks for every tip, held or not; `have` skips, object by object, what the main store holds. | The fix changed the history loop's skip, not the request that feeds it. Fix: in a `main_only` pull, ask for every tip (as `widen` does), and keep the per-object `have` check on the main store. | `server_hub` `thin::s3rd2_a_pull_from_another_remote_puts_what_its_snapshots_reach_in_the_main_store` (every object `up`'s tips reach is in the main store; its byte bound is the packs' compressed size) |
| BUG-1319 | important (fixed; **introduced** by the BUG-1268 fix, `sync::history`; guarantee 2: a thin clone answers as a full clone made at the same time) | thin clones / history paging | **After anyone rewrites pushed history, a thin clone made before cannot read the history below its own old tip, and shows its parent as withheld.** A thin clone and a full clone of 6 commits are made; the admin runs `vl describe -r <first change>` and `vl push --force` elsewhere; neither clone pulls. In the thin clone, `vl log --json` lists `commit 5` with its parent `"withheld": true` and nothing below; `vl show main--` and `vl show main-----` fail with "object … is not present in this store"; the full clone shows `commit 3` and `commit 0`. The same holds for a pulled clone whose `@` or local work still stands on the old versions. The fix makes a history page start only from snapshots the viewer's branches reach (`sync.rs`, `reached_from_branches`), so a page asked for at the parent of a snapshot the clone holds (an old version now) is empty, and the empty answer reads as "not in your history" (`Missing`), a redaction. The old versions are the person's own projected history (they were sent them): nothing is withheld, the answer is wrong. **Fixed** (S3 redesign, cycle 2): two rules. A history page starts from any snapshot of the caller's viewer graph that is not withheld, reached or not (`query::page_starts`). A name is what the branches reach, and what the snapshots the clone names in `q/resolve`'s new `from` reach (its own refs on the server, each the caller's own id: a real id of a hidden snapshot is left out, BUG-1070's class). On the client, `Repo::deepen` asks for a page only where a full clone made now holds the snapshot (`Repo::may_page`): a parent of a held snapshot, or a name the server's branches, or the clone's refs and operation log, reach; divergent change ids choose the version the clone's own heads reach exactly. A predecessor `vl evolog` follows to an old version nothing reaches is not found, as in a full clone. | The rule of BUG-1268 ("an old version is not found") belongs to names (`q/resolve`, an id typed), not to paging below what a clone holds. Fix: keep `history` pages from any snapshot of the viewer's graph, and apply "the branches reach it" where a name is resolved (`Exact::snapshot` of a name not reached from what the clone holds or the server's tips), so a full clone made at the same time and a thin one agree. | `server_hub` `thin::s3rd2_a_thin_clone_reads_its_own_history_after_a_rewrite_elsewhere`, `thin::s3rd2_a_thin_clone_made_before_a_rewrite_pulls_it_as_a_full_clone`, `query::s3rd2_names_keep_to_the_branches_and_pages_to_the_viewer_graph`, `thin::s3rd_a_thin_clone_names_what_a_full_clone_names_after_a_rewrite` |

**Guarantees that hold (tests):** `q/generations` answers only rows of the caller's viewer graph (`None` for no row or a withheld one), at most 1,000 per request, with the client's arithmetic but for BUG-1316; `q/resolve`'s snapshot step filters withheld rows in SQL and unreached ones before counting (`query::s3rd_resolve_caps_…`, `s3rd_resolve_of_a_change_prefix_…`). Descendant rewrites (`describe`, `abandon`, `squash`, `rebase -s`, `split`) of unheld history match a full clone (`thin::s3rd_rewrites_of_unheld_history_…`), and bisect, `x..y`, `Exact::range`, `is_ancestor`, `merge_bases` and `common_ancestor` page in only their range (`core_sync` `thin::s3rd_exact_walks_page_in_only_their_range`). The public store read of a snapshot beyond the boundary fails (`Unavailable`), never answers held history as the person's (`core_sync` `thin::s3rd2_no_read_of_history_outside_held_or_exact`). The unchanged-file shortcut needs a public parent entry of the same kind, mode and content id, after the secret scan: a fetched file made executable after a switch round trip is recorded (`thin::s3rd2_a_rescanned_fetched_file_whose_mode_changed_is_recorded`). Removing a thin clone's own remote is refused with the way out, and the way out works (`thin::s3rd2_removing_a_thin_clones_own_remote_is_refused_with_the_way_out`).

**Not filed:** the type split is closed in effect, not to the letter: `ObjectStore::get` and `get_raw` still compile outside the engine (they fail beyond the boundary, above), and the engine's `ObjectStore::snapshot` is read outside `repo.rs` in `transaction.rs` (`fetch_ahead_move`), `remote.rs` (`ancestors_in`, `push_closure`, `unusable_target`), `gc.rs`, `fsck.rs` and `maintenance.rs`, each where held history is the right answer. A held walk now asks the server for one boundary generation per request (`boundary_generation` sends one id; the route takes 1,000).

Three findings, all **introduced** by the cycle 2 fixes; properties 1 (names and pages show each viewer only their own history) and 5 (a pull from another remote fills the main store) hold. Reproductions: `core_engine` `graph_index::bug_1381_…`, `server_hub` `startup::s3rd3_…` and `thin::s3rd3_…`; property 1's evidence: `server_hub` `query::s3rd3_resolve_from_roots_is_projection_equivalent` (passing).

### S9 cycle 1

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of milestone S9, the regional cache (`t3/88fba7f4` @ `a7e05e6` on `228eb1b`, merged with `integration` @ `3f84531`; one hand-resolved conflict, two route additions side by side in `api.rs`): `crates/veil-server/src/cache/`, `POST /v1/cache/epochs` and `hub-cache-token`, `skip` in `grant.rs` and `veil_core::hub::grant::BatchRequest`. All three findings are introduced by S9, and none leaks an object. Reproductions: `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/cache.rs`, module `s9_adversarial` (the container suite, `scripts/verify-server.sh`).

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1180 | medium (**fixed**, S9 cycle 1; introduced by S9; denial of service of coalescing, by anyone on Earth; the large-object half needs no attacker) | server / regional cache / coalescing | **Fixed:** a request marks only objects whose chain checked and whose recorded size the store keeps (at most 16 MiB), at most 256 of them; a mark is let go once its object is kept, every mark once the server's answer has passed, and every mark before the request waits for the budget, or for its client past 100 ms, so a stalled client holds none for longer (a grace added after `verify-server` caught a client's momentarily full channel giving the marks up before its object was kept: 24 requests for 24 readers). **A request marks an object in flight whether or not its fetch can help anyone, and keeps the mark until its own client has read the whole answer.** (a) An object larger than the store's largest (16 MiB) is never kept, yet its fetch is marked: every concurrent reader waits for it (up to `FLIGHT_WAIT`, 2 s), then asks the server anyway (measured 2.08 s for a 17 MiB public file while another reader's client was slow). (b) After one want misses a tree, every later want of the batch is planned for the server and marked, including ids nobody has. One batch from anyone on Earth (100,000 wants are allowed, 65,536 marks fit), whose client stops reading, fills the in-flight map for as long as it likes: coalescing then stops for every project (24 readers of a new root: 24 requests to the server; at most 3 with the same request without the 70,000 random ids). | `decide_joined` (`cache/mod.rs:437-451`) marks every planned want with no size, whatever its size or whether its chain was checked, with no share per request; the mark (`Flight`) is dropped only after `answer` or `forward_get` has sent the last byte to the client (`mod.rs:694-698`, `815`), not when the object is kept or the server's part of the answer has passed. | `server_hub` `cache::s9_adversarial::bug_1180_readers_wait_on_a_fetch_of_an_object_never_kept`, `…::bug_1180_one_stalled_request_fills_the_in_flight_map` |

Each connection's HTTP/1 write buffer is 64 KiB (HTTP/1.1 only), a write pending 30 s closes the connection, and at most `--max-connections` (1,024) are open: the cache holds at most `--memory` + about 128 KiB a connection (≈ 384 MiB with the defaults).
