Fix: once an id is planned for the server, do not plan it again from the store; the server places it. | `server_hub` `cache::s9_adversarial::bug_1182_a_repeated_id_keeps_the_servers_order` |

**Held up** (tested or traced):
- **No object the server would not give.** Every path that serves from the store goes through `decide`: the grant verifies under the grant key the feed last named, `usable` (project, expiry) and `request_signed` (the grant's device, over every want's id in order, `skip` included) before the epochs, the epochs before any chain, and a chain before any object lookup (`Chains::check`, the server's own, over trees reached from the grant's root only, each read hash-checked from the store, or from decoded trees that were). A batch's answer serves only planned ids, a `GET` only the URL's id. A refusal is final only if every tree it read was held (`missed`, shared across the request, which can only make later refusals not final). Entries are keyed by project name and id; projects cannot be renamed or deleted, so a name always means one project. The builder's tests pass here (five viewers, anyone on Earth included, cold and warm, every real hidden id with every chain).
- **Coalescing hands nothing over.** A request that waited decides again from the start (grant, signature, epochs, chain) with its own grant; what the fetcher kept is served only if the waiter's own chain reaches it.
- **The bound on removal.** A key's confirmation is its poll's send time, taken before the request, and the feed's statements run after it, so an access change committed at R is in every confirmation dated after R; polls run one at a time, a stale answer never moves a confirmation back, keys added after a poll began are not confirmed by it, and each project and device is matched by its own name in its own map. Freshness uses the cache's monotonic clock only, so clock skew with the server cannot stretch it. The feed reads the same rows as `Grants::current` (a removed or pending device left out, a person's epoch through the device's person). Without an answer for 5 s nothing is served from the store, public included; a server error, a timeout, or a partial answer confirms nothing (`the_cache_fails_closed_without_the_feed` passes). Epochs are rows in the database, so a server restart changes none.
- **`skip`.** Unsigned and applied by the server after the grant and signature checks, over the wants only: it can only shrink an answer. A status never depends on it.
- **Statuses and bodies.** The cache checks in the server's order (grant header, id, chain, signature, then the grant) with the server's own error constructors; a refused chain is the server's `404`, a refused batch want is left out. Timing tells only which trees and objects the asker may read are in the store (design row 14, accepted): a hidden final id is never looked up.
- **Integrity.** `Store::put` keeps only bytes whose hash is their id, written to a temporary file and renamed; `Store::get` hashes on every read and removes a mismatch (a flipped byte, a torn or truncated file). The open at start keeps files by name and length only, which is safe since every read hashes. A hostile upstream's frames are relayed as sent (the server is trusted) and kept only if wanted, at most 16 MiB, and matching their id.
- **The token.** `hub-cache-token` is made with `create_new` and mode 0600, compared through its BLAKE3 hash (constant time), checked before the body is read; a session, even an admin's, is refused.

**Not filed:**
- **What a stolen cache token gives** (a cache is trusted, row 11): for any project name, whether it exists, and its epoch; for any device key, whether it is active, and its person's epoch, so devices of one person are linked by an equal value, and polling shows when each project and person had an access change. There is no rotation but replacing the file and restarting the server and its caches.
- **Clock skew of the cache's wall clock** (operator configuration): grant expiry and request skew are checked against it. A cache far behind accepts expired grants, but only while both epochs are current, so only what the holder may read now; a cache far ahead refuses valid grants (`401`) instead of passing them to the server.
- **`--upstream http://…`** is accepted: the token and the grant key would cross the network in clear, and an attacker on the path could name its own grant key. The design and docs say `https://`; refusing other schemes is a one-line guard.
- **Unverified, the server's own `GET /v1/objects/…`** holds the whole object while a slow client reads it, with no read-ahead share; whether the server's object cache shares those bytes was not checked.

### S9 cycle 2

Review cycle 2 (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of milestone S9's cycle-1 fixes (`t3/88fba7f4` @ `7210ded`, merged with `integration` @ `6bcd09a`; one conflict, in this file, both sides kept): `crates/veil-server/src/cache/` (`deadline.rs` included), the listener limits in `lib.rs`, `docs/HUB.md` §13.18. All three findings are introduced by the cycle-1 fixes or by S9, none leaks an object, and each is a denial of service of the cache by anyone on Earth. Reproductions: `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/cache.rs`, module `s9_cycle2` (the container suite, `scripts/verify-server.sh`).

**Held up** (tested or traced):
- **Same answers as the server** (BUG-1182's class). A wider property, `the_caches_answers_are_the_servers_for_every_viewer_and_project`, passes: 4 viewers (anyone on Earth, a developer, finance, the admin), 2 projects (the cache holding random parts of both), wants naming the other project's ids under its trees and ours, ids the viewer may not see under their real chains and under the viewer's trees, repeats under refused chains, random `skip` lists, and `GET`s with ranges; 120 batches and 328 `GET`s, statuses and bodies the server's. The fix's rule (an id wanted again after a want only the server decides forwards the whole batch) is checked before the chain, so it also covers a repeat after a not-final refusal.
- **Only permitted objects are served.** The new code serves only `Plan::Local` ids of a plan `decide` made (grant, signature, epochs, chain), and a `GET` only the URL's id after its check; the BUG-1182 rule only forwards more. Not new: an answer decided while the epochs were confirmed may wait for the budget (or a slow client) and read from the store later than 5 s after an access change, as the server's own streams do once decided (the code before cycle 1 waited for the budget after deciding too).
- **Memory, the other buffers:** the index and the decoded trees (a quarter of `--memory` each), the in-flight map (at most 65,536 marks), connections in the TLS handshake (bounded by the cap and the 20 s limit), answers relayed from the server to clients that stall: `a_cache_process_with_stalled_clients_stays_within_its_bound` runs `veil-server cache` as its own process with 192 stalled clients of cold objects at `--memory 64M`: +4 to +6 MiB (the kernel's socket buffers take most of each answer). By reading the code (not measured), a connection may hold more than 128 KiB: the HTTP write buffer (up to two slices), rustls's outgoing records (64 KiB by default), the HTTP read buffer (64 KiB) and, while its answer waits for the budget, the chunk read from the server (up to the HTTP client's read buffer, about 400 KiB).
- **No circular waits** apart from BUG-1185: marks are let go before any wait for the budget, and after 100 ms of waiting for a client. The coalescing tests (`concurrent_readers_…`, both `bug_1180_…`) pass as 8 copies at once: 1 request to the server for 24 readers in every copy.
- **A cut-off body is an error:** `a_get_cut_off_after_its_head_is_an_error_for_the_client` (an object removed from the store after its `GET`'s head went out) ends the chunked answer without its last chunk, and the client's read fails (`Peer disconnected`), never a short `200`. A batch leaves out an object it lost, and its clients ask again. No `vl` code reads through a cache: `vl` fetches through `/v1/projects/{p}/fetch`, checking each part's count, ids and hashes (`hub.rs` `fetch_each`); there is no S3 promisor yet; the bench's reader (`veil-bench` `load.rs`) hash-checks frames (`read_frames`) and asks again for what is missing.
- **Fail closed** (`the_cache_fails_closed_without_the_feed`) and removal within the bound (`a_removed_person_is_refused_at_the_cache_within_the_bound`) pass as 8 copies at once; the connection cap and deadlines are on the client side only, so polls of the feed never wait for a slot.

### S24 cycle 1

The review of S24 part A (branch `t3/ba501622` @ `627292f1`, merged with `integration` @ `6b65ed62`), against six properties (a client within its limits is never refused; one project's or client's load cannot hold another past a stated bound; memory within the budget; every connection slot back in bounded time; refusals reveal nothing; existing behaviour unchanged). All introduced by S24. Reproductions in `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/limits.rs` (the container suite, `scripts/verify-server.sh`), each ignored until fixed. Also: BUG-1332's scope is wider than its row says: a forwarded batch carries no session, so every batch a cache forwards, signed-in readers' too, is read in the anonymous pool under the cache address's one quarter (32 MiB in flight for the whole cache), not only anonymous readers' requests.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1333 | medium (**fixed**, S24 cycle 2; **introduced by S24**; denial of service of every request with a body: one signed-in person, or anyone on Earth from four addresses) | server limits / request bodies (`limits/body.rs`) | **Fixed** (S24 cycle 2, `limits/body.rs`): a body's share grows as its bytes arrive (declared or not), so a head with no body holds nothing; small bodies (a declared 1 MiB or less: sign-in, most pushes, fetches) grow in a reserve of an eighth of the budget that no large body takes; a body must bring at least 8 KiB/s in every 20 s window after the grace (besides 16 KiB/s on average) and holds at most ten minutes of its last window's rate, so a slow client holds in proportion to its rate and one that stops is cut off within a window. A large signed-in upload still grows past its quarter while it is all its device holds (a 50 MiB file at `--request-memory 64M`, a 40 MiB pool, lands). **A few slow bodies hold a whole pool of the request budget, and every other body on the server is then refused `busy`.** A body of declared length takes its whole share before any byte arrives and keeps it for as long as it takes at the minimum rate. (a) One signed-in upload larger than its quarter takes the whole signed-in pool: at `--request-memory 64M`, one person's 50 MiB upload on a slow link makes someone else's push of one small file, in another project, wait 10 s and fail "the server is busy". At the defaults that is any upload over 384 MiB (a large file `vl push` sends as one body), for as long as it takes: a 400 MiB file at 10 Mbit/s holds every push and pull on the server for five minutes. (b) Four addresses, each within its quarter, hold the anonymous pool with request heads alone (`content-length: 32 MiB`, no byte sent), and every sign-in on the server waits 10 s and is refused `busy`, for 20 s + 32 MiB / 16 KiB/s (35 minutes) at 64 KiB/s in all. The design's "one client holds at most a quarter of its pool, so one cannot refuse the others" does not hold: one (signed-in) or four (anonymous) can. | `Pools::read` acquires `want(declared)` (up to the whole pool) before reading and holds it until the answer is made; `claim` lets a signed-in device past its quarter while it holds nothing else; the anonymous pool is shared by everyone on Earth with only a per-address quarter. Suggested fix, for the class: a declared body takes its share as it arrives (as a chunked one does), so a slow body holds what it has received; a body larger than a quarter of its pool is not buffered under it (an upload streamed to storage, or refused with "split it", as `HUB.md` §4.7's "larger: split"); and small bodies (a few KiB: sign-in, push, fetch) keep a reserve no large body takes. | `limits::bug_1333_one_slow_large_upload_refuses_every_other_signed_in_body`, `limits::bug_1333_four_addresses_holding_bodies_refuse_every_sign_in`; the two reproductions (their checks of the held shares now that a body holds what has arrived), `limits::a_push_of_one_file_larger_than_the_signed_in_pool_lands`, `limits::body::tests::a_head_without_its_body_holds_nothing`, `…::small_bodies_have_a_reserve`, `…::slow_bodies_are_cut_off_in_proportion_to_their_rate` |

## Adversarial pass: S14

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of milestone S14, blame and file history (`t3/84ec247f` @ `8860257` on `9cddf93`, reviewed merged with `integration` @ `3f84531`): `query/files.rs`, `derive/blame.rs`, the fill hook in `query/graph.rs`, `query/trees.rs` (rename pairing), the routes in `query/mod.rs` and `api.rs`, `veil-core`'s `map_lines`, migration `0015_file_history_and_blame.sql`. All four findings are introduced by S14; none leaks. Tests: `server_hub blame::s14c1_adversarial::*`.

### S14 cycle 1

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1210 | medium (a wrong result, for good; needs an S13 server running beside S14 after migration 0015, which a rolling restart is and `db::migrate` supports, **fixed**, S14 cycle 1 fixes) | server / file history, viewer-graph fills, migration 0015 | **Fixed:** a viewer-graph row is read as present only with `files` set (`view_graph.files`, migration 0015), which S14 sets when it writes the row, after the row's file history; an S13 server's insert never sets it. So an S13 row is not filled for S14: S14 fills it again (its file history first) and marks it (`ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE SET files = TRUE`), and every row S14 reads as present has its file history and so do its ancestors. `View::key` is unchanged. The reproduction now writes exactly the state an S13 server leaves (the row unmarked, no file history, not in this server's cache) and gets c2's line and c2 in the history; `s13_filled_graphs_are_filled_again_with_file_history` unmarks every row of a project and drops its file history (an S13 fill), lands one more change, and every viewer's blame and history equal the model's. **A viewer-graph row without file-history rows is trusted as if it had them, so blame and history answer from an older version silently, and every later landing builds on the gap.** Migration 0015 drops the S13 graphs (`DELETE FROM view_graph`) so that S14 fills them again with file history. But an S13 server still running (a rolling restart: `db::migrate` only reads a current schema, so the S13 servers keep serving) goes on filling viewer graphs, writing graph rows only. An S14 fill of the next landing then finds those snapshots present and reads their file history from the database (`Fill::intro`, `Files::intro`): it finds none, so its `prev` names the version before. Nothing marks or detects such a row, and nothing fills it again (rows are a cache that is never re-validated). Reproduced by writing the state an S13 fill leaves (one snapshot's graph row without its file-history rows), then landing one more change with S14: the blame of `one/two/three` gives line 2 to c3 (it is c2's) and the history lists c3 and c1, missing c2. No error, on either database. | `query/files.rs:146` (`Fill::intro`: a parent the fill did not compute is read from the database, trusted because its graph row exists) and `query/mod.rs:731`/`:772` (`Files::intro` on the same assumption); `migrations/0015_file_history_and_blame.sql:36` (invalidation by deleting what an older server keeps writing). Suggested fix (also closes BUG-1211): make the S14 graphs a key space an S13 server never writes, instead of deleting S13's: e.g. a new domain for `View::key` (and a new name than `admin` for the admins' key), so S13 and S14 servers fill disjoint rows and an S13 row is never read; drop the `DELETE` (old rows are garbage for the purge, §8). | `bug_1210_graph_rows_without_file_history_give_silently_wrong_answers` |
| BUG-1211 | medium (no S14 server starts; YugabyteDB with the graphs of a few large projects, **fixed**, S14 cycle 1 fixes) | server / migration 0015 | **Fixed:** migration 0015 rewrites no rows: it adds the nullable `files` column (BUG-1210) instead of deleting the S13 graphs. Measured: the migration over 300,000 graph rows in 0.5 ms (PostgreSQL) and 108 ms (YugabyteDB, about 41 million rows within the statement timeout; was 3.1–6.7 s). **Migration 0015's one `DELETE FROM view_graph` cannot finish within the 15 s statement timeout on a server with many graph rows, so the migration fails and no S14 server starts.** `migrate_once` runs each migration in one transaction on a pooled connection, under `db::STATEMENT_TIMEOUT` (15 s); the cancellation (57014) is retryable, so `migrate_locked` repeats the same doomed statement until `MIGRATION_DEADLINE` (10 minutes) and gives up. Measured over 300,000 graph rows: YugabyteDB 3.1–6.7 s (about 45,000–95,000 rows/s: 0.7–1.4 million rows within the timeout, the graphs of three to seven projects of 20,000 snapshots and 10 view keys); PostgreSQL 0.11–0.13 s (about 34–40 million). The test's bar is 10 million rows. It is the first migration that rewrites data; earlier ones only create tables. | `migrations/0015_file_history_and_blame.sql:36`; `db.rs` runs it under the pool's statement timeout. Suggested fix: BUG-1210's (no data rewrite in a migration: new view keys need no `DELETE`); otherwise delete in batches outside the migration transaction. | `bug_1211_migration_0015_cannot_finish_on_a_large_server` (fails on YugabyteDB; passes on PostgreSQL) |
| BUG-1212 | medium (denial of service of one file's blame, for good; anyone on Earth asks; a long history, or a pusher's renames, makes it, **fixed**, S14 cycle 1 fixes) | server / query `blame` | **Fixed:** the walk down is bounded by its own work (`BlameLimits::walk`, 20,000 rows, objects and trees read) and by the memory bound, and when it stops (on either, or on the deadline) it keeps where it got to: the deepest versions still to walk (`blame_walks`, at most 64). The next request follows those walks down to the deepest version not kept yet and blames it first, keeping it, then goes back up; so every request leaves a kept version or a deeper walk. The reproduction answers within its 40 requests. **A blame keeps its progress when it stops while computing, but not when it stops on its walk down to the versions it starts from, so a first blame whose walk down passes the deadline never answers.** The design says "each request is bounded and the work is never lost". `Blamer::run` first walks down from the version asked for to kept versions or the file's first version (one `view_file_history` read per version, and with `follow` a projected diff and rename pairing of each version that added the file), holding it all in memory, and only then computes upwards. A deadline (or the memory bound) during that walk leaves `last` empty and nothing to write, so the next request walks the same way and stops in the same place. Measured (PostgreSQL, debug): a file renamed at each of 400 changes, `follow`, a walk down of 220 ms and a deadline of 55 ms: 40 requests, 40 `deadline`, 0 kept blames. With the 2 s deadline, the same happens to a file with tens of thousands of versions (fewer with renames, or on YugabyteDB). | `query/files.rs:549`–`575` (the walk down keeps nothing); `:529`–`537` (`blame` keeps only `last`, set by the upward pass). Suggested fix: bound the walk down (e.g. by a count of versions or a share of the deadline), and when it is cut, blame the deepest versions it reached first, keeping them, so that each request leaves a kept version for the next to start from. | `bug_1212_a_blame_stopped_on_its_walk_down_never_makes_progress` |
| BUG-1213 | medium (BUG-1076's class; anyone who may push to a folder shows it; ordinary for long paths or many open branches, **fixed**, S14 cycle 1 fixes) | server / query `history` | **Fixed:** a history cursor longer than 8 KiB, or of more than `Limits::cursor` versions, is kept by the server in `log_cursors` (keyed by view key and the hash of its text; the log's TTL and per-project byte cap) and handed out as `frontier-<hash>`; a page ends before its frontier would pass `Limits::frontier` versions or 1 MiB of cursor text. The reproduction pages to the end (a cursor of 41 bytes). **A file-history cursor can be longer than a request can carry, so the history cannot be paged past it, for everyone who sees the file.** The cursor names every version still to walk, path included (`snapshot.hex(path)`: 66 bytes plus twice the path's length), up to `Limits::cursor` (1,000) versions, and the route takes it in its URL. A request line carries at most 64 KiB (the `http` crate's `Uri` limit, which the server and every Rust client share). So the cursor passes it at about 22 open versions of a file whose path has 1,500 bytes (a path may have 4,096), 246 of a 100-byte path, and 1,000 versions of any path is up to 8 MB. Measured: a 1,500-byte path changed on 30 branches and merged: the first page's `next` has 92,519 bytes, and the next request fails before it is sent (`InvalidUri(TooLong)`). The log has had the fix since BUG-1076 (wide cursors kept by the server in `log_cursors`); history did not take it. | `query/files.rs:771` (`cursor`: paths inline), `:838` (bounded by a count of versions, not by bytes); `query/mod.rs:758`. Suggested fix: as the log: keep a cursor past a small size in `log_cursors` (keyed by view key and its hash) and hand out its key. | `bug_1213_a_history_cursor_is_longer_than_a_request_carries` |

**What held up** (tested, or traced at `file:line`):
* **No leak found.** Blame and history read only the viewer's graph and `view_file_history`, written from their projected trees (`Fill::add`: `t.roots_of`, `changes::diff` on projected trees), so a hidden path or change is never in a row; an origin is a projected snapshot and a readable path. Hidden and missing paths, and cursors naming hidden or missing versions, take one code path. Kept blames are keyed by the view key, a hash of every rule's path and read bit (`View::key`), so they are shared only by viewers who read exactly the same paths (and see the same projected history); a removed member's key changes, so blames kept before are never found under it. Blame objects are put in the project's object store, but the object routes serve only objects reached from a granted chain (`grant::reached`), which a blame object never is.
* **Boundary cuts:** a file moved back out of a hidden folder is added for the viewer (its `prev` is the deletion, which holds no lines; the rename source is not in their trees), so lines edited in hidden history are the moving change's, with no hidden change, path or line number shown.
* **Fills:** the rows are a function of the projected history. `Fill::intro` trusts its own rows only along a first-parent run it computed (`fresh`), and below the run reads what is written; a parent another fill wrote has its file history first (`Walk::flush` writes file history before graph rows, statement by statement). A fill interrupted between the two leaves rows that the next fill writes again identically (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`). Embargo lines (`FLAG_EMBARGO_LINE` propagates to every descendant) get no rows, so no `prev` points into one.
* **Secrets:** `blame` refuses a start entry that is not `Public`; any version read (`texty`, then `Trees::content`) must be labelled `Public` and be a plain blob object, so a mislabelled object holds no lines. History lists a secret's entries only.
* **Bounds otherwise:** 4 blames at once per process, each request's diff work, the 2 s deadline; history pages by `n`, bytes and work.

**Not filed:**
* **Kept-blame storage and memory:** every version asked for is kept, per view key and `follow`, and nothing purges them (accepted in the design: bounded by history, purge §8). The `writes` buffer (up to 31 kept blames of up to 8 MiB each, copied again for the upload) and the walk's windows and nodes are outside the 64 MiB `held` bound; it needs a crafted file of hundreds of thousands of lines with fragmented origins, and the deadline cuts it.
* **Residual timing** from kept blames shared by view key, and the background cost of a fill (one projected diff per new snapshot and view key): accepted in the design.

### S14 cycle 2

Review cycle 2 (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of milestone S14's cycle-1 fixes (`t3/84ec247f` @ `4ab1257`, merged with `integration` @ `0584d06`; conflicts only in `docs/BUGS.md` and `docs/HUB.md`, both sides kept): `query/files.rs` (`Blamer::resumed`, `run`, `walked_from`, `write_cuts`, `history_page`), `query/graph.rs` (the `files` mark), `query/mod.rs` (kept history cursors), `veil-core` `blame::map_lines` and `textmerge::fits_middle`, migration 0015. One finding; no leak. Tests: `server_hub blame::s14c2_adversarial::*`, `veil-core blame::tests::s14c2_trimmed_map_lines_equals_the_whole_texts_diff`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1215 | medium (**fixed**, S14 cycle 2 fixes; BUG-1212's class, not closed by its fix; denial of service of one file's blame, for good; anyone on Earth asks; a pusher's renames, or a long history, make it) | server / query `blame` | **Fixed:** a cut walk records what it expanded (each version's entry and the versions it came from) as well as its frontier, and no walk from a recorded version is made again. Each request follows the records down (one small read each) to the deepest unfinished place: it walks from a frontier version no walk started from (recording a deeper cut if cut), or, once a record's frontier is settled (kept, or not plain text), blames that record's versions from the record and keeps them. A version already kept costs no walk budget; kept-blame lists cost one read whatever their length; a version far below its path's rows read so far gets a window of its own instead of paging from the tip; every computed version is kept (no size cap: a blame is bounded by its file). So every `partial` answer keeps a version or records a deeper walk, never neither (while a first walk is still on its way down nothing below can be blamed yet). The reproduction answers after 9, 2 and 1 `partial` answers (walk budgets 150, 400, 1,000); `every_stopped_blame_leaves_progress` checks (kept blames, recorded walks) after every `partial` answer over chains, renames at every step with `follow` and wide merges with small walk and diff budgets, and that the final blame equals one unbounded request's. **A blame whose walk down passes its budget (`BlameLimits::walk`) can stall for good: once the deeper versions its cut walks recorded are kept, every request walks the same way again, is cut at the same place and answers `partial`, keeping nothing more.** A cut walk records only its frontier, the versions it had not expanded yet (`files.rs:679`, `blame_walks`), and `Blamer::resumed` (`files.rs:578`) blames the deepest of them not kept first. Nothing ever shortens the walk from the version asked for (or from any recorded version) down to its frontier: no version between them is ever blamed, since only the walk's own up pass would blame them. Once the frontier is kept, `resumed` picks that version again (`files.rs:595`), and its walk costs what it cost the first time (each request reads rows, windows, kept-blame lists and renames afresh), and the budget is checked before a version is expanded, kept or not (`files.rs:670`), so it is cut at the same version, the same frontier is written again (`ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE`, `files.rs:638`), and nothing is kept. Reproduced: a file renamed at each of 80 changes, blamed with `follow`, with a walk budget of 150 reads and a 120 s deadline: 11 cut walks and 1 kept blame after 12 requests, then the same `(1 kept, 11 walks)` and `partial` for each of the next 188 requests (budgets of 400 and 1,000 reads converge; whether a walk stalls depends on where its cuts fall). Measured there, the whole walk is about 15 reads a version, so the default 20,000 reads is passed by some 1,300 renamed versions with `follow`. A second route of the same cause, slow rather than stuck: a request's file-history window starts at the tip (`files.rs:263`), so reaching a deep frontier costs its depth in reads again each time; a file edited in each of 120 changes with a walk budget of 60 answered after 111 `partial` answers, one version deeper each (the default budget: files of over about 20,000 versions; past the deadline instead, the first expansion fails and nothing at all is recorded). `docs/HUB.md` §13.22 ("each request leaves progress") and phase-3 §12 say otherwise. | Progress is recorded as where a walk stopped, not as versions blamed, so the cost of reaching the recorded place is paid again in full by every request and never shrinks (step 5.6's lesson: the check must compare what keeps progress, here kept versions). Smallest fix for the class: each request must keep a version between the one it walks from and its recorded frontier, e.g. record with a cut the deepest versions it expanded (the frontier's children) as well, blamed once the frontier is kept, so that every request keeps a version and each walk from the start ends sooner; and count the walk's own reads, not reads of what is already known. | `server_hub` `blame::s14c2_adversarial::bug_1215_a_blame_whose_walk_down_passes_its_budget_never_finishes` |

**What held up** (tested, or traced at `file:line`):
* **Guarantee 1, the `files` mark (BUG-1210).** Every read of `view_graph` checks it: `G::row` (`graph.rs:220`), `G::present` (`graph.rs:270`, the fill's presence) and `warm` (`graph.rs:876`); `hub.query.rows` is filled only from `G::row`, so no cache holds an unmarked row, and nothing ever clears a mark (S13's insert is `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; no code deletes graph rows). A marked row's ancestors are marked (a fill walks down to marked rows and writes parents first). The row S14 keeps for an S13 row is S13's own (`DO UPDATE SET files = TRUE`), and `VRow::compute` is unchanged since S13, so it is the same row. New: `s13_rows_refilled_by_servers_at_once_equal_one_fill` (all rows unmarked, or those above a generation; 1, 3 and 6 servers refilling at once for every viewer) writes exactly one S14 fill's graph rows, all marked, and file history, on both databases; `s13_filled_graphs_are_filled_again_with_file_history` checks the answers.
* **Guarantee 2, apart from BUG-1215:** `blame_walks` and kept blames are read and written by view key, path key, `follow` and snapshot, and hold only versions of the viewer's own graph; a memory bound in the walk answers `partial` with its frontier kept; `Cx::db` does not check the request deadline, so a walk cut by the deadline is still written.
* **Guarantee 3 (BUG-1213):** inline cursors are at most 8 KiB and 1,000 versions, kept ones `frontier-` and 32 hex digits; a kept cursor is looked up by project and view key. New: `kept_history_cursors_answer_only_their_viewer_and_project` (another viewer, and the same history in another project, get `invalid cursor`). An inline cursor's versions must be rows of the viewer's graph in this project.
* **Guarantee 4:** `textmerge::fits_middle` is `fits` on the whole texts by construction (`ids_fit` strips the same shared ends itself and is given the same line count); the trim is exact because diffy strips the shared ends before its search and its compaction only moves an edit past lines equal to its own. New: `s14c2_trimmed_map_lines_equals_the_whole_texts_diff`, 40,000 cases of few distinct lines, runs of the edge line inside the middle, CRLF and bare CR, empty texts and no final newline, plus texts straddling the work limit (both sides seen), against the pre-trim answer. `vl blame` uses the same function.
* **Guarantee 5 (BUG-1211):** `bug_1211_…` runs 0015 on a database `db::migrate` already brought to 0015, where `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` does nothing, so it no longer measures the table's change. New: `migration_0015_adds_its_column_in_bounded_time_beside_s13_servers` drops the column, then runs 0015 over 300,000 rows while four S13-style writers and readers run: 2 ms on PostgreSQL and 127 ms on YugabyteDB, the S13 statements failing at most with retryable errors (a few on YugabyteDB, which S13's `Cx::db` retries).

**Not filed:**
* **Kept history cursors share the log's per-project cap** (32 MiB): one may now be 1 MiB (a log's at most about 650 KB), so a few wide histories paged at once push other viewers' kept cursors out sooner (`invalid cursor`, the page asked for again from the start). BUG-1076's accepted design.

### S14 cycle 3

Review cycle 3 (the last; layer 3, tier A, Deep; new diff only) of milestone S14's cycle-2 fixes, BUG-1215 (`t3/84ec247f` @ `5e3f9c6`, merged with `integration` @ `6fa552c`, no conflicts): `query/files.rs` (`Blamer::resumed`, `next_work`, `settled`, `walked_from`, `segment`, `run`, `keep`, `Files::find`'s re-anchoring) and migration 0015's `blame_walks.expanded`. Three findings, all costs; no leak, no wrong answer. Tests: `server_hub blame::s14c3_adversarial::*`.

Nothing is persisted between requests but kept blames, so nothing is redone: whatever the deadlines, the job blames each version once (`bug_1216_…`: 150 versions blamed at deadlines of 25, 40 and 60 ms, as by one request from nothing; `s14c3_blames_resumed_at_once_on_two_servers_…`: two servers together blame each version once). **A resumed blame walks again (or blames again from its record) a version it has just blamed, up to 32 times in one request: the stated "no walk is made twice" and "reaching recorded progress costs one small read per record" do not hold.** When `resumed` finishes a piece of work below the version asked for (a frontier version walked to the end, or a cut walk's versions blamed from its record), that version's blame is only in the write buffer; the request's view of kept blames learns of it when the buffer is written, after 32 kept blames. So `next_work` finds the version unsettled again and does the same work again, round after round, until 32 have piled up. Measured (PostgreSQL and YugabyteDB, a 150-version chain): one unbounded request from nothing costs 432 reads; with walk budgets that cut the first walk, the request that finishes costs 1,206 (one partial answer before) and 1,880 (two). The reproduction: a 3,490-byte file at a 3,809-byte path, 13 kept blames, the largest 46,251 bytes (bound 51,264; was 1.56 MB), 334,209 bytes in all (was 11 MB). **A kept blame is not "bounded by its file, at most 1 MiB", and the kept blames a request computes wait in its write buffer outside the memory bound.** A kept blame object holds, for each origin, its snapshot id and path, and a run per stretch of lines: its size is the versions its lines come from times the path's length, not the file's size. Measured (both databases): a 3,490-byte file at a 3,809-byte path, 400 versions each adding a line: one request keeps 13 blames (the checkpoints and the version asked for), the largest 1,557,051 bytes, 11,272,401 bytes in all, every one held in the buffer until the request wrote them, against a memory bound of 8 MiB that the request never reported passing (`write` then copies the buffer again for the upload). Suggested fix: end a walk at versions an existing record already covers (follow that record instead), or bound what is recorded per file and view key (dropping the oldest records); and purge recorded progress with kept blames (§8). | `server_hub` `blame::s14c3_adversarial::bug_1218_cut_walk_records_grow_with_revisions_blamed_times_history` (ignored) |

**What held up** (tested, or traced at `file:line`):
* **Guarantee 1, termination and the invariant.** Every `partial` answer kept a new version or recorded a walk from a version no record starts at, and every blame finished with the answer of one unbounded request, on both databases: a 300-version chain, diamonds (a ladder of 40 two-sided merges, where a later walk re-walks versions an earlier record expanded), renames every few changes with `follow` and 7-parent merges that rename the file, a file deleted and re-added twice, versions holding a NUL byte though their entry says a small file (walked through, never kept, blamed as holding no line), and a 1,000-line file under a 160 KiB memory bound, with walk budgets of 25–90 reads and diff budgets of 1,500–40,000 (`s14c3_every_shape_finishes_with_progress_at_every_partial`, which also checks that partial answers stay within twice the viewer's file-history rows). The bound follows from the invariant: records start at distinct versions and kept blames are per version, so at most two partial answers per version. Records followed go strictly down the history (a record's frontier holds ancestors of its start), so `next_work` ends; a record's frontier holds every parent of every version it expanded that it did not expand (`run` pushes each parent not yet expanded, and the cut takes every unexpanded stack entry), so `segment` never meets an unsettled version. With the server's limits, `MAX_SEGMENT` (at most 2,048 × (256 + 4,096) bytes of node weight, about 8.9 MB) cuts a walk long before the 64 MiB bound could, so no record's segment starts above the memory bound (a walk cut by that bound would answer `too_wide` from its segment for good; only a test-sized bound reaches it).
* **Guarantee 2, per view key.** Every read and write of `blame_walks` and `blame_memo` binds the view key (`query/files.rs:557`, `:700`, `:722`, `:776`, `:972`). `s14c3_recorded_progress_is_read_only_under_its_view_key`: a file moved from `fin/` into `pub/` with hidden changes between, blamed with `follow` by anyone on Earth, finance and an admin: every record starts at, and names only, snapshots of its own viewer's graph and paths that viewer reads; with every other key's records and kept blames made unreadable, each viewer finishes with the answer of one unbounded request, and so does a finance member removed from finance (a new key; finance's records are never read under it).
* **Guarantee 4, concurrency.** Records are written `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and never changed, kept blames are content-addressed and a function of the version alone, and a record's versions carry what a fresh walk derives. `s14c3_blames_resumed_at_once_on_two_servers_keep_only_right_blames`: six requests on two servers, each with its own small budgets, resume the same blame at once (a chain, diamonds, renamed merges): all answer as one unbounded request does, no two records disagree on a version, and every kept blame is the object a request from nothing keeps for that version; 16 runs, 8 at once, all green.
* **Guarantee 5 otherwise:** a blame object is decoded with at most `MAX_LINES` lines, and only plain public blobs of at most 1 MiB are read, on every path.

### S14 speed (for S16)

Measured by S14's cycle-3 speed fixes (`blame_speed`, release, through `bench-quiet.sh`, 10,000 versions of a 5,000-line file). Precomputed blame meets its target (18.1 / 21.3 ms p99 for an admin, 25.4 / 40.4 ms for anyone on Earth, against 50 ms); the first blame does not.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1214 | low (**fixed**, S16; speed gate, not correctness: requests answer `warming` within their deadline and the job finishes in the background) | server / blame jobs | **Fixed (S16):** `Blamer::run` (`query/files.rs`) reads a path's `view_file_history` rows in pages up to 10,000, pre-warms pack indexes (`Objects::warm_packs`), loads version texts (`plain_text_line_ranges_from_parent`, reusing unchanged prefix/suffix line ranges from the previous version) and computes parent-to-child line diffs (`derive::blame::diff_parent`, with fast `isolated_replacements` for equal-length versions differing at isolated lines) in parallel across a worker pool over a sliding window of in-flight texts within `BlameLimits::held`, propagates blames in place (`step_mapped_in_place`) maintaining origin reference counts so dead origins are compacted immediately, and loads snapshot metadata (`Meta`) and generations only for origins referenced by kept checkpoints (`pending_keeps`). In a release build (`blame::bug_1214_a_first_blame_costs_more_than_its_gate`, 10,000 versions of a 5,000-line file from nothing), the first blame finishes in **430.2 ms (43.0 µs a version)** with objects on local disk and **526.6 ms (52.7 µs a version)** with objects in S3 (MinIO), both well under the 1 s (100 µs/version) gate. **The first blame of a long history misses its gate (1 s at 10,000 versions) by about 20×:** a job blames about 2.1 ms a version of a 5,000-line file, so 10,000 versions take 21.2 s (admin) and 23.1 s (anyone on Earth), the first answer coming after 17.9 s and 20.3 s. Interning origin paths once per job and spacing checkpoints by bytes (cycle 3's fixes) changed it little (27.4 s and 21.8 s before). | Each version is read, decoded and line-split, and diffed against its parent version one after another on one thread (`Blamer::run`, `derive::blame::step`, `veil_core::blame::map_lines`); not profiled further. Suggested: compute the line maps of a job's version pairs in parallel (each depends only on its two texts; only their composition is sequential), and keep each version's line hashes beside it so that a diff neither reads nor hashes its text again. | `server_hub` `blame::bug_1214_a_first_blame_costs_more_than_its_gate` (un-ignored; timing gate asserted under `cfg(not(debug_assertions))` at 10,000 versions) |

### S14 redesign

Review cycle 1 of S14's redesign (layer 3, tier A, Deep): first blames as background jobs, and the bounded kept blames (`t3/84ec247f` @ `fa2504f4`, the commits after `962fe94d`, merged with `integration` @ `ebabc15c`, no conflicts): `query/files.rs` (`Blamer::run`, `keep`, `write`, `kept_blame`, `kept_answer`, `wait_for_blame`, `leased_job`), `derive/blame.rs` (`Meta`, the stored form), `query/mod.rs` (`blame`), migration 0015 (`blame_memo`, `blame_paths`, `blame_jobs`). Five findings. No content leaks; one side channel shows the size of hidden files' blames. Tests: `server_hub blame::s14rd_review::*`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1306 | medium (**fixed**, S14 redesign review cycle 1; denial of service of every first blame on a server, across projects, for as long as its table of waiting jobs stays full; introduced by the redesign) | server / blame jobs | **Fixed:** a project fills only its own share of the queue and of the slots. At most `MAX_PENDING_JOBS` (256) jobs of one project wait per server, and 4,096 of all projects (`MAX_PENDING_ALL`); past that a project below its fair share (4,096 ÷ the projects with jobs waiting) still queues, up to 8,192 in all. The two slots are handed out in turn: a freed slot goes to the next project after the one last served that has a job waiting (first come first served within a project: `Slots`, `query/files.rs`), so another project's queue holds one back by at most one job a slot. A job waiting for another server's lease holds no slot (it takes the lease first), and every queued job ends: it waits at most `BlameLimits::wait` for a lease (BUG-1307), then computes in turn. The reproduction now passes (project two's first blame answers at its first request, beside project one's 256 waiting jobs), and `query::files::tests::slots_go_to_requesters_in_turn` (renamed in cycle 3) checks the order (a project queuing three jobs, then two others: the others are served first). **A first blame is not guaranteed to answer: while a server's table of waiting blame jobs is full, every first blame of any other key on that server answers `warming` and queues nothing.** `MAX_PENDING_JOBS` (256) counts every job in the server's `waiting` map, whatever its project or viewer: jobs waiting for one of the two slots, and jobs waiting for another server's lease (each stays up to `JOB_WAIT`, 600 s, polling every 250 ms). Past it, `wait_for_blame` answers `warming` without queuing (`query/files.rs:922`), so a caller whose key is not in the table only gets in when an entry ends and its own request happens to arrive first. Nothing gives a project, a viewer or a long-waiting caller a share. Reproduced: 256 jobs of one project wait on leases another live server holds; a 10-version first blame of a second project on the same server answers `warming` to all 145 requests over 30 s. | The bound is one global count with no share per project or per caller, and a refused request leaves nothing that would admit it later. A request that finds the table full gets the same answer as one whose job is running ("try again"), so a client retrying cannot tell starvation from progress. Smallest fix for the class: bound the table per project (and per viewer) as well as per server, and admit a refused key in order (for example a bounded queue of keys refused so far, served first), so every caller gets in within a bounded number of jobs. | `server_hub` `blame::s14rd_review::bug_1306_a_full_job_table_starves_other_projects_blames` (un-ignored), `query::files::tests::slots_go_to_requesters_in_turn` (renamed in cycle 3) |
| BUG-1307 | medium (**fixed**, S14 redesign review cycle 1; duplicate work, not a wrong answer: kept blames are a function of their version and written `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; introduced by the redesign) | server / blame jobs, `blame_jobs` | **Fixed:** a job computes only while it holds its key's lease. It takes the lease first and renews it every 30 s while it waits for a slot and while it computes; it checks the lease at every version it walks or blames (`Blamer::stopped`), and stops (`warming`) once a renewal finds the row taken over (no row updated), or once the lease's end, less 20 s for clocks (`JOB_MARGIN`), passes without a successful renewal (`Lease::live`). A job that does not get the lease within `BlameLimits::wait` (600 s) ends `warming` without computing; the next request starts a new one. The reproduction (with a 20 s wait, watched for 60 s) blames nothing, and `query::files::tests::a_lease_not_renewed_is_not_live` checks the stop. **"One job per (view key, version, `follow`) across servers" does not hold: a job that waited `JOB_WAIT` (600 s) for another server's live lease blames the version itself, without any lease.** `leased_job` polls the lease until `JOB_WAIT` (`query/files.rs:1002`); when it never gets it, `leased` stays false, no renewal starts (`:1009`), and the job goes on to take a slot and blame anyway (`:1029`), beside the holder. A holder is still live 600 s on when its job is slow, or when it took the lease and then waits for one of its own server's two slots (the lease is taken before the slot), which a full table (BUG-1306) makes up to 256 jobs long. The same class, rarer: a holder whose renewals stopped (its `UPDATE` result is ignored, `:1014`) for more than the 120 s lease keeps blaming after another server took the lease over. Reproduced: a lease held and renewed by another live server; after 600 s this server's job blames the version (20 versions blamed). | A job does not stop when it does not hold its key's lease: the end of waiting is treated as a lease. Smallest fix for the class: blame only while holding the lease. After `JOB_WAIT`, end the job (`warming`; the next request starts a new one), and stop a job whose renewal finds the lease gone. Taking the slot before the lease would also keep a queued job from holding a lease it cannot use. | `server_hub` `blame::s14rd_review::bug_1307_a_job_blames_a_version_another_server_still_holds` (un-ignored; a 20 s wait, `BlameLimits::wait`, watched for 60 s), `query::files::tests::a_lease_not_renewed_is_not_live`, `blame::s14rd2_review::s14rd2_a_job_that_loses_its_lease_mid_walk_stops` (cycle 2: a job losing its lease mid-walk) |
| BUG-1308 | important (**fixed**, S14 redesign review cycle 1; a side channel across view keys: the size of other people's kept blames, a function of hidden files' lines and the changes that wrote them; not their content; introduced by the redesign's per-project cap) | server / kept blames, the project's cap | **Fixed:** each view key has its own cap (`KEPT_BYTES`, 32 MiB a view key): a write drops its own view key's oldest kept blames past it and nothing of any other key's, so which of a viewer's blames stay kept is a function of their own key's blames alone. A project keeps at most 32 MiB × its view keys in use, and the view keys are bounded by the distinct access combinations of its people (groups and grants), not by agents (a narrowed agent session has its person's key). Checkpoints are spaced to about 8 MiB a job (`JOB_CHECKPOINT_BYTES`, a quarter of the cap). The reproduction passes: anyone on Earth's kept blames are the same after an admin's blame of a 5-line or a 600-line hidden file. **Which of a viewer's kept blames survive depends on files they cannot read.** The project's cap (`KEPT_BYTES`, 256 MiB) is shared by every view key and drops the oldest blames first (`query/files.rs:809`). So when someone who reads `fin/` blames a file there, the bytes of that blame decide how many of anyone else's kept blames are dropped. A viewer can see whether their own blame is still kept (it answers from the kept blame, or it starts a new job: `warming`, then `work`). That shows them the size of a blame of a hidden file (about 100 bytes an origin plus the changes named), so roughly its line count and number of authoring changes. Phase-3 §12's residual (row 4) allows only "that such a person blamed that file". Reproduced: two projects that differ only in `fin/ledger.txt` (5 lines, or 600 lines from 100 changes); anyone on Earth blames a public file at 24 revisions (9 kept under a 96 KiB cap); an admin blames the hidden file; 8 of anyone on Earth's blames stay kept in the first project, none in the second. | The cap is per project, while what it holds is per view key: eviction makes one key's state depend on another's. Smallest fix for the class: make what a viewer can observe a function of their own key alone, e.g. cap kept blames per (project, view key) (the bound becomes the cap times the project's view keys, which the policy bounds), or a per-key share of the project's cap. | `server_hub` `blame::s14rd_review::bug_1308_which_kept_blames_survive_depends_on_hidden_files` (un-ignored) |
| BUG-1309 | medium (**fixed**, S14 redesign review cycle 1; denial of service: one of a server's two job slots for a whole walk to the memory bound per request, repeatable; anyone on Earth who may read such a file; introduced by the redesign) | server / blame jobs | **Fixed:** a job that passes the memory bound records it (`blame_ends`, migration 0015: view key, version, `follow`, and the bound passed), and a request of that key under a bound no larger answers `too_wide` from the record (one statement, with the check for a kept blame: `settled`) without starting a job; a job waiting for another server's lease also stops on it. The record stays true: a version's history below it never changes, and a change of access is a new view key. A view key keeps at most 4,096 (its oldest dropped). The reproduction passes: 4 requests, 4 `too_wide`, 1 job. **A blame past the memory bound walks the file's history again at every request.** A job that passes `BlameLimits::held` on its way down keeps nothing (`run` fails before it blames any version; nothing records how it ended), and the job is removed from the table when it ends (`query/files.rs:934`). With the server's limits a walk to the bound is some 200,000 versions (more reads a version with `follow`), so each request holds one of the server's two slots for that whole walk. The projector's trees a rename search makes are dropped after each version (`Trees::forget_now`). The formula's base is now 128 bytes (`BASE_BYTES`): the header and an empty blame's JSON at the largest depth take 101, checked by `stored_blames_round_trip_and_stay_bounded`. Both reproductions pass: the job's peak memory under a 16 MiB bound, `follow` on the 3,000 renames at 3 KB paths, grows the process by 0.96 to 1.28 times the bound (2.58 times before), and it answers `too_wide`. (Corrected in the redesign review's cycle 2: the 0.96 first stated here was one run; phase-3 §12 has the measurement with warm caches.) **A blame job holds more than `BlameLimits::held`, and a kept blame can be larger than "64 + 128 a line + 768 a change".** Phase-3 §12 says a job counts "the walk's versions, texts, blames, interned paths and its write buffer" against the bound. The walk does not count the file-history rows it reads and keeps (`Files::windows`, `query/files.rs:215`), the rename map (`:502`), or the copies of each version's path in its stack, `order` and `edges` (`:651`, `:675`); `held` counts one path per version and one per parent (`:663`). Measured as the process's peak resident memory, reset just before one job: with `follow` on a file renamed at each of 3,000 changes at 3 KB paths, under a 16 MiB bound, +43 MB (2.58 times) before `too_wide`; 0.55 times with short paths and no renames. With the default 64 MiB that is some 165 MB a job and 330 MB for the two slots. Second, the kept-blame formula: an empty file's kept blame (no line, no change) takes 82 bytes, past the stated 64. The magic line is 21 bytes and the JSON skeleton about 60 (`derive/blame.rs:172`). | The bound counts estimates of some structures, not everything a job keeps; the formula's base was not measured. Smallest fix for the class: count every structure that grows with the walk (each window row as read, each rename entry, each path copy, or intern the walk's paths as the blames' are), and state the base as what encoding an empty blame takes (about 100 bytes), checked by a test at 0 lines. | `server_hub` `blame::s14rd_review::bug_1219_a_blame_job_holds_more_than_its_memory_bound` (ignored only to run alone, `--exact`: it measures the process's peak memory), `bug_1219_an_empty_files_kept_blame_passes_its_stated_bound` (un-ignored), `derive::blame::tests::stored_blames_round_trip_and_stay_bounded` |

**What held up** (tested, or traced at `file:line`):
* **Guarantee 1, a stopped server and a restart.** A lease left by a server that stopped mid-job is taken over when it expires (another server's job polls it every 250 ms), and the blame answers, each version blamed once: `s14rd_a_stopped_servers_job_is_taken_over_when_its_lease_expires` (a 3 s lease: answered after 3.06 s, 40 versions blamed). A restarted server has an empty table and does the same. A job that passes the memory bound answers `too_wide`, never `warming`, to the requests waiting on it (`bug_1309_…`'s first assertions); a kept blame dropped by the cap between a job's end and the request's read answers `warming`, and the next request runs a new job.
* **Guarantee 2 otherwise.** Within a server one task per key (`waiting`), and across servers the lease, as `s14c3_blames_resumed_at_once_on_two_servers_…` checks. Where it fails: BUG-1307 (and BUG-1309 for keys that fail).
* **Guarantee 3, kept blames and `blame_paths`.** Every read and write of `blame_memo` binds the view key (`query/files.rs:538`, `:584`, `:792`, `:952`) but the cap's `DELETE` (`:809`, BUG-1308). `blame_paths` is read only through the keys a kept blame of the viewer's own key names (`kept_blame`, `:584`). A path's key is 128 bits of a keyed BLAKE3 hash, and a viewer's blames name only paths of their projected trees, so no path of a hidden folder is reachable through another key's row (`s14c3_kept_blames_are_read_only_under_their_view_key` passes). The per-change metadata is the viewer's projected snapshot's (`Meta::of(g.snapshot(id))`, `:568`): `s14rd_blame_changes_show_what_the_viewers_log_shows` checks that each change a blame names shows exactly what that viewer's log shows (change id, author, date, first line of the description; a change of `fin/` and `pub/` included), for anyone on Earth, finance and an admin, and that the entries carry no `description`. Where it fails: BUG-1308 (the cap).
* **Guarantee 4 otherwise.** The per-server job count (2 slots) and queue (256 entries of a key each) hold. A kept blame of at least one line keeps within the formula with the hostile inputs `stored_blames_round_trip_and_stay_bounded` uses (400 changes, a 4 KB path, authors and summaries of characters JSON escapes); `first_line` turns every control character into a space, so JSON escapes at most double them. Per-project storage stays at the cap (`bug_1218_…`). `blame_paths` is outside the cap but holds each path once, at most the paths the project's history has. Not bounded by the stated per-server figure, and not filed: a request reading a kept blame decodes the whole blame (up to the 1 MiB file's lines) for each page, as S13's file reads hold one file.
* **Guarantee 5.** `query_projection_equivalence`, `blame_and_history_match_the_projected_files` and `blame_and_history_cut_at_the_boundary` are unchanged in what they compare (the redesign's one change to `query.rs` drops the `work` and `walk` budgets, which no longer exist, from the harness's small limits; pages of 3 lines remain) and pass on both databases.

### S14 redesign, cycle 2

Review cycle 2 of S14's redesign (layer 3, tier A, Deep; only the new diff): the cycle-1 fixes of BUG-1306 to 1309 and BUG-1219 (`t3/84ec247f` @ `4460d455`, on `integration` @ `6b65ed62`, no conflicts): `query/files.rs` (`Slots`, `Lease`, `settled`, `record_too_wide`, `leased_job`, `wait_for_blame`, the walk's accounting, the per-key cap), `query/mod.rs` (`keep_cursor`), `query/trees.rs` (`forget_now`), `derive/blame.rs` (`BASE_BYTES`), migration 0015 (`blame_ends`). Four findings, all introduced by S14 (not merged yet). Nothing leaks content; BUG-1410 lets one view key see that another's blames fill the project's queue. Tests: `server_hub blame::s14rd2_review::*`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1410 | medium (**fixed**, S14 redesign review cycle 2; denial of service of a project's first blames by any viewer of it, anyone on Earth included where a folder is public; a viewer's answer, an at-once `warming` and no job, shows another view key's activity; introduced by BUG-1306's fix) | server / blame jobs, the fair queue | **Fixed:** the share and the turn are a view key's of a project. At most `MAX_PENDING_JOBS` (256) jobs of one (project, view key) wait per server; past the server-wide 4,096 a view key below its fair share (4,096 ÷ the view keys with jobs waiting) still queues, up to 8,192. The slots go in turn by project, then within it by view key (`Slots`: two levels of turns), first come first served within a view key. So an at-once refusal is a function of the requester's own key's jobs (below the server-wide limit), and no view key of a project holds another back. The other limits of `wait_for_blame` and `Slots` were checked for the class: the server-wide limit and its fair share count view keys, not projects; nothing else is per project. The reproduction passes (finance's blame answers beside anyone on Earth's 256 waiting jobs), and `query::files::tests::slots_go_to_projects_and_view_keys_in_turn` checked the order (by requester since BUG-1553: `slots_go_to_requesters_in_turn`). Each project's share of a server's waiting jobs (`MAX_PENDING_JOBS`, 256) is shared by every viewer of it. Anyone on Earth fills it with blames of a public file: here each waits on a lease another server holds, as when that server's job is slow or waiting for a slot (each up to `BlameLimits::wait`, 600 s); 256 slow first blames in that server's own slots do the same. While the share is full, a member of finance's first blame of a 10-version file in `fin/` answers `warming` at once and queues nothing (292 requests in 30 s, no job). Within a project, slots are also handed out first come first served across view keys. | Fairness is keyed by the project, but the people who share it are different view keys, and a public project's outsiders are the whole world: the same class as BUG-1306 one level down. Key the share and the turn by (project, view key), so one view key fills only its own share and slots go in turn by view key within a project; the server-wide limits stay. | `server_hub blame::s14rd2_review::bug_1410_one_viewer_fills_the_projects_job_share_for_every_viewer` |

A checkpoint larger is not kept; a version asked whose blame is larger answers `too_wide`, recorded (`blame_ends` now records the cap too, so only limits no larger are answered from it), so the next requests answer at once without a job. A batch holds at most a quarter of the cap before it is written, so a batch and the one blame past it take at most half the cap; and the cap's `DELETE` counts the rows just written first and never drops them. The reproduction now checks the chosen behaviour: under a cap of half the blame, `too_wide` at the first request, one job, no walk again; under a cap of four times it, full of older blames of the key, the blame answers and the key keeps within its cap. The job ends `Kept`, the request reads no kept blame and answers `warming`, and every request after starts a new job that walks and blames every version again: 250 requests in 30 s ran 250 jobs and blamed 10,000 versions (a 12,071-byte blame of 40 changes under a 6,035-byte cap), with no answer. The stated bounds allow it with the real cap: a kept blame takes up to 128 + 128 bytes a line and 768 a change it names, a plain-text file of 1 MiB has up to 524,288 lines, so one kept blame can take 64 MiB and more, past the 32 MiB of `KEPT_BYTES` (some 60,000 lines from as many changes with full summaries do). | The cap's `DELETE` keeps the newest rows that fit, and a row larger than the cap never fits; nothing bounds one kept blame by the cap. A kept blame dropped by the cap only lengthens walks, so it never makes a record wrong. The reproduction passes: after every 5th version is kept, the head answers (5 versions blamed). A too-wide record is served after the kept blames below its version change so that the job would fit. Whether a job passes its bound depends on where its walk stops, at kept blames, and those are added (by blames of older versions, the natural way round a too-wide head) and dropped (the cap). A 400-version file is too wide from nothing under a 96 KiB bound; the viewer then blames every 5th version (each answers and is kept); the head still answers `too_wide` from the record, with no job. With the record dropped, the same request answers after blaming 5 versions. | The record's key (view key, version, `follow`, bound) leaves out what the outcome depends on: the kept blames below the version. One statement compares a digest of what view keys are a function of (policy, bindings, admins, members) with what `view_access` (migration 0015) last recorded; the one server whose update records the change computes the keys in use (`derive::view_keys`, the deriver's list, now shared with `memo_tips`) and drops the rest. **What held up** (tested, or traced at `file:line`):
* **Property 1, kept blames, kept cursors and too-wide records.** The cap's `DELETE`s bind the view key (`query/files.rs:888`, `query/mod.rs:376`, `query/files.rs:1207`); a cursor read checks its expiry (`query/mod.rs:396`), so the project-wide delete of expired cursors (`:369`) is unobservable; `settled` (`query/files.rs:1167`) reads only the requester's key. `bug_1308_which_kept_blames_survive_depends_on_hidden_files` and S13's `kept_history_cursors_answer_only_their_viewer_and_project` pass. Where it fails: BUG-1410 (the queue and slots are per project).
* **Property 2.** A stopped server's lease is taken over (`s14rd_a_stopped_servers_job_…`); another project at its share does not block (`bug_1306_…`, `slots_go_to_projects_in_turn`); a job waiting for another server's lease holds no slot (it takes the lease before `Slots::take`, `query/files.rs:1266`–`1310`) and ends after `BlameLimits::wait` (`bug_1307_…`). At the server-wide limit (8,192) every project is refused until jobs end, as stated. Where it fails: BUG-1410 and BUG-1411.
* **Property 3, the lease.** The job takes the lease before a slot, checks `Lease::live` before every version it expands and every step (`Blamer::stopped`), and the renewal runs on its own task, so a slow step does not lose it. `until` is set from the clock read before the statement, so a slow statement only shortens it. With servers' clocks less than 20 s apart, the holder stops before any other server can take the lease; beyond the margin, by Δ, they overlap for at most Δ − 20 s (the holder stops at its own `until` either way, or at its next renewal, which finds the row taken over). The overlap costs duplicate work only: a kept blame is a function of its key and is written `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, and a too-wide record takes the larger bound (`GREATEST`). `Lease::live` reads the wall clock: a backward step of the holder's own clock acts as skew. Not tested end to end: a running job that loses its lease mid-walk (it needs a job running past one 30 s renewal); `a_lease_not_renewed_is_not_live` covers `Lease` alone.
* **Property 4 otherwise.** A record answers only a bound no larger (`held >= $6`); a change of access is a new view key (`View::key` hashes every rule's read bit, `veil-core/src/hub/access.rs:211`); a version's file and history below it never change. Where it fails: BUG-1412.
* **Property 5 otherwise.** Each key's kept blames, cursors (32 MiB, rows of at most some 650 KB, expiring after an hour) and records (4,096) are capped. Per-job memory, run alone (`--exact`): the peak test passes its 1.5 times threshold, but measured 1.19 to 1.26 times the bound here (1.24, 1.22, 1.22 with objects in a directory, 1.19 on MinIO; 1.25 and 1.26 under 4 and 8 MiB bounds), not the 0.96 times that phase-3 §12 and the fix's commit state. The excess grows with the bound, so it is per version; a second job of the same file, with the server's object caches warm, raised the peak by 0.07 times, so the excess may be those caches (shared, and bounded on their own) rather than the job, though the allocator's reuse of the first job's freed pages blurs that second figure. Not filed; the stated 0.96 should be corrected, and the test should measure with caches warm to tell them apart. The empty-blame base (128 bytes) holds (`bug_1219_an_empty_files_…`).

### S14 redesign, cycle 3

Review cycle 3 (the last) of S14's redesign (layer 3, tier A, Deep): the cycle-2 fixes of BUG-1410 to 1413 (`t3/84ec247f` @ `48103d40`, on `integration` @ `3984695c`, merged in): the fair queue per (project, view key), one kept blame at most a quarter of its key's cap, too-wide records naming the paths their walks reached, `files::sweep_keys` and `view_access` (migration 0015, edited in place: S14's own, not on `integration`). Rows BUG-1553 to 1555; tests in `server_hub` `blame::s14rd3_review`. None leaks: what an answer shows stays the viewer's projected history.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1553 | medium (**fixed**, S14 redesign review cycle 3; denial of service of every outsider's first blames of a public project on a server, by any one outsider, account or none; an outsider's answer, an at-once `warming` and no job, shows another outsider's activity; introduced by BUG-1410's fix, which keys the share by view key) | server / blame jobs, the fair queue | **Fixed:** every share and turn is the requester's: the signed-in person who asked for the job first, or one pool for every caller without an account (`files::Requester`). A requester may have at most 256 jobs waiting per server, whatever projects and view keys they ask in, and that is the only at-once refusal, so it depends only on the requester's own jobs; slots go in turn by requester (`Slots`). Kept blames stay per view key. Residual, as decided: callers without an account share one share. The reproduction passes (the second outsider, signed in, answers at the first request); `query::files::tests::slots_go_to_requesters_in_turn` and `the_queue_refuses_only_on_the_requesters_own_jobs` check the turn and the admission. **One outsider fills anyone on Earth's job share for every other outsider.** The share of waiting jobs (`MAX_PENDING_JOBS`, 256) and the turn within a project are a (project, view key)'s (`query/files.rs:1227`, `:1231`), and every outsider of a project has one view key: anyone on Earth, and every signed-in person in none of its groups (a view key is a function of what is read, not of who reads). Phase-3 §12 gives the reason for BUG-1410's fix as "a public project's outsiders are the whole world", and the fix puts the whole world in one share. Reproduced: one outsider holds 256 blames of a public file (each waiting on another server's lease, as in BUG-1410's reproduction: a slow job elsewhere, up to `BlameLimits::wait`, 600 s each); a second outsider, signed in, with the same view key, asks a first blame of a 10-version public file: 293 requests in 30 s, all `warming` at once, no job queued. Within the share, outsiders' jobs are also served first come first served, so one outsider's 255 waiting jobs come before another's. The same holds for any view key many people share (every member of one group with no other grant). | The fair share's identity is the view key; what has to be isolated is the requester. A view key is the right identity for what is computed and kept (projections, kept blames: equal for equal read sets), not for who waits. Smallest fix for the class: count the share, and take the turn within a (project, view key), by requester: the signed-in person, or for callers without an account one share between them (or one per client address, if the server sees one); kept blames stay per view key (row 4's residual: a blame can find one that another person with the same read set computed). The server-wide count and its fair share then count requesters (BUG-1554). | `server_hub blame::s14rd3_review::bug_1553_one_outsider_fills_the_job_share_of_every_outsider` |
| BUG-1554 | medium (**fixed**, S14 redesign review cycle 3; denial of service of every first blame on a server, every project, by one signed-in person; introduced by BUG-1306's fix, kept by BUG-1410's) | server / blame jobs, the server-wide limit | **Fixed** with BUG-1553: one person's projects and view keys share their one share of 256. The server-wide `MAX_PENDING_ALL` (4,096) is a hard ceiling: at it a new job takes the place of the newest waiting job (not computing) of the requester with the most waiting, the furthest past its fair share, which ends `warming` where it waits (for a lease or for a slot; `Waiting::admit`, `Ticket`), so the ceiling never refuses a requester below its share. A job is marked computing under the table's lock, where refusals are made, so a computing job is never refused. The reproduction now checks the fixed behaviour: one person's second project queues nothing past their share; 16 people fill the ceiling; a 17th person's first blame answers. **One person's view keys fill the server-wide job limit for every project.** Past `MAX_PENDING_ALL` (4,096 waiting jobs) a view key below its fair share (4,096 ÷ the view keys waiting) still queues, but only while fewer than 8,192 wait in all (`query/files.rs:1231`): at 8,192 every request of a key not already queued is refused at once, whatever its share. Each project's admins are a view key of their own, and any signed-in person may create projects (`api.rs`, `create_project`), so one person reaches the ceiling alone: 16 projects at 256 jobs each, then 29 more at their shrinking fair shares (240, 227, … 45). Reproduced: one person's 45 projects of 128 files, each blame (with and without `follow`) waiting on another server's lease, bring the server to 8,192 waiting jobs; then another project's first blame of a 10-version public file answers `warming` at once to all 289 requests in 30 s, no job queued. The brief's "the same person under two view keys" is this route: each key a person has is a full share. | The fair share is defeated by the hard ceiling, and both count view keys, which one person multiplies at will (projects, or as an admin, rules naming accounts). Smallest fix for the class, with BUG-1553's: count shares by requester, so one person's projects and keys share one share; and at the ceiling, admit a requester below its fair share by refusing the newest waiting job (not yet computing) of the requester furthest past its share, so the ceiling never refuses one below it. | `server_hub blame::s14rd3_review::bug_1554_one_persons_projects_fill_the_server_wide_job_limit` (about 2 minutes: 8,192 requests) |
| BUG-1555 | medium (**fixed**, S14 redesign review cycle 3; a blame that never answers, for its view key, until a blame of a path its walk reached is kept by another job; a whole job's work lost each time; introduced by BUG-1309's fix, and not closed by BUG-1412's) | server / blame jobs, `blame_ends` | **Fixed:** the record is written only if no blame of the view key, `follow` and a path its walk reached (its own included) was kept at or after the job's start, less the lease's clock margin, in the same statement (`record_too_wide`: `INSERT … SELECT … WHERE NOT EXISTS`). That covers both routes: the job's own checkpoints, and another job's of the key while it walked. A job that keeps nothing (too wide on its way down) still records (BUG-1309). Phase-3 §12 now states the bound as measured (some 30,000 to 60,000 versions from nothing under 64 MiB, fewer with long paths or renames). The reproduction now checks the fixed behaviour: no record after the first job's 5 checkpoints, and the head answers on its third job. **A too-wide record outlives its own job's checkpoints.** A job that passes its memory bound on its walk up has already kept checkpoints of the path: written in batches as it goes, and the rest when it fails (`Blamer::blame`, `query/files.rs:717`: "what it kept is written, also when it fails"). Each of those writes drops the view key's records of the path that exist then (`Blamer::write`, BUG-1412's fix), but the job's own record is written after them (`leased_job`, `:1536`).
