The same class by a second route: another job of the key keeping blames of the path while this one walks (it read the path's kept versions once, at its first version: `Blamer::is_kept`) leaves the record it writes afterwards. Reproduced: a 600-version chain from nothing under an 800,000-byte bound: the first job blames 179 versions, keeps 5 checkpoints and records `too_wide`; 10 more requests answer `too_wide` from the record, with no job; with each record dropped, jobs from the checkpoints answer (453 versions blamed in all). | The record is keyed by the view key, version, `follow` and limits, but it is true only of the kept set the walk read, which writes change, the job's own among them; BUG-1412's fix drops records at the writes, which can come before the record they should drop. Smallest fix for the class: make the record conditional on the kept set it was made under, in the statement that writes it: insert it only if no kept blame of the view key, `follow` and a path it reached was written since the job read the kept versions (`created_at` at or after the job's start, less the lease's clock margin), which a job that kept checkpoints never passes (its next request makes progress). Phase-3 §12's "some 200,000 versions" then states the bound as measured. | `server_hub blame::s14rd3_review::bug_1555_a_too_wide_record_outlives_its_own_jobs_checkpoints` |

**What held up** (tested, or traced at `file:line`):
* **Property 1, other view keys, other projects, and within a view key.** Every share and turn is the requester's (`files::Requester`: the signed-in person, or one pool for callers without an account), and the only at-once refusal is when the requester already has `MAX_PENDING_JOBS` (256) waiting jobs (`Waiting::admit`), so a refusal depends only on the requester's own jobs and never reveals another person's activity (`bug_1306_…`, `bug_1410_…`, `bug_1553_…`, `bug_1554_…`, `the_queue_refuses_only_on_the_requesters_own_jobs`, `slots_go_to_requesters_in_turn`). Kept blames, records and cursors bind the view key in every read and write.
* **Property 2, no starvation and displacement.** Slots go in turn by requester (`Slots`), each requester waits at most 256 jobs, and at the server-wide ceiling (4,096) a new job takes the place of the newest waiting job (not computing) of the requester with the most waiting, never one with few jobs (`bug_1554_…`, `the_queue_refuses_only_on_the_requesters_own_jobs`, `displacement_spares_few_jobs_and_computing_jobs_and_releases_leases_and_slots`). Records answer only limits no larger than theirs, both the memory bound and the cap (`records_made_under_other_limits_answer_only_their_own`); with `follow`, a record is dropped by kept blames of the path its walk crossed a rename into (`a_follow_record_is_dropped_by_kept_blames_across_its_rename`); a blame past a quarter of the cap answers `too_wide` once (`bug_1411_…`).
* **Property 3, computing jobs, leases and slots.** A job is marked computing under the refusal lock (`waiting.lock()`), after checking `ticket.refused()`, so a computing job is never refused or displaced; a displaced waiting job ends `warming` where it waits (for a lease or for a slot) and releases its lease (`DELETE FROM blame_jobs … AND holder = $6`), its slot (`Slot::drop` / `Slots::give` skipping a cancelled waiter), and its table entry (`e.seq == seq` check) (`a_computing_job_is_never_displaced_and_a_refused_waiter_releases_its_slot`, `displacement_spares_few_jobs_and_computing_jobs_and_releases_leases_and_slots`, `s14rd2_a_job_that_loses_its_lease_mid_walk_stops`).
* **Property 4, `blame_ends` and `sweep_keys`.** A `too_wide` record is written only if no blame of the view key, `follow` and a path its walk reached (its own included) was kept since the job started (less the lease's clock margin), in the same statement (`record_too_wide`), and writes of kept blames delete matching records (`Blamer::write`), so a `too_wide` record never outlives what made it true (`bug_1412_…`, `bug_1555_…`, `a_follow_record_is_dropped_by_kept_blames_across_its_rename`, `a_too_wide_walk_down_records_nothing_when_another_job_kept_a_reached_path`). `sweep_keys` keeps every current key's rows (`sweeps_keep_every_current_keys_rows`, `sweeps_on_servers_at_once_keep_every_current_keys_rows`).
* **Property 5, projection equivalence and bounds.** The projection-equivalence harness on fresh seeds (`query_projection_equivalence`, `blame_and_history_match_the_projected_files`, `query_work_ignores_hidden_content` with `VEIL_QUERY_SEED=58200` and `68400` on PostgreSQL, `58300` on YugabyteDB): all pass. Per-key caps and the queue's bounds hold as stated (`bug_1308_…`, `bug_1411_…`, `bug_1413_…`, `bug_1306_…`, `bug_1410_…`, `bug_1219_…`).
* **Property 6.** All new and changed tests assert their primary action first before checking anything else.

## Findings from S15 (search, 2026-11-07)

None open. Departures and limits are in `docs/design/server/phase-3-server-history.md` §13 (unreferenced segments wait for S29's garbage collection; descriptions are not searched; path search over 11,111 matching names takes 24 ms at p99 against the 20 ms target).

## S15 cycle 1

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of milestone S15, search (`t3/782e8aab` @ `f01fe84` on `9cddf93`, merged with `integration` @ `6bcd09a`): `crates/veil-server/src/search/`, `migrations/0016_search.sql`, the hook in `derive::landing`, the routes `q/search` and `q/grep`, `vl search` and `Client::query`. No leak found: every finding is a cost or a wrong result. BUG-1230 and BUG-1232 are one class, **work a query does outside its deadline and bounds** (the deadline is checked only in the loop that reads candidates); the fix belongs where that work is, not in a new layer. All three are introduced by S15.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1230 | medium (**fixed**, s15b; denial of service; anyone on Earth who may read one long-lined file) | server / search `grep` | **Fixed:** a grep searches a file line by line and checks the deadline before each line; a line longer than its pattern allows (`Pattern::max_line`: `SCAN_COST` (2³¹) over the compiled pattern's size, a power of two from 1 KiB: 2 MiB for a literal, 16 KiB for the reproduction's 128 KiB pattern) is not searched, and the file counts it (`long_lines_skipped`), so no one search call can run past about a deadline's worth. The same `examine` serves the index and the scan. **One file's regular expression search runs to its end, whatever the deadline.** `(?-u)[\x00-\xff]*[a-f][\x00-\xff]{1000}[A-Z]` (41 bytes; compiles under the 1 MiB size limit) over a 1 MiB single-line file (a minified bundle) took 12 s in a debug build against the 2 s deadline at a branch tip (through the index); a scan at an old revision runs the same `examine`. In a release build, measured outside the server, `{4000}` took 9.8 s and `{8000}` 14.8 s for one MiB. The linear-time engine is linear in the haystack times the compiled pattern: a counted repetition of a class with no literal to skip by makes the lazy DFA give up and fall back to the PikeVM. Each request holds a blocking thread for seconds per file it is allowed to read (up to 20,000 a page). | `GrepPage::examine` (`search/mod.rs:515`) runs `is_match` per line with no deadline; `Work::tick` and `G::tick` are checked only between files (`search/mod.rs:594`, `query/trees.rs:167`); `REGEX_SIZE` bounds memory, not time. | `server_hub` `search::bug_1230_grep_pattern_cost_passes_the_deadline` |
| BUG-1231 | important (**fixed**, s15b; wrong result; not a leak) | server / search index | **Fixed:** every update also takes every branch whose code index or names walk is behind its tip, missing, or built under another policy (one statement; as BUG-982), a branch's failure no longer stops the others, the server resumes lagging projects at start (`index::resume`, after `derive::resume`), and a query whose branch's index is behind schedules its update and answers from the old snapshot with `behind: true` and `tip_id` (compared in the viewer's ids, so a landing they cannot see shows nothing). **The index follows only the branches an update was asked for, and nothing resumes an update that did not run.** (a) A name search answers "every path the project's history held", but the names index walks only branches updated since it began (a landing's moved branches, or the branch a query names): after an upgrade, a branch that has not landed since is never walked, and a path only its history held is not found. (b) An update that fails (its error is only logged) or is cut by a restart is resumed by nothing but that branch's next landing: queries keep answering from the old tip (they name it), as `search` and `grep` at `main` both do, for as long as the branch is quiet. S12 closed the same class for derivation (BUG-982: every landing takes every lagging branch, and `derive::resume` at start). | `index::landed` is called only from `derive::landing` with `stats.branches`, and from `search::shards` only when a head is missing or under other lines (`search/mod.rs:255`), never when it is behind its tip; `index::update` filters to the branches given plus the default (`search/index.rs:597`); no start-up resume. | `server_hub` `search::bug_1231_index_follows_only_the_branches_asked_for` |
| BUG-1232 | medium (**fixed**, s15b; denial of service; anyone on Earth, of a large public project) | server / search `search` | **Fixed:** candidates are taken one at a time: each segment's postings are intersected as they are decoded, within the range of `path` and the cursor (`Segment::range`), and the segments are merged in tree order (`Merge`), so a query reads only what comes before its bound; a word's document count for ranking saturates at 10,000 (`DF_CAP`, the same whatever the layout); a page is the best `n + 1` kept in a bounded heap; the deadline is checked every 4,096 postings and documents (`Budget`) and before each segment is loaded. The indexed grep takes the same path. **A query collects, deduplicates and sorts every candidate before its bounds and deadline apply**, so its time and memory grow with the viewer's shards, not with the 4,000 candidates (or 100,000 names, or a grep page) it reads. Over 300,000 public files (debug build), a code search for eight short words and a name search for `txt` took 1.8 s and 1.9 s against a 300 ms deadline, then failed with `deadline`: the deadline ends the request only after the work. §12's "code search stays under 200 ms however large the project" holds only while the viewer's matching documents are few (release timings at this size not measured): the collection is linear in them and holds a copy of each path. Before the loop, `Opened::open` also loads (and holds, apart from the 256 MiB cache) every segment of the viewer's shards, unbounded and with no deadline. A grep's indexed page collects and sorts every candidate after its cursor the same way (cheap only while they arrive sorted, as from one segment). | `code_hits` and `name_hits` (`search/mod.rs:374`, `:441`) and the indexed grep (`:582`) build the whole candidate list (`cands`), and `Opened::each` the per-word sets, with no tick; the bounds are applied to the sorted list afterwards. | `server_hub` `search::bug_1232_candidates_are_collected_past_the_bounds` |

## S15 cycle 2

Re-review (layer 3, tier A, Deep; new diff only) of the cycle 1 fixes of S15 (`t3/782e8aab` @ `4ec0b00` on `integration` @ `1b00bee`): BUG-1230's long-line rule, BUG-1231's catch-up and `behind`/`tip_id`, BUG-1232's streamed candidates, `DF_CAP` and bounded pages. Held, with tests: answers equal across hidden files and segment layouts with `DF_CAP` saturated and long lines skipped (`search_counts_and_long_lines_are_per_viewer`); every route within a 300 ms deadline over 300,000 files in three landings (`search_every_route_is_bounded_at_scale`); a cut walk and a policy change caught up for a branch no update asked for (`search_index_catches_up_every_branch`); the longest line searched took at most 80 ms per call in a release build for 30 hostile patterns (measured outside the server). One finding, introduced by cycle 1; not a leak.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1233 | important (**fixed**, orchestrator at the S15 merge: the walk head is read before the shards; wrong result: a stale answer presented as current; not a leak) | server / search `search?kind=path` | **Fixed:** the branch's walked tip is read before the names shards, so shards read afterwards are at least as new as the tip it reports; a race can only say "behind" when it is not. Before: **A name search can say it is current (`behind: false`) while its names are from before the tip.** The branch's walked tip, which decides `behind` for a name search, is read in its own statement after the names shards (and their head) were read; an update that commits the names and the walk in between gives an answer from the old shards with `snapshot_id` and `tip_id` both the new tip. Measured: each of 40 rounds adds a file and asks for its name from six searches at once while the update runs; 18 of the 240 first answers saying `behind: false` (and `tip_id` the new tip) found nothing. Reading the walk before the shards (so a race can only make an answer say `behind` when it is not) made the test pass, 0 of 240. The code index is not affected: its covered snapshot is the head `read_state` reads with its shards. | `search::shards` (`search/mod.rs:329`–`330`) reads `read_state(NAMES)` and then `read_head(WALK, branch)`, two reads of state one transaction commits together (`index::commit`), outside `read_state`'s head-shards-head check. | `server_hub` `search::bug_1233_a_name_search_is_current_only_with_its_names` |


## S28 packs (2026-11-07)

Found while building S28 (packs, staged uploads, checks several at once: `HUB.md` §13.20).

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1150 | low (open; **pre-existing** class: S1; S28 makes it about a third closer) | server / push / limits | **A push's JSON body grows with the objects it introduces, against the 64 MiB body limit:** each new object's receipt rides in it. On the 1 GB profile's initial push (327,017 objects) the body was about 34 MB before S28 and is about 45 MB with S28's receipts (33 bytes longer: they name their staged pack). A history about 1.5 times larger in objects is refused with 413, and `vl` has no way to split the push. | `PushRequest::receipts` holds one receipt per introduced object, and `db::body_limit` gives every route but `/objects` 64 MiB. Suggested fix: receipts per staged pack instead of per object (a push then names each staged pack once), or the push's checks reading the receipts from the uploads' own records. | (by arithmetic; `scripts/bench-server.sh 5g` would show it) |
| BUG-1151 | low (open; **pre-existing**; the class of BUG-970 and BUG-1085: timing under load) | tests / timing | **`adversarial_s10::bug_1053_a_change_of_ten_thousand_files_lands_on_s3` fails in a full parallel `server_hub` run while the machine's load is 100–500:** its client gives each request 120 s, and an API commit of 100,000 objects onto MinIO takes longer then. Alone it passes, on `integration` @ `228eb1b` and with S28 alike (27.9 / 44.4 s and 27.9 / 32.9 s, back to back), and `verify-server.sh` passed it on both databases. | The test's `ureq` agent has `timeout_global` 120 s (`support.rs`), and the 100,000 loose puts of an API commit (S10 stores them one per object) share MinIO with the rest of the suite. | `cargo test … --test server_hub` under load |
| BUG-1152 | low (open, narrowed in S28 cycle 2; introduced by S28; speed, never correctness) | server / clone speed / MinIO | **Narrowed:** a `fetch` now reads the packed objects it will send, neighbours of one pack in one ranged request (`Objects::prefetch`: slots at most 64 KiB apart, at most 2 MiB a request, within the bound on bytes read ahead): the full clone of the 1 GB profile is **59.8 s** with S28 against 68.5 s on `integration` @ `6fa552c4` (`bench-server.sh 1g`, back to back, quiet). **Left:** the clone of one directory, whose objects lie scattered across many packs, is 8.0 s against 4.7 s: one ranged `GET` per object into a large pack costs more on MinIO than one `GET` of a small object. S29's merged packs, written in fetch order, and the daemon's and regional caches (S6, S9) are where that goes. **A full clone of the 1 GB profile reads packed objects about 1.5 times slower on MinIO:** 78 s on `integration` @ `228eb1b` against 119 s with S28 (same harness and client, both under `bench-quiet.sh`, load 22 and 44: noisy). Each object is one ranged `GET` into a pack of up to about 8 MiB, where it was one `GET` of its own object; MinIO's ranged reads of large objects cost more than whole reads of small ones. Push and memory are better (`HUB.md` §13.20); the clone's request count is unchanged. | One ranged request per object out of large packs (`Objects::pack_range`). Suggested fix: read neighbouring slots of one pack in one ranged request when a fetch wants several (the fetch knows its wants up front), and let S29's merged packs follow fetch order; the Veil daemon and regional caches (S6, S9) absorb most reads anyway (`storage-and-cost.md` §7). | `.scratch` harness: push, then `vl clone`, per server build |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1153 | medium (**fixed**, S28 cycle 2; introduced by the merge of S28 with S15: neither branch alone) | server / cost counters / search | **Fixed:** the search index stores its segments with `Objects::put_background` (counted apart, as the deriver's), and the deriver's and indexer's start-up catch-up runs inside `store::in_background`. **S15's search segments count as a push's storage writes:** on the merge, an admin's push is 9 storage writes once the background work is done, not 1, so S28's `packs::a_push_is_one_storage_write_and_reads_come_from_its_pack` fails whenever the indexer runs before it counts (3 of 4 runs here), and `veil-bench load`'s `GATE_STORAGE_WRITES_PER_PUSH` counts the indexer's writes as the push's. | `search/index.rs` `put` stores each segment with `Objects::put` through `rt.block_on` on a blocking thread, outside `store::in_background` (a task-local does not cross `spawn_blocking`), and `search::index::landed` spawns the indexer without it; the deriver uses `put_background`. Suggested fix: store segments as background writes (`put_background`, or `BACKGROUND.scope` around the `block_on`). | `server_hub` `packs::bug_1153_background_indexing_is_not_counted_as_a_pushs_writes` |
| BUG-1154 | important (**fixed**, S28 cycle 2; introduced by S28) | server / object reads / packs | **Fixed:** every pack entry starts with its object's id (format `veilpack2`), and every read of a slot, whole, ranged or of its first bytes, checks it before using a byte (`pack::entry`); a range far into a large object reads the id first. **A `Range` read of a plain packed object serves the bytes its index slot names, unchecked:** with one entry of a pack's index naming another object's slot (a damaged index, or a wrong one a later pack merger writes: S29), a whole read is refused (checked against the id), but `GET /v1/objects/{p}/{id}` with `Range: bytes=0-` serves the other object, which shares the pack with it and so may be in a folder the reader cannot see. `HUB.md` §13.20 says "a wrong slot is an error, never other content". Attacker: none controls the index (storage damage or a server bug); harm: a cross-folder read for whoever holds a grant to a neighbour. Before S28 a loose object's key was its id, so a damaged one was only ever its own bytes. | `Objects::get_range` (`store.rs`): a packed object whose first bytes are not compressed is read with `pack_range` for the bytes asked and returned; nothing ties the slot to the id. Suggested fix: make each pack entry carry its id (`id ‖ encoding`), and refuse a read whose slot does not start with the id asked for (one ranged `GET` that also covers those 32 bytes); every read then proves its slot is the object's. | `veil-server` `store::tests::bug_1154_a_wrong_slot_never_serves_another_objects_range` |
| BUG-1155 | important (**fixed**, S28 cycle 2; introduced by S28; BUG-824's class) | server / push / receipts | **Fixed:** an object counts as uploaded only if its receipt's pack holds it and the pack is the pusher's and staged or listed (the `packs` rows, one statement); a staged object is read from its pack only, never from the project's store. Re-review (tier A, Deep; the new diff only, `02394f7e..04833d01`) of the S28 cycle 1 fixes (`t3/1461f222` @ `04833d01`, merged with `integration` @ `6b65ed62`: BUG-1294's fix, the test-database prefix, S9, S15; only `docs/BUGS.md` conflicted). For BUG-1398 (the second route of BUG-1153's class), count a push's own writes rather than subtracting known kinds of background.

## S28 cycle 3 (review, 2026-11-08)

Last review cycle (tier A, Deep) of S28 (`t3/1461f222` @ `2e19f61c`, merged with `integration` @ `333d54fa`), the cycle 3 diff (`a10084d9..2e19f61c`) and the tier A files it touches (`pack.rs`, `store.rs`, `sync.rs`) in full. BUG-1159, 1394 (for the routes its test names), 1395 to 1399 hold. Four findings, all introduced by S28: BUG-1497 is a second route of BUG-1394's class (the tiling compares slots with each other, never with the entries), BUG-1495 a race of cycle 3's paging, BUG-1496 the class of BUG-1087 for pack indexes, BUG-1498 a gap in what S29 is documented to remove. New property test, passing: `store::tests::packed_reads_answer_their_own_object_or_refuse_whatever_the_damage` (240 damaged packs: any index byte, other entries' slots and ids, truncation before and after the index is read, swapped slots and entries; whole, encoded, ranged, neighbour and blocking reads).

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1497 | important (**fixed**, S28 cycle 4; introduced by S28; BUG-1154's and BUG-1394's class) | server / object reads / packs | **Fixed** (`veilpack3`): every pack entry states the length of its encoding after its id, and every read, whole, ranged, neighbour or blocking, checks the id and the length against its slot (`pack::entry`) before it uses a byte, so a slot is tied to its entry at both ends and a read never leaves its slot; `veilpack2` is refused as not a pack. The property test gains moved boundaries. **A boundary moved between two neighbouring slots passes `parse_index`, and a ranged read of a plain packed object serves the next entry's id and bytes.** With the first slot `d` bytes longer and the next one starting `d` bytes later and `d` shorter (a merger's off-by-`d`, BUG-1154's model of a damaged index), the slots still tile the pack: the first passes its id check, and `get_range(open, 0, MAX)` answered its 47 bytes, the neighbour's 32-byte id and the first byte of its entry (80 bytes, "length 80"); any `d` up to the neighbour's length leaks `d - 32` bytes of it, possibly of a folder the reader cannot see. Moved the other way, a range answers a length that is not the object's. Whole and neighbour reads decode and check the id, so they refuse; ranges and `head`'s length do not. | `pack::parse_index` checks that each slot starts where the one before ends, never that a boundary is where an entry ends: the tiling compares slots with one another, and `Objects::pack_range` checks only the id at a slot's start, so a slot's end is checked against nothing in the pack. Suggested fix (the class): make each entry state its own length after its id (`veilpack3`: `id ‖ len u32be ‖ encoding`, free before S28 merges) and check it with the id on every read (`pack::entry`), so a slot is checked against its entry at both ends; or read the 32 bytes after a slot with it and check they are the next entry's id (or the pack's end). | `veil-server` lib `store::tests::bug_1497_a_boundary_moved_between_neighbours_never_serves_the_neighbours_bytes` |
| BUG-1495 | medium (**fixed**, S28 cycle 4; introduced by S28 cycle 3) | server / object reads / lookup maps | **Fixed:** `Packs::find_paged` searches the loaded indexes and names the unloaded ones under one read of the map, then reads those from storage (`Packs::locate` runs the whole lookup on one project entry), so every listed pack is searched whatever pages in or out meanwhile. **A lookup racing another lookup's page-in reads an object of a listed pack as missing.** `Objects::in_pack` asks `Packs::find` (the loaded indexes) and, on `Paged`, `Packs::find_paged`, which searches only the indexes that are unloaded **when it starts**; nothing holds the map between the two calls. A lookup of the same project that pages the object's index in between (a clone's or fetch's concurrent reads of a project past `LOOKUP_BUDGET`) makes it loaded, so neither call searches it: `in_pack` answers `None`, and the read is "missing object" (a fetch's "read went missing", a push refused, an object route's 404). Reproduced by interleaving the two lookups by hand: the second answers `None` for an object of the first pack. | `pack.rs` `Packs::find_paged` snapshots `l.index.is_none()` packs only; `store.rs` `Objects::in_pack` calls `find` and `find_paged` apart. Suggested fix: have `find_paged` search the loaded indexes and collect the unloaded ones under one read of the map (and search a pack's index again once it is loaded), so the two together cover every listed pack. | `veil-server` lib `pack::tests::bug_1495_a_lookup_racing_a_page_in_still_finds_its_object` |
| BUG-1496 | medium (**fixed**, S28 cycle 4; introduced by S28; BUG-1087's class: memory outside every bound) | server / memory / pack indexes | **Fixed:** every index held outside the lookup maps holds a share of one server-wide bound (`pack::INDEXES_HELD`, 96 MiB; `pack::Bound`, `Held`), taken before it is read or built: `read_index` (lookups, listings), the staged-index cache (32 MiB of it), a push's own pack; a push keeps of each staged index only its object count, length and the slots its receipts name (`Packs::staged_slots`); `Packs::refresh` enters packs unloaded and loads each as it is read, leaving the rest unloaded when the bound is full; a request without a share after 10 s is answered 503 `busy`. **Pack indexes read into memory are held outside every bound.** A push reads the index of every staged pack its receipts name (`sync::staging`) and holds them all until it is answered; an index is 48 bytes a slot in memory, a staged pack may hold 2^21 objects (an upload request may be 2 GiB), and the staged-index cache (32 MiB) keeps none larger than itself, so each push reads and holds copies of its own. A participant uploaded two packs of a million tiny objects once, then sent eight pushes that named one receipt of each and lost their race (wrong expected tip: the uploads stay staged): the server grew **1,131 MiB**, from requests of a few hundred bytes. More pushes, more memory. The same class: `Packs::refresh` collects every index of a project it has not read (16 reads at once) before it adds any, so a server's first lookup of a project whose indexes pass `LOOKUP_BUDGET` holds them all (BUG-1395's fix bounds what stays, not this); `Packs::find_paged` holds one per lookup, any number at once. | `sync.rs` `staging`: `packs.push((n, index, size))` for every usable pack, read with `staged_index`; `pack.rs` `Packs::refresh`: `got` holds every new index until `add`; `find_paged` reads without a share. Suggested fix (the class): every index read into memory holds a share of a server-wide bound while it is held (e.g. `store::DECODED_IN_FLIGHT`, taken before the read from the head's count); `refresh` adds each index as it is read (or lists the packs unloaded for `find_paged`); and a push keeps of each staged index only the slots its receipts name and the index's length (`packs_to_list` needs no more: "every object read" is a count). | `server_hub` `packs::hostile_bug_1496_pushes_hold_the_staged_indexes_they_name_within_a_bound` (hostile set) |
| BUG-1498 | low (**fixed**, S28 cycle 4; introduced by S28) | server / storage / discarding | **Fixed:** `Packs::discard` tries every delete and reports the failures once all were tried; `storage-and-cost.md` §8 says S29's job deletes the packs of discarded rows, then the rows, and names the hook it needs to drop a pack from servers' lookup maps. **A failed delete stops a discard, and discarded packs left in storage are removed by nothing.** `Packs::discard` turns the rows discarded, then deletes the packs one by one and returns at the first delete that fails (a store error past its 10 s of retries): the packs after it stay in storage, discarded. A server stopped between the update and the deletes leaves the same. `HUB.md` §13.20 says S29's job removes "the staged rows older than its grace, and their packs", not discarded ones, so what a refused push uploaded (a plain-text secret, BUG-930) can stay stored for good. Reproduced with a store whose first delete fails: of three discarded packs, all three stay. | `pack.rs` `Packs::discard`: `store.delete(…).await?` in the loop. Suggested fix: try every delete (log the failures); and document, for S29, that its job also deletes the packs of discarded rows (a discarded row's pack may still be in storage), then the rows. | `veil-server` lib `pack::tests::bug_1498_a_failed_delete_leaves_no_other_discarded_pack_stored` |

## S28 cycle 4 (fixes, 2026-11-09)

The cycle 3 findings closed by changing what is checked, past the review-cycle limit (owner's decisions). BUG-1497: pack format `veilpack3`, each entry self-describing (id, then its encoding's length), checked by every read against its slot; `store::tests::packed_reads_answer_their_own_object_or_refuse_whatever_the_damage` now also moves boundaries between neighbours (280 damaged packs). BUG-1495: `Packs::find_paged` searches loaded indexes and names unloaded ones under one read of the map. BUG-1496: one server-wide bound on every index held outside the lookup maps (`pack::INDEXES_HELD`), guarantee test `pack::tests::indexes_held_outside_the_lookup_maps_share_one_bound`; a push keeps only the slots its receipts name. BUG-1498: every delete tried; S29's sweep of discarded rows' packs and the lookup-map hook written down (`storage-and-cost.md` §8). The four reproductions are un-ignored and pass. No new finding.

## S28 cycle 4 (review s28r4, 2026-11-09)

Review (tier A, Deep) of `s28-c4` @ `c9345b95` against `integration` @ `21370c6a`, scoped to `46110259..c9345b95`: the S28 cycle 4 work (`488960c1..c9345b95`: `pack.rs`, `store.rs`, `sync.rs`, `error.rs`, tests) read in full; the rest of the diff is integration's own (S8, merged at `488960c1`), reviewed there. Held, with tests: (1) a read answers exactly its object's bytes or a refusal: every packed read goes through `pack::entry` (id, stated length equal to the slot's, no more bytes than the slot); new `store::tests::s28r4_entries_whose_head_lies_and_packs_before_cycle_4_are_refused_never_misread` (each entry's stated length damaged nine ways and its id two, through whole, encoded, ranged and blocking reads; a `veilpack2` pack refused, relabelled `veilpack3` it answers no read) beside cycle 4's 280-pack property test. A damaged byte inside a plain object's encoding can still be served by a range read (ranges of plain objects are not hash-checked, documented since S5; the client checks the whole object). (2) No lookup answers "missing" for a stored object: `locate` holds one entry across its steps, `find_paged_in` searches and names under one read; new `pack::tests::s28r4_no_lookup_answers_missing_while_others_page_in_out_and_list` (15 tasks paging in and out, packs listed meanwhile, on eight threads; then with the bound tight: found or refused, never missing). (4) Permissions stay per object: no access check changed; `staging` and `packs_to_list` are as strict as before or stricter (existing `server_hub` receipt and BUG-1155 tests). (5) No refused upload's pack stays reachable: reachability is the rows' state (`usable`), set discarded before any delete; `bug_1498_*` passes. (6) Tests assert success first. (3) Index memory within the bound: **not held**, BUG-1620, 1621, 1622, all medium, all introduced by cycle 4. One client can force 503s on every other project for as long as it keeps pushes in flight (BUG-1620): not acceptable for a shared server.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|----|------|------|---------|------------|-------------------|
| BUG-1620 | medium (**fixed**, S28 cycle 5; introduced by S28 cycle 4) | server / storage / availability | **Fixed:** (a) `Packs::staged_slots` finds a push's receipt slots in an uncached staged pack by bisecting the sorted index in storage with 64 KiB ranged reads (`lookup_slice`, `bisect_slots`) under a single `FIRST_READ` (64 KiB) share, never reading or parsing the whole index; and (b) `Bound` gives each project its own fair share of the active bound (at most a quarter of `most` across concurrent shares of one project, or one larger share alone yielding round-robin when another project waits; cached shares in `Packs::staged` are detached from the active project quota), so one project's index reads or writes never starve another project's. **One person's requests can make every other project's uploads, pushes and paged lookups wait 10 s and be answered 503, for as long as they keep sending.** The bound on indexes held outside the lookup maps is one fair (first come, first served) queue for the whole server, with no share per project or person. The staged-index cache's 32 MiB of shares fills with the person's own small uploads (an upload that would evict them needs a share first). A push reads the index of every staged pack its receipts name, 16 at once; an index past 32 MiB (about 700,000 objects) is never cached, so each read takes 64 MiB, all the cache leaves. A few pushes of a few hundred bytes in flight, each naming one receipt of each of a few such staged packs (the pushes lose their race, so the uploads stay staged), keep more than 10 s of exclusive reads queued, and every other request queued behind them is answered 503. S24's limits (200 requests a second per device, per-project bulkheads, 512 MiB of bodies) do not stop it. Reproduced at a small scale with the server's proportions: three other projects' lookups of a 10-object pack, one after another, are refused. | `pack.rs:305-328` `Bound` (one `tokio::sync::Semaphore`, `INDEX_WAIT` 10 s, `pack.rs:283`), taken by `read_index` (`pack.rs:380`) for `staged_slots`, `find_paged` and `refresh`, and by `Objects::write_pack` (`store.rs:762`); `sync.rs:2133` `staging` reads every named staged index. Suggested fix: a push finds its receipts' slots by bisecting the stored (sorted) index with ranged reads, so it never holds a whole index; and/or a share per project or person, or index reads inside S24's per-project bulkheads, so one project's reads queue only behind its own. | `veil-server` lib `pack::tests::bug_1620_one_persons_index_reads_never_starve_another_projects_lookup` |
| BUG-1621 | medium (**fixed**, S28 cycle 5; introduced by S28 cycle 4) | server / storage / memory | **Fixed:** `Bound::permits` never clamps a share below what it holds (a share above `most` is refused); `MAX_OBJECTS` is lowered to `256 << 10` (262,144 objects; uploads and pushes with more split into multiple packs), so a full pack's index takes at most 27 MiB to read and parse (`Index::read_weight_of`), 23 MiB to build (`Index::write_weight_of`, taken by `Objects::write_pack`), and 12 MiB to hold (`Index::weight_of`), fitting inside `most` (64 MiB) and half the active bound (32 MiB); `pack::build` deduplicates in place using sorted index entries without a `HashSet` or second object vector; `read_index` takes a `FIRST_READ` (64 KiB) share before reading the first 64 KiB; and `ListedPack.held` drops its share as soon as `listed()` enters the index in the lookup map before `projected()`. Measured in a child process (`bug_1621_…`): with the 32 MiB staged-index cache full (~30.4 MiB) and two full `MAX_OBJECTS` indexes read concurrently, peak RSS growth is ~64 MiB against the 96 MiB `INDEXES_HELD` bound. **Indexes outside the lookup maps can hold about 250 MiB, against the 96 MiB `HUB.md` §13.20 promises.** A share is clamped at what one holder may take (`Bound::permits`, 64 MiB, so a share can always come free), but a pack may hold `MAX_OBJECTS` (2^21) objects: reading its index holds about 216 MiB (88 MiB of index bytes, 96 MiB parsed, the parse's 32 MiB working copy) and holding it 96 MiB, under a 64 MiB share. Writing a pack is counted short too: `write_pack` takes a share for the parsed index only, while `build` also holds the index bytes (44 bytes a slot) and its set of ids seen. With the cache's 32 MiB, that is about 250 MiB. An upload of a million tiny objects reaches it (the hostile test of BUG-1496 sends two). Reproduced: an index of 98,368 bytes held under a share of 65,536; at the server's sizes, a 216 MiB read under a 64 MiB share. | `pack.rs:317-319` `Bound::permits` (`clamp(1, most)`); `pack.rs:380` `read_index`'s share; `store.rs:762` `write_pack`'s share. Suggested fix: count every allocation in a share (bytes read, parsed, working copy; `build`'s set and index bytes), and cap a pack's objects (vl uploads 8 MiB of frames at a time, so 2^18 or 2^19 does not touch it; a push's own pack would be split) so that the largest share fits `most` and the clamp can go. | `veil-server` lib `pack::tests::bug_1621_an_index_held_outside_the_lookup_maps_holds_a_share_of_all_it_holds` |

## Op log race (BUG-1294)

Found by `verify-fast.sh s3e` on S3's branch, reproduced on `integration` 6fa552c; fixed on branch `bug1294`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1294 | important (**fixed**, bug1294; **pre-existing**: reproduced on `integration` 6fa552c as on the S3 branch, found by `verify-fast.sh s3e`; a lost update) | op log / lock-free commits | **Fixed:** the merge of concurrent operations compares each key with what the two sides' shared history holds, not only with their newest common operation (`oplog::shared_base`): a side's value that no operation only it reaches introduced is the shared history's, so the other side's change wins. **Under load, a lock-free commit's tag named a tree without the file the commit wrote.** `core_durability` `metadata_lock::grant_racing_lock_free_commits` (three workspaces each commit three new files and tag each commit, while key-ring grants and a pull run in other handles) failed about one run in 70 with the machine's load near 100, always on the memory backend: tag `c0-1` named a tree of `["f0-0", "f0-2"]`, `c1-2` one of `["f1-0", "f1-1"]`. Stress, six runs at a time: 3 failures in 360 runs of the branch, 1 in 330 of `integration`; 8 copies of the 200-round reproduction at once: 5 of 8 failed before the fix, 8 of 8 passed after; the whole `core_durability` binary, 8 copies at once three times beside a build: 23 of 24 failed the reproduction before (all else passing), 24 of 24 passed after. | **A criss-cross of merges, merged against one of its bases.** Traced: `20d8053f` (a snapshot of w0) and `dcc32746` (w1's snapshot holding `f1-1`) were concurrent. One settler listed `{20d8053f, dcc32746}` and wrote `f0f5128e`; others had meanwhile merged `dcc32746` into `f50c8437` and that with `20d8053f` into `82b1b09b`, on which w1 committed (`247fa8b8`, w1 → a new working copy) and set `c1-1`. Merging those two heads (`1be961d5`), `OpStore::split` found two nearest common operations, `20d8053f` and `dcc32746`, and `Repo::merge_plan` used the newest alone, `20d8053f`, whose view still had w1's working copy before `f1-1`. So w1 looked moved on both sides, and the conflict rule (first side wins) kept `f0f5128e`'s working copy from before the commit (rebased by the commit's rewrite to `d9535942`) over the commit's new one. The next merge, of that with w1's snapshot holding `f1-2` (`6c01da6c`), saw two moved working copies against `f84a8857` and kept `d9535942` again; w1's commit then committed it, and `c1-2` lacked `f1-2`. The class: any key one side changed while the other still held a value from the shared history that the chosen base lacked (workspaces, tags, remote tags, heads, removals too); `Repo::parent_view` (undo of a merge) had the same single-base merge and now uses `merge_plan`. A recursive (Git-style) merge base was tried first and dropped: in a storm criss-crosses nest down the whole history, and each merge cost O(history) merges (the reproduction ran more than four times slower); the fix reads only the operations `split` already walks. | `core_durability` `metadata_lock::bug_1294_lock_free_commits_keep_their_files` (200 rounds of the race; under load); `core_props` `oplog_merge::criss_cross_keeps_the_newer_commit` (the traced interleaving, and an undo back to a shared value), `oplog_merge::merges_keep_every_operation_memory` and `_disk` (three writers and settlers of random subsets of the heads, every one publishing after a random delay: every writer finds all its files, and every tag a commit with all of them) |

### BUG-1294 review

Review (tier A, Deep) of branch `bug1294` @ `f6f4eb11` on `integration` @ `6fa552c`. The fix holds for its stated class: the review's model check (`core_props` `oplog_merge::every_write_survives_concurrent_merges_{memory,disk}`: 2 to 5 writers, tag moves and deletes, remote tags set and dropped, extra workspaces created and removed, settlers of random subsets of the heads, everything publishing late; each command's view and the final one must hold, for every key, the causally last write's value, a real conflict's losers must stay visible and be warned of) passed on the branch in 15 runs of 128 memory cases (8 of them at once, beside 8 copies of every other op-log test, all green) and 156 disk cases, and failed 4 runs in 4 on `integration` (working copies, a workspace removal and a remote-tag removal lost). Both findings below are **pre-existing** (they fail the same way on `6fa552c`) and outside what the fix claims; neither blocks the merge.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1295 | medium (**fixed**, b1295; **pre-existing**: fails identically on `integration` 6fa552c; a wrong result, no content lost: the workspace ends on the commit, whose tree is the undone working copy's) | op log / merge of concurrent operations, rewrites | **Fixed:** `Repo::merge_plan` keeps every rewrite it collects with the operations that recorded it and decides at every fold step, not only at the one that collected it, whether it was undone: a rewrite is not applied when a side that saw it shows its old snapshot again (BUG-802, as before), when a head merged later reaches an operation that recorded it and shows the old snapshot, or when a side shows the old snapshot where the step's shared history (`shared_base`) does not (it brought the snapshot back: an undo or op restore of a rewrite from the shared history, which a merge on the other side recorded again; merges record the rewrites they applied). A second route of the class, found by the model check once undo ran: the commit's rewrite re-recorded by a settler's merge on the side that never saw the commit, merged with the undo, whose history holds the commit as a common operation. **`vl undo` of a commit is reversed by a merge of three heads.** From the commit's operation, one command undoes it (the workspace back on its working copy before the commit) and another does something else; a third command never saw the commit. When the fold (heads in id order) merges the undo last, the workspace ends on the commit itself, not on the undone working copy. The review's model check with undo and `op restore` among the commands failed in every run (16 of 16), most often this way (the rest: BUG-1296). | `Repo::merge_plan` (`repo.rs`, the `rewrites` block) skips a side's rewrite of `old` only if *that side's* refs (or their ancestors) show `old` again; it decides per fold step. Merging the head that saw the commit (its `only` ops hold the commit's rewrite of the working copy into the commit; its refs do not show the old working copy) with the head that never saw it collects the rewrite; the next step merges the undo, whose `only` ops hold no rewrite, so nothing takes it out, and `Transaction::for_merge` applies it to the merged view, where the undo put the old working copy back. BUG-802's class (an undone rewrite re-applied), by a third head. Fix: decide the skip against the final merged view (a rewrite of a snapshot the merged view still refers to, or shows as an ancestor of a ref, is not applied), not per side and step. | `core_props` `oplog_merge::bug_1295_an_undone_commit_stays_undone_through_a_three_way_merge` (deterministic: builds the interleaving until the undo's operation id sorts last); `oplog_merge::bug_1295_every_write_survives_with_undo_and_restore` and `every_write_survives_with_undo_and_restore_disk` (the model check with undo, op restore and writes back to earlier values; also finds BUG-1296). Two corrections to the model, which asserted something wrong: each command runs as its own user, so two commands never write the same operation (with writes back allowed, a tag set to the value it has from the same head in the same millisecond was one operation, counted as two commands), and a conflict's losing target may go once a later command that saw it took its head away (an op restore to before the command that wrote it) |
| BUG-1296 | medium (**fixed**, b1295; **pre-existing**: fails identically on `integration` 6fa552c; a lost update of a tag or remote tag, the target stays visible; the builder's account says an undo back to an older value counts as a change, which holds only when the other side changed nothing) | op log / merge of concurrent operations | **Fixed:** when both sides introduced their (different) values, `oplog::shared_base` gives the key no base value (absent: equal to neither side), so `merge_views` sees two changes: a change beats a removal, and two moves keep the first side's with the other visible and a warning. Heads likewise: added on one side and dropped on the other, both by operations only that side reaches, the addition wins. This exposed BUG-1297, which had made a stale value look introduced. **A write back to the merge base's value loses to a concurrent removal or move.** One command moves a tag away and back (`vl tag set`, or `vl undo` of a command that moved it), another deletes it, concurrently: after the merge the tag is gone, though a change beats a removal ("a key removed on one side and changed on another keeps the change", `ARCHITECTURE.md`). ### Op log merges review

Review (tier A, Deep) of branch `t3/70bd60c4` @ `f02d0ed6` (BUG-1295 to 1298 fixes) on `integration` @ `ebabc15c`. The four fixes hold for their stated reproductions and the model checks, at the pinned seed and with fresh seeds, more writers and many copies at once (`core_props` `oplog_merge::*`, writers widened to 2 to 9 and steps to 240, fresh seeds, 8 copies at once: `bug_1295_every_write_survives_with_undo_and_restore` 8 runs of 300 cases and 8 of 200, `every_write_survives_concurrent_merges_memory` 8 of 200, `every_write_survives_with_undo_and_restore_disk` (2 to 7 writers, 160 steps) 6 of 40, all passed). Cost stays bounded: a merge at open of 64 heads, each describing a different old commit, over 2,000 commits took 9.6 s against 8.8 s before (32 heads: 2.1 s against 1.7 s; debug build), with the same peak memory (305 MB). Two corrections to the model were checked and are right: two identical commands of one user in one millisecond from the same heads are one operation with one effect, and collapsing them is correct (`portable` `identical_commands_in_one_millisecond_are_one_operation`: a later command that saw the first keeps its move when the second lands late); and a conflict's loser that a later command which saw it took away (an undo of the commit that made it, an op restore before it) may go, as with any head (the model still passes with the excuse narrowed to undo and op restore). The clamp keeps the op log newest first and `vl undo` on the last operation with the clock set back and forward (`portable` `operation_times_never_go_back_and_the_log_stays_in_order`). An auto-rebase still moves a commit made on a snapshot another command described (`core_durability` `oplog_concurrency::describe_racing_a_commit_on_it_moves_the_commit`). Findings:

Two more routes of the class, found by the new auto-rebase model check: on one side a later rewrite of a snapshot replaced an earlier one even when the two were concurrent (merged on that side as a divergent change), so the survivor was lost once the other was undone (pre-existing); now only an operation that descends from the other's replaces it. ## S11 cycle 1

Review (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of milestone S11, agent sessions, attribution and attempts (`t3/dbf17b5e` @ `983e9e8d` on `integration` @ `6fa552c4`). Held, with tests: narrowing on every file route, fetch and grants, history the person's; the folders on the way to a narrowed path are byte for byte the person's (`agents::the_folders_on_the_way_are_exactly_what_the_person_sees`); an agent session loses what its person loses, at once (`agents::an_agent_session_loses_what_its_person_loses_at_once`); attribution stamped by the server, never by the caller; attempts never a tip, parent or base. Five findings, all introduced by S11; none leaks sealed content.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |

Test: the reproduction, with the previous release's query verbatim. **A server that predates migration 20 takes an agent session's token for its person's own session.** Agent sessions are rows of `sessions` with the person's device and an ordinary `token_hash`; the release before finds a session by `token_hash`, `expires_at` and the device alone, and ignores the new columns. In a rolling upgrade (migration first, then servers replaced one at a time) a new server makes agent sessions while old ones still answer on the same database: a token narrowed to `src/api` in one project is then, at an old server, unnarrowed, in every project, and may make sessions, invites, access changes, rings and shares. `HUB.md` §13.27 notes it only for a revert. An unnarrowed agent session of an admin commits `{PERSON_DIR}/ public` through `POST …/changes` with `onto: main`: accepted (`access accepted: …`), and carol's private folder is readable by anyone on Earth. ## S11 cycle 2

Review (layer 3, tier A, Deep; new diff only) of S11 cycle 2 (`t3/dbf17b5e` @ `f9ccba63`, merged with `integration` @ `6b65ed62`: a docs-only conflict in this file). Held, with tests: an agent session never changes `.veilpolicy` or `.veilrules` by its own push or API commit, in any folder, nor by a merge taking someone else's change (the fix's test); case variants are no policy file (the server and `vl` read `.veilpolicy` by its exact name, and checkout refuses names that fold together); no agent session forces or deletes a branch, and a narrowed one's moves are compared tree to tree (the fix's tests); no route changes a project's default branch, so a new branch never becomes it; an older server's lookup never finds an agent session, and a new server never takes a token as the other kind (`agents::a_token_is_only_ever_the_kind_of_session_it_was_made_as`: the bare token, a person's token with the prefix, every stored hash); `repo.json` and its remotes keep unknown fields, refused on open, upgrade and fsck; an older `vl` gets no format-10 snapshot by any route (`agents::an_older_vl_gets_no_format_10_snapshot_by_any_route`: history answers 426 `update_vl`; fetch and the object routes, and so the regional cache, serve only trees and files; the query API answers JSON). S17's landing service is not in `integration` yet: it will need BUG-1391's tree-to-tree check of the files that decide access, the narrowing check, and the agent's attribution on what it lands.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1391 | important (**fixed**, S11 cycle 3; introduced by S11 cycle 2's partial fix of BUG-1377; a broken stated guarantee: `ACCESS_FILES` says "… or a branch move that lands one"; an admin's agent session, with its token alone) | server / push | **Fixed:** every branch move by an agent session (push, API commit with `onto`) compares the old tip's tree with the new tip's for files that decide access or review, in any folder, whoever made the change (`sync::changes_access_files`, on the walker the narrowing check uses, `sync::differs_where`), and refuses one that changes any (403 `agent_session` on a push; `rejected` for an API commit). Tests: the reproduction (a fast-forward and an API commit onto the admin's draft of `.veilpolicy` tier lines and `.veilrules`). **An agent session lands someone else's change of `.veilpolicy` or `.veilrules` by moving a branch onto it.** The admin parks a change of `.veilpolicy` that changes no access line (a tier line, `src/api/generated/  ignore`; tier lines decide what every member's `vl` seals, ignores or scans) and of `.veilrules` on a side branch; the admin's agent session pushes `main` from its tip to the draft: `ok`, and `main` carries both. No new snapshot is made, so `check_changes` never sees the files; only the default branch's access lines are compared (`same_rules`), so only an access-line change is refused. The same holds for any move onto a merge whose first parent holds the change. (An API commit on the draft `onto` main is refused.) The class: the rule is checked on each new snapshot's diff from its first parent, while a branch move changes the tip from its old tree to its new one. | BUG-1392 | important (**fixed**, S11 cycle 3; S11, cycle 1's narrowing, not fixed by cycle 2's fix of the stack check's message, the same class; names, not content, of files the person sees; a narrowed agent session, with its token and its person's device key) | server / push | **Fixed:** `check_changes` refuses any change outside a narrowed session's paths first, with one message naming nothing (`NARROWED_WRITE`), so none of its path-naming refusals is reached; an API commit refuses an edit outside the paths before it reads anything, so a path that exists and one that does not get the same answer. ### S24 cycle 2

The review of S24 part A at `1d08df80` (merged with `integration` @ `ae3d57ed`), cycle 2 of 3, against the brief's guarantees (a client within its limits is never refused, and no project's load starves another; refusals reveal nothing about other projects or people; memory and connection slots bounded, every slot back in bounded time; health metrics for admins only; the shedding order as designed, and the cycle 2 aging rule not usable to starve landings; the builder's open hostile-set failure; tests assert success first). One finding, introduced by cycle 2's aging rule (`becfff33`). Reproduction in `crates/veil-server/src/limits/gate.rs` (a unit test), ignored until fixed. Also fixed by the review: `docs/HUB.md` §4.7 still gave the cycle 0 rates (60/s, 5,000/h) where the defaults are 200/s and 50,000/h a device (BUG-1339), and `cache::bug_1332_a_caches_forwarded_reads_count_against_its_address` now also covers cold `POST :batch` reads through a regional cache (`limits::admit`'s deferred body grant check). The builder's open item (one `hostile-postgres` test failed once at `57f8495f`, in `verify-server-c2c.log`, run `665588`) is traced: in that run every container step (`postgres`, `yugabyte`, `hostile-postgres`, `hostile-yugabyte`, `load-postgres`, `load-yugabyte`) failed together because leftover MinIO buckets from earlier runs had exhausted all 244 million inodes on `/` (`No space left on device` in `verify-server-c2c.log`), which `bfd2c3d3` immediately fixed by removing per-run and dead-run MinIO buckets in `scripts/verify-server.sh`. `hostile-postgres` passed 9/9 in `c2` (`4028890`), `c2b` (`2161811`), `c2e` (`2855007`), `c2g` (`3556033`), and in this review's run with `VEIL_VERIFY_HOSTILE=1`.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1630 | medium (**fixed**: `Gate::leave` alternates; after a place goes to an aged pull the next goes by the normal order, `State::aged_turn`; reproduction un-ignored; was open; **introduced by S24 cycle 2**, `becfff33`; availability: landings shed before pulls under a flood of pulls, the reverse of the designed order; by a project's members, or anyone on Earth for a project with `public` folders, in that project's gate; in the server's gate for every project) | server limits / bulkheads (`limits/gate.rs` `Gate::leave`) | **A steady stream of pulls whose waits pass 1 s takes every free place: a landing waits behind all of them, until its 20 s deadline, then `503 busy`.** The cycle 2 rule gives a free place to the oldest pull first when it has waited `AGE` (1 s) so that a stream of landings cannot starve pulls; but it has no bound in the other direction: whenever the pulls' queue is longer than a second's worth of places (any sustained pull flood: 40 pulls of 100 ms on one place in the test), the pull at its front has always waited more than a second, and every place goes to pulls. Design §4.11 sheds pulls before landings. Fix for the class: alternate. After a place went to an aged pull, the next free place goes by the usual order (landings first), whatever the pulls' age: pulls get at most every other place under a landing stream, landings at least every other place under a pull flood. One `bool` in the gate's state. | `gate::leave` orders the queues `[read, write, read, search]` whenever the front pull is aged, with no memory of the last hand-over. | `limits::gate::tests::a_stream_of_aged_pulls_does_not_starve_landings` (ignored) |

Found by it: BUG-1562, BUG-1563. **A thin clone made before its person's access changed fails on the history and trees it never fetched.** Steps (`server_hub`): `feature` changes `src/` and the billing folder; a thin clone of `fin` (nothing of `feature` fetched); remove `fin` from `finance`; `vl show feature`. Expected: the readable changes (a clone made after the removal shows them; `vl pull` first makes this one show them too). Actual: `error: object … is not present in this store` (`feature`'s parent snapshot); `vl new feature` and `vl blame -r feature src/lib.rs` fail the same way on `feature`'s root tree (refused at `/`). **Design (owner's decision, `s8i`: after an access change the clone moves to the person's current view by itself; not built this round, it is larger than one):** (1) *Detect*: the server answers `history` for an older view's snapshot with its projection in the current view, under another id (`sync::history` resolves through the real snapshot); `server_knows` (BUG-1530) already sends that request, so the first refusal under such a snapshot names the change. (2) *Refresh, once, then retry the command*: a pull of the current view's tips, and a map from each older-view snapshot the clone's view refers to (tags, remote tags, workspaces' bases, heads) to its current-view projection, from batched `history` requests. (3) *Move local work into the current view*: each change only this clone holds is rebased onto its parents' current projections, its tree without the entries the new parent no longer shows (what the person cannot see is grafted back by the server on push, `docs/HUB.md` §13.4), as one undoable operation; tags, workspaces and the checkout record (a left-out folder is then absent from the tree, not carried) move with it. A change that edited inside a folder the person can no longer see cannot be expressed in the current view: it is refused by name and stays where it is, never dropped. (4) *Writes in the current view* then carry by id only what that view shows, and pushes are grafted by the server (the reviewer's push test passes). With BUG-1508's fix a refused root tree is shown as `redacted /` by readers and refused by writers; a snapshot not served is still an error. Fix (to decide): on such a refusal, ask the server for the snapshot's projection in the current view (`history`) and say so, or point at `vl pull` in the message. **Another route** (found by the review of `s8h`): work built on the old view cannot be pushed. fin (in `devs`) rebases a change of `src/` onto `feature`, the billing folder kept by id; `vl push -t kid` is refused with `you do not have access to 'bill-…' (server: forbidden)`, though the change leaves that folder exactly as its parent has it; after `vl pull` it fails as BUG-1530. (2) **The new name chosen**: the first half holds `a.txt` sealed beside the secret, a copy, which both commands kept sealed and the push check refuses the same way. | BUG-1833's fix (`dde32b23`) decides the sealing of every snapshot a transaction writes by the push check's rule, which made the property's model (tree identity) wrong for these halves. BUG-1837's commit (`23e64a53`) then made the property pass most of the time by weakening the rule instead of correcting the model: `Transaction::keep_sealing` switched the rule off for `split`, and a new clause accepted any sealed entry whose object a parent, or the snapshot itself at a secret's path, already held (`known_secret_ids`; the server passes `known = false`). That reopened BUG-1833 for a split and for a copy, and left the squash of case (1) as the property's rare failure. **Fix:** both weakenings removed, so `reconcile_sealing` is again exactly the server's rule (`policy::sealed_secret` with `known = false`: the path is a secret's, a parent holds a sealed file there, or the snapshot moves a secret of that scope away) for every snapshot a split, a squash or a rebase writes; a file the rule does not explain is recorded as `vl commit` would record it (plain, scanned: a secret-looking one refuses the command, which changes nothing). The property's model now states that: each written snapshot is its half as the rule records it on its parents (the same tree when the rule explains every entry, which is every case without a renamed secret), holds nothing the rule refuses, and one undo restores the view. Nothing of BUG-1833 or BUG-1837 is given up (their tests pass unchanged; attempts are untouched). (b) The test's comment, "the repository lock serialises them", was false. `start`, `good`, `bad`, `skip` and `reset` read the state, decided and wrote it under no lock (the op log is lock-free; the directory's lock is held only while a command records the directory when it starts and checks it out when it ends). The test now accepts the one correct refusal exactly (at most one, and only when the bisection has ended) and checks what it claimed: every verdict that succeeded is in the log, each on a candidate of its own, and the working copy is on the candidate the state names. ### S6 review, cycle 1

Found by the review of S6, the Veil daemon (`t3/7426739d` @ `bdb4a0c5`, tier A, merged with `integration` @ `3984695c` on `t3/s6-review-r1`). Rows BUG-1512–1514. None lets the daemon serve anyone more than the server would: its per-request decision (grant under the key it fetched, device signature, epochs confirmed within 5 s, chain from the grant's root) held under every test. ### S6 review, cycle 3

Found by the last review of S6 (`t3/7426739d` @ `93772ac8`, the cycle-2 fixes, tier A, on `s6r3`, which finishes a review stopped at `b39678ab`). Rows BUG-1582 and BUG-1583. The cycle's other guarantees held: no route lets a confined command reach the Veil home or the daemon's folders but BUG-1519's (`confine_cli::s6r3_a_linked_home_and_unusual_xdg_values_never_show_or_misplace_the_daemon`, with the cycle-2 tests); a `vl` connects only to a socket its own user listens on (the peer's uid is read from the connection itself, so there is no window between the check and the use; run once against a listener of uid 0 at the daemon's socket path, in a container: three connections, not one byte sent, the clone served by its own daemon); a stop never reaches a newer daemon or another user's; and `server_hub` `daemon::` and `thin::` (63 tests) pass.

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1582 | medium (**fixed**, `s6-c4`; was open; **introduced** by S6 (the progress-only route by its cycle-2 fixes, BUG-1518's; the trickle since `BETWEEN`, which bounded each gap too); a denial of service: a `vl` that never ends, no wrong answer, nothing leaks; `docs/HUB.md` §13.29's "a stalled daemon costs a process one short wait" and threat row 8 (a lying same-user process) are false for it) | client / daemon | **Fixed:** besides the 0.5 s gap rule (`ACK_WAIT`), `client::request` (`crates/vl/src/daemon/mod.rs`) bounds the time between whole objects (or from the acknowledgement to the first object or the answer's end) at `BETWEEN_OBJECTS` (35 s, the daemon's own 30 s read of the server and a margin), whatever `P` messages (`since_object.elapsed() > BETWEEN_OBJECTS`) or partial object bytes (`proto::read_object`, bounded by `since_object + BETWEEN_OBJECTS`) arrive meanwhile; past it, `give_up()` marks the daemon failed for the rest of the process (`UNUSABLE`) and `vl` reads from the server instead. `docs/HUB.md` §13.29 updated. Tests: both reproductions un-ignored and passing (the clone and `vl status` finish after one 35 s wait, under 50 s). **A daemon that acknowledges and then never finishes anything holds every `vl` process forever.** BUG-1518's fix has the daemon send `P` every 0.1 s from a thread of its own until the request's thread ends the answer (`serve.rs`, `connection`), and the client take any gap over 0.5 s for a failed daemon, with no bound on the answer as a whole (`client::request`, `proto::P => {}`; each `read` waits 0.5 s at most, `read_payload` takes as many as the object needs). Two routes: (1) **progress without end.** A real daemon wedged after its acknowledgement (its store on a hung disk in `store.read`, a budget never granted in `answers.take`), the very case BUG-1518 named, now looks alive for as long as it is wedged: before the fix it cost 35 s (`BETWEEN`), now it costs the process forever, and `vl status` in a thin clone with it (it pins through the daemon). The same for a same-user process on its socket that acknowledges and beats (HUB.md threat row 8: "a lying or broken daemon"). (2) **an object trickled.** One that begins an object of 1 MiB and sends a byte every 0.3 s keeps every gap under 0.5 s for 3.6 days. Reproduced: a clone killed by `timeout` after 40 s, both routes, where a daemon that stalls silently costs 0.9 s. | The client's one rule (a gap over 0.5 s) bounds silence, not progress: a progress message or a byte of an object restarts it, and nothing in either says the answer moves. Fix for the class: bound the time between **whole objects** (or the end), whatever `P` messages or partial bytes arrive meanwhile, at the daemon's own longest legitimate wait (its 30 s read of the server and a margin), after which the daemon is failed for the process as a silent one is; or (BUG-1518's first proposal) send `P` only while the daemon waits on the server, keep store reads and chain checks under the short wait, and bound an object's own transfer. ## Adversarial pass: S21

### S21 cycle 1

Security review (layer 3, tier A, Deep) of milestone S21, PRs and review (`t3/d7fefcdf` @ `d9229a2` on `9cddf93`, merged here with `integration` @ `3f84531` without conflicts): `crates/veil-server/src/prs/`, migration `0017_prs.sql`, `query::resolve_real`, the routes in `api.rs`, the `hub-pr-review` context and `vl pr`. All six findings are introduced by S21. Reproductions: `crates/veil-server/tests/server_hub/prs.rs`, module `s21_adversarial` (the container suite, `scripts/verify-server.sh`); each fails on PostgreSQL + MinIO and on YugabyteDB + MinIO (BUG-1255 on PostgreSQL; it takes minutes per run).

| ID | Sev. | Area | Finding | Root cause | Reproducing tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-1250 | important (**fixed**, S21 cycle 1; a leak of hidden paths' PRs; needs an access-line change while a PR gets a revision) | server / PRs / visibility classes | **Fixed:** every write of a visibility class is conditional on its inputs: `reclassify` updates a row only `WHERE policy_key = <read> AND revision = <read>` (only a new revision adds paths, and it moves `revision`), in one pass over the stale rows in id order; a row that changed stays stale (visible to nobody) until the next request. `add_revision` was already a compare-and-swap of the revision with key and lines from one policy. Tests: the reproduction (made order-independent: it now holds the PR the pass takes first, by id) fails 3/3 without the guard; `class_writes_race_revisions_and_access_lines` races revisions, access-line flips and listings on both databases. **A reclassification racing a new revision writes the class of the PR's old paths over the new revision's, so the PR is shown to people who cannot read a folder its new revision touched,** until the access lines change again. `reclassify` reads the stale PRs and their `pr_paths`, then updates each row `WHERE policy_key = <the key it read>`. A new revision made by a request that loaded the project before the change writes its class under the *old* key, so that guard still matches after it commits, and the reclassification, still holding the paths it read before, sets the class of revision 1's paths under the new key. The leak needs no attacker: an admin adds any access line while someone with access to a folder (an admin, a finance member) adds a revision touching it, and a list by anyone is reclassifying a batch of the project's PRs. Measured (both databases): a dev who cannot read `fin/` lists and opens a PR whose revision 2 changed `fin/ledger.txt`: its title, body, `files: 2`, both patches and revisions, and would see threads anchored on `fin/` paths and risk reasons naming them (`changes a dependency manifest … (fin/Cargo.toml)`). The diff itself is projected, so `fin/`'s content stays hidden. | `prs/class.rs:133` reads the paths outside any lock, and `:146`'s guard (`policy_key = $5`) does not change when `add_revision` (`prs/mod.rs:743`, the request's own `ask.project.policy`) writes new paths under the old key. **Held up, as tested or traced:**
* **Existence.** Every PR route takes the same path for a hidden PR, an unknown id and a malformed one: `participant` (writes) and then `visible`, which answers `no such PR that you can see` from one statement before any input that depends on the PR is read; route bodies are parsed by axum before the handler, so their errors do not depend on the PR. Lists, counts and searches read only `prs_by_class` rows of classes the viewer satisfies under the current lines; cursors only bound the scan; nothing is ranked. Ids are 32 random bits and every id answers alike. The class test (`class.rs`, every subset of paths for every viewer the policy tells apart) re-derived: the deciding line of a path decides its own path, so `satisfies` equals reading every touched path, `""` (admins only) included.
* **Per-viewer content.** With every touched path readable (else no PR), only the base differs in hidden folders: revisions collapse exactly when the projected base and head are equal, and `pushed_by`, `at`, `patch`, `risk`, `files` and reviews' revision numbers are taken from the first revision of a run. Anchors carry unchanged over such a rebase (the file is the same object), so outdated threads betray nothing. `resolve_real`'s real id goes only into the stored revision and `compute`; every answer projects it.
* **Approvals.** The signature binds project name, PR id, patch and verdict, NUL-separated, under `hub-pr-review`, and is checked against the signed-in device's key, so a signature is useless to anyone but its device's session. The patch hashes each change's id, every file's path, kind, executable bit and object on both sides, so any change to the files (a hidden one cannot be in a visible PR) dismisses approvals and a rebase over unrelated changes keeps them. The author is refused and never counted (by person, so every device); eligibility is re-read from the database at each answer (admin, groups, person bindings); write access to every path of every revision is required; `people_only` is forced for high risk. `.veilrules` is read from the default branch's real tip; only admins can write a root file or force or delete the default branch (`sync.rs:1198`, `:1384`); a broken file only adds requirements beyond the defaults; its warnings reach admins only.
* **Bounds.** Stacks (100 changes), paths (10,000), anchors (1,000 lines of text ≤ 1 MiB), titles and bodies are checked; thread and comment counts are checked under the PR's row lock.

**Not filed (nits; all three fixed in S21 cycle 1: one refusal of a stack for anyone but an admin, `prs::not_a_pr`; a request for changes holds until that reviewer approves or no longer may write the files; a broken `.veilrules` keeps the last valid rules, `revision::rules_at`):**
* `revision::compute`'s refusals come before `readable_by`, so opening a PR from a stack that holds a hidden merge names that change's short id, and a hidden part of more than 100 changes or 10,000 paths gets that refusal instead of "files you cannot see". Needs an admin's merge on a branch the caller builds on.
* A request for changes stops holding the PR at the next revision (it is on an old patch), although §13.24 says it "holds the PR until they approve". Either is defensible; the doc and the code should agree.
* `rules.rs`'s "a file that does not parse never weakens review" is true against the defaults only: a broken file turns an admin's `normal = { approvals = 3 }` into one approval (admins' own file).

**Out of scope (trusted):** an admin may push a revision of someone's PR and approve it themselves (admins may also force `main`, threat 19); `vl pr review` signs the patch hash the server shows without recomputing it (the server is trusted for code).

**Held up, as tested or traced:**
* **Classes (BUG-1250).** `s21_cycle2::class_writes_hold_under_scripted_interleavings` pauses a reclassification between its reads and its writes (it holds the first PR's row) and runs scripted interleavings meanwhile: a new revision under the old lines; the lines going back, a revision, the new lines again; both again with a revision touching a path only the new line decides (`pub/zz/`, `security`); the lines going back alone. The end state is checked under the lines the script ended with first, then the others: lists, counts and `show` for a dev equal the oracle from the files, and every class under the current lines is its PR's paths' class. With the `revision` guard removed (`AND $6 = $6`), scripts 0 to 3 each fail on PostgreSQL and the whole test fails on YugabyteDB; with it, it passes on both, and 8 copies at once pass on PostgreSQL. (Checking the old lines first, as `class_writes_race_revisions_and_access_lines` does, recomputes every class and hides a wrong one: why that test passes without the guard.) Traced: a revision's paths and its `revision` commit in one transaction, read in two statements after the stale rows, so a guard that holds means the paths read are that revision's; paths only grow, so ABA on the key is harmless; `create` and `add_revision` take key and lines from one policy.
* **Per-viewer answers.** "That is revision N already" uses the caller's numbers; the 100-revision limit names no count; stack refusals to non-admins are the one `forbidden`; outdated marks and the carry budget depend only on files every viewer of the PR may read (a rebase over hidden changes keeps every object, so nothing is diffed); thread cursors and paging boundaries count visible comments only; a stale row is no PR for everyone alike.
* **Bounds.** Carrying checks the deadline between files, each diff is bounded (BUG-484), and 1,000 threads on one file read it once. Paging bounds every answer.
* **Approvals.** A request for changes holds across new revisions and rebases (any revision), and across a reviewer's access removed and restored (it holds again once restored; landing is S17's, so nothing lands in between today).

**Out of scope (trusted):** an admin's broken `.veilrules` is the admins' own file (the finding is that review drops later without anyone acting, not the edit). **Product decision 12 (unchanged):** tests are low risk; tests run on CI machines with whatever secrets CI holds, so a change to a real test can do what BUG-1257's cases do.
